title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
在
令甲諸鄉國三歲論士則錄其
人文之入彀者籍
奏之
上紀萬曆之七年巡按山西監察
御史黃〔應坤〕在事夙夜懍懍
務操精白爲百執事先提調
則屬左布政使張〔士佩〕右布
政使呂〔鳴珂〕監試則屬按察
===
使秦〔吉士〕副使王〔基〕會先御
史賈〔如式〕遣聘諸文學自四
方至則以教諭趙〔日新〕王〔銳〕
主考試教諭朱〔綸〕莊〔文龍〕李
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序
在令甲，諸鄉國三歲論士，則錄其人文之入彀者，籍奏之。上紀萬曆之七年，巡按山西監察御史黃〔應坤〕在事，夙夜懍懍，務操精白，爲百執事先。提調則屬左布政使張〔士佩〕、右布政使呂〔鳴珂〕；監試則屬按察使秦〔吉士〕、副使王〔基〕。會先御史賈〔如式〕遣聘諸文學自四方至，則以教諭趙〔日新〕、王〔銳〕主考試，教諭朱〔綸〕、莊〔文龍〕、李
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

According to the statutory regulations, when the various provinces evaluate scholars every three years, they record the names and essays of those who meet the standard and compile them into a register to be memorialized to the throne. In the seventh year of His Majesty's Wanli reign (1579), Regional Inspector of Shanxi and Investigating Censor Huang [Yingkun 黃應坤] was in charge of the affair. Day and night he maintained a reverent awe, striving to uphold pure integrity as an example for all the officiating functionaries. The duties of Proctor were assigned to Left Administration Commissioner Zhang [Shipei 張士佩] and Right Administration Commissioner Lü [Mingke 呂鳴珂]; the duties of Surveillance of the Examination were assigned to Surveillance Commissioner Qin [Jishi 秦吉士] and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang [Ji 王基]. Just then, the learned scholars whom the former Censor Jia [Rushi 賈如式] had dispatched envoys to invite arrived from all quarters. Thus, District Directors of Studies Zhao [Rixin 趙日新] and Wang [Rui 王銳] were appointed as Chief Examiners, while District Directors of Studies Zhu [Lun 朱綸], Zhuang [Wenlong 莊文龍], Li…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
〔希稷〕謝〔時泰〕侯〔賓家〕李〔中立〕
同考試闈以内外陳力蕆事
惟其人乃合巡按宣大御史
郭〔汝〕提學副使賀〔邦泰〕選士
二千二百有奇三試之得儁
六十五人文二十首將籍以
獻〔日新〕自惟豎儒駑下猥辱任
===
使竊附於以人事
君以故不避不馴首宣言以諗多
士頃自
皇上初受曆數有司首舉賓興
觀人文而化成蓋於兹三舉矣
比年
布功令廣厲視學諸臣直將洗
punctuated: 〔希稷〕、謝〔時泰〕、侯〔賓家〕、李〔中立〕同考試。闈以内外陳力蕆事，惟其人。乃合巡按宣大御史郭〔汝〕、提學副使賀〔邦泰〕選士二千二百有奇，三試之，得儁六十五人、文二十首，將籍以獻。〔日新〕自惟豎儒駑下，猥辱任使，竊附於以人事君，以故不避不馴，首宣言以諗多士：頃自皇上初受曆數，有司首舉賓興，觀人文而化成，蓋於兹三舉矣。比年布功令，廣厲視學諸臣，直將洗
translation_en:
… [Li] Xiji 李希稷, Xie Shitai 謝時泰, Hou Binjia 侯賓家, and Li Zhongli 李中立 to serve as Associate Examiners. Inside and outside the examination compound, those who exerted their strength to bring the affair to completion were all the right men for their posts. Together with the Regional Inspector of Xuanfu and Datong, Censor Guo Ru 郭汝, and the Education Intendant Assistant Surveillance Commissioner He Bangtai 賀邦泰, they gathered more than two thousand two hundred selected scholars. Having tested them in three sessions, they obtained sixty-five eminent graduates and twenty model compositions, which are now being registered for presentation to the throne.

I, [Zhao] Rixin 趙日新, reflect that I am but a petty, dull-witted scholar who has been undeservedly honored with this commission. Humbly aspiring to the principle of serving the ruler by recommending worthy men, I do not shrink from my own inelegance of expression in speaking first at the head of this record to counsel the many scholars:

Recently, since His Majesty first received theheavenly mandate of the calendar, the authorities first held the triennial examination to select worthy guests, observing cultural patterns in order to bring about moral transformation; counting to the present, it has now been held three times. In recent years, the court has promulgated academic regulations, broadly rousing the officials who inspect the schools, intending nothing less than to wash away…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
舊染而一新之中令不啻三
五其首舉也士若在蟄而昭
蘇趯趯思奮再舉則毛羽既
具躍然而知嚮方乃今三舉
若起溟渤挾扶搖蓬蓬然天
飛矣夫樹人如樹穀其必因
地利乘天時雖有汙萊不廢
===
穮蔉中歲而穰三歲而登三
歲而升而平又三歲而太平
矣山西古冀州地堯舜禹之
所更都當堯之時封可比屋
三聖相授野無遺賢其分職
爲四岳爲十二牧爲九官其
類族爲十六相其亮天工也
punctuated:
舊染而一新之，申令不啻三五。其首舉也，士若在蟄而昭蘇，趯趯思奮；再舉，則毛羽既具，躍然而知嚮方；乃今三舉，若起溟渤，挾扶搖，蓬蓬然天飛矣。夫樹人如樹穀，其必因地利、乘天時，雖有汙萊，不廢穮蔉，中歲而穰，三歲而登，三歲而升而平，又三歲而太平矣。

山西，古冀州地，堯、舜、禹之所更都。當堯之時，封可比屋；三聖相授，野無遺賢。其分職爲四岳、爲十二牧、爲九官，其類族爲十六相，其亮天工也…
translation_en:
…away old taints and renew them completely, reiterating the decrees not merely three or five times. At the first holding of the examinations, the scholars were like hibernating creatures awakening to life, leaping up and eager to rouse themselves. At the second holding, their plumage was already full-grown, and they sprang forth knowing which direction to take. Now, at this third holding, it is as though they are rising from the vast ocean, riding a whirlwind, and soaring vigorously into the heavens! Now, cultivating men is like cultivating grain: one must rely on the advantages of the soil and seize the seasons of Heaven. Even where there are low-lying and weed-choked fields, if one does not neglect weeding and hoeing, in an average year there will be an abundant harvest, in three years the grain will be gathered in, in another three years it will advance to a state of sufficiency and peace, and in yet another three years there will be Great Peace.

Shanxi is the land of ancient Jizhou, where Yao, Shun, and Yu successively established their capitals. In the time of Yao, every household was worthy of enfeoffment; as the three sages handed down the throne to one another, no worthy men were left neglected in the wilderness. In the division of offices, they served as the Four Peaks, the Twelve Pastors, and the Nine Officials; grouped by their clans, they were the Sixteen Assistants; in aiding the work of Heaven…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
爲二十有二人其褎然而首
百官則得五臣而天下治矣
其後千有餘歲唐叔始以晉
封歷世阜昌文公始伯帥諸
侯以獎王室世主齊盟乃若
股肱之良則九宗五正咸在
始於狐偃趙衰迄於叔向寔
===
蕃有材邇主庇民視一臣爲
尤烈後儒闇於大較直將以
陪隷畢視之善謀國者將爲
異代求材慨九原不可復作
幸而借一國將有瘳如使賫
適逢時得聞孔子之道其所
就業不亦磬乎大哉要以表
punctuated: 爲二十有二人。其褎然而首百官，則得五臣而天下治矣。其後千有餘歲，唐叔始以晉封，歷世阜昌，文公始伯，帥諸侯以獎王室，世主齊盟。乃若股肱之良，則九宗五正咸在，始於狐偃、趙衰，迄於叔向，寔蕃有材。邇主庇民，視一臣爲尤烈。後儒闇於大較，直將以陪隷畢視之。善謀國者，將爲異代求材，慨九原不可復作，幸而借一，國將有瘳。如使賫適逢時，得聞孔子之道，其所就業，不亦磬乎大哉！要以表
translation_en: … numbered twenty-two men. And as for those who stood preeminent at the head of all officials, there were five ministers, and the realm was well-governed. More than a thousand years later, Tang Shu 唐叔 was first enfeoffed with Jin 晉. Through successive generations it grew prosperous and flourishing, until Duke Wen 文公 first became Hegemon, leading the feudal lords to support the royal house and presiding over the covenants of alliance for generations. As for the excellence of its chief ministers, the Nine Lineages and Five Officials were all present. Beginning with Hu Yan 狐偃 and Zhao Cui 趙衰 and extending down to Shuxiang 叔向, it truly abounded in men of talent. In standing close to their rulers and sheltering the people, they were even more illustrious than that single minister [Guan Zhong]. Later Confucians, blind to the broader picture, would simply lump them all together as mere rear-vassals and underlings. Yet those skilled in planning for a state, when seeking talent from other ages, sigh that the men buried in the Nine Springs cannot be raised again; if by good fortune even one could be borrowed, the state would be cured of its ills. Had they been endowed with the good fortune to meet the right time and hear the Way of Confucius 孔子, would their achievements not have been vast and great [?]? In sum, flanked within and without…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
裹山河林林然皆晉產也上
之帝則帝臣王則王佐下之
而伯不失世卿其斯爲九州
之上腴其賦上上則自昔然
矣其後千有餘歲觀
明德而服西戎都人士應感而
興無異唐虞之際薛文清以
躬行著巋然不繼列祀瞽宗
於當世無兩邇者起家仕國
往往具文武材宰執師保之
===
臣踵相接也
主上方作人以待舉至於再至於
三經沃土而授上農庶幾得
邁種者其人爲秋之實矣顧
punctuated: 裹山河，林林然皆晉產也。上之，帝則帝臣，王則王佐；下之，而伯不失世卿。其斯爲九州之上腴，其賦上上，則自昔然矣。其後千有餘歲，觀明德而服西戎，都人士應感而興，無異唐、虞之際。薛文清以躬行著，巋然不繼，列祀瞽宗，於當世無兩。邇者起家仕國，往往具文武材，宰執師保之臣，踵相接也。主上方作人以待舉，至於再，至於三。經沃土而授上農，庶幾得邁種者其人，爲秋之實矣。顧
translation_en:
…girdled by mountains and rivers, teeming in multitudes, all are natives of Jin. At the highest level, under an emperor they were imperial ministers, and under a true king they were kingly aides; at a lower level, under a hegemon they did not fail to be hereditary senior officials. That this land is the richest soil of the Nine Provinces, and its revenue ranked top of the top, has been so since antiquity. More than a thousand years later, beholding the illustrious virtue of the Ming and the pacification of the western Rong, the gentlemen of this region responded to the inspiration and rose up, no differently than in the era of Yao and Shun. Xue Wenqing (Xue Xuan 薛瑄) became renowned for his personal practice of the Way; standing lofty and peerless, he was enshrined in the Confucian temple (Guzong), unmatched in the present age. In recent times, those who have risen from their families to serve the state have time and again possessed both civil and military talents, and chief councilors and Grand Tutors and Protectors have followed closely upon one another's heels.

His Majesty is just now cultivating men of talent to await their selection, doing so a second time and even a third time. When one parcels out fertile soil and entrusts it to superior farmers, one may hope to obtain men who vigorously sow virtue to serve as the autumn harvest. Yet…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
賓興之典昉於成周由前則
揖讓而未遑由後則師武臣
力而不急於時士烝烝嚮用
無虞鄉舉而里選之自漢設
科周制未改乃若漢霍宣成
唐狄梁國裴晉國宋司馬溫
國文潞國之數臣者率皆有
===
待而興然或曠千里而一鳴
或曠百世而一覯方諸疇昔
宜若徑庭
今制特詳於周官而多士咸誦
法乎孔子槩其所舉視三代
之英何讓焉藉令染者不鑿
而美稗先登詩矣以此而讓
punctuated: 賓興之典，昉於成周。由前，則揖讓而未遑；由後，則師武臣力而不急。於時士烝烝嚮用，無虞鄉舉而里選之。自漢設科，周制未改。乃若漢霍宣成，唐狄梁國、裴晉國，宋司馬溫國、文潞國，之數臣者，率皆有待而興。然或曠千里而一鳴，或曠百世而一覯，方諸疇昔，宜若徑庭。今制特詳於《周官》，而多士咸誦法乎孔子，槩其所舉，視三代之英何讓焉？藉令染者不鑿，而美稗先登，詩矣！以此而讓
translation_en: … the institution of presenting worthies as guests at court (binxing) began in the flourishing Zhou dynasty. Prior to that, rulers yielded the throne with bowed hands and had no leisure for it; subsequent to that, rulers relied on the martial prowess of their generals and the strength of their ministers and felt no urgency for it. At that time, scholars flourished in great numbers and aspired to be employed, so there was no worry in recommending them from the districts and selecting them from the villages. Since the Han dynasty established examination categories, the Zhou system was not wholly altered. Consider such figures as Huo Guang 霍光 (Marquis Xuancheng 宣成侯) of the Han, Di Renjie 狄仁傑 (Duke of Liang 梁國公) and Pei Du 裴度 (Duke of Jin 晉國公) of the Tang, and Sima Guang 司馬光 (Duke of Wen 溫國公) and Wen Yanbo 文彥博 (Duke of Lu 潞國公) of the Song—these several ministers all generally awaited their moment to rise. Yet sometimes a thousand miles would pass before a single one cried out, or a hundred generations would elapse before a single one was met; compared with remote antiquity, this naturally seems worlds apart. The present institution is even more detailed than the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), and the multitude of scholars all recite and model themselves upon Confucius; judging by the general standard of those recommended, how do they yield anything to the finest talents of the Three Dynasties? Suppose, however, that what is dyed is not polished [?], and fine tares are harvested first—that would be perverse [reading 詩 as 悖]! If on this account one were to reproach …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
舉者將安所追溥責哉及縱
觀多士所爲文斐然較著莫
不竭心思而中典要窮經術
而達時宜卽其緒餘亦皆援
古而準今尊王而賤伯此故
都之流風遺俗誦法之成效
而
===
振德之明徵也幸而得士若此舉
者庶無罪悔矣乎旣卒業而
深惟中心之縣未解也古者
以鄉三物爲敎則德爲上行
爲先借曰藝成於斯爲下及
其以鄉射而賓多士規規乎
程一藝而衡石之射義有言
punctuated: 舉者，將安所追溥責哉？及縱觀多士所爲文，斐然較著，莫不竭心思而中典要，窮經術而達時宜；卽其緒餘，亦皆援古而準今，尊王而賤伯。此故都之流風遺俗、誦法之成效，而振德之明徵也。幸而得士若此，舉者庶無罪悔矣乎？旣卒業，而深惟中心之縣未解也。古者以鄉三物爲敎，則德爲上，行爲先，借曰「藝成」，於斯爲下。及其以鄉射而賓多士，規規乎程一藝而衡石之。《射義》有言：
translation_en: … those who recommend them, how could we escape widespread blame? Yet when we survey at length the essays composed by the many scholars, they are brilliantly manifest: none fail to exhaust their mental powers and hit the canonical essentials, or thoroughly master classicist learning and grasp what is appropriate to the times; even in their secondary points, they all cite antiquity to set the standard for the present, revering the True King and disparaging the Hegemon. These are the lingering customs and bequeathed mores of the ancient capitals, the achieved results of reciting and modeling oneself upon Confucius, and the clear evidence of rousing and cultivating virtue. Being fortunate enough to obtain scholars like these, may those who recommend them perhaps be free of fault and regret? Yet after finishing reading their work and reflecting deeply, the suspense in my heart is still not relieved. In antiquity, when the Three Things of the Districts (xiang sanwu) were used for instruction, virtues were placed highest and conduct was put first; even when it was called "accomplishment in the arts," that ranked lowest here. Yet when it came to treating the many scholars as guests through the District Archery Ritual (xiangshe), they fastidiously measured a single art and weighed it as if by balance and stone. The Meaning of the Archery Ritual (Sheyi) has a saying: …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
此可以觀德行彼其逢萌鴻
超丗蠅飛衛紀昌之屬其德
行寧有足多者邪何以得當
君子觀也今多士不以射角
而以言揚射之中侯宜莫如
言之中窾也君子言必顧行
故有德者必有言用是而觀
===
其於德行爲近第帝堯在位
比屋可封而靜言庸違四岳
咸薦聽其言而信其行所不
爲蕙稗也者幾希抑或懲其
不然惟其言而莫之信則皐
陶賛賛賛厥有昌言雖有百揆
聞言則拜有嘉於是乎罔攸
punctuated: 「此可以觀德行。」彼其逢萌鴻超、丗蠅飛衛、紀昌之屬，其德行寧有足多者邪？何以得當君子觀也？今多士不以射角，而以言揚。射之中侯，宜莫如言之中窾也。君子言必顧行，故有德者必有言。用是而觀，其於德行爲近。第帝堯在位，比屋可封，而靜言庸違，四岳咸薦。聽其言而信其行，所不爲蕙稗也者幾希。抑或懲其不然，惟其言而莫之信，則皐陶賛賛，厥有昌言；雖有百揆，聞言則拜；有嘉於是乎罔攸…
translation_en: … "By this one may observe virtuous conduct." Yet as for those of the ilk of Peng Meng [reading 逢蒙] who shot wild geese high in the sky, or Fei Wei and Ji Chang who treated lice as large as flies, did their virtuous conduct really have anything worthy of high praise? How could they be fit to serve as examples for a gentleman's observation of virtue? Today, the many scholars do not compete in archery, but are promoted through their words. Hitting the target in archery surely cannot compare to hitting the mark in speech. A gentleman's words must take into account his actions, and therefore one who possesses virtue will certainly possess notable words. Viewed in this way, speech comes closer to revealing virtuous conduct. However, when Emperor Yao was on the throne and every household was worthy of enfeoffment, there was still one who spoke artfully when quiet yet acted perversely when employed, whom the Four Peaks all recommended. If one listens to people's words and trusts their conduct, it is rare indeed not to mistake barnyard grass for fragrant orchids. Or if, taking warning from such failures, one simply refuses to trust any words at all—then think of Gaoyao assisting and counseling, offering his splendid words; even the General Regulator [Shun], upon hearing virtuous words, would bow; and because fine men were accepted, no worthy remained…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
伏奚言之不可已也如是無
寧以一廢百乎哉昔者晉獻
嘉禾史書諸策惟是爲王者
之瑞而大鹵之金垂棘之璧
汾之鼎不與焉晉之乘可攷
已爾多士以昌言進則爲嘉
禾由此而爲馨香有司庶可
藉手否則違言而爲莠稗豈
===
惟爾多士之羞其在詩曰先
民是程多士勉矣是役也總
督軍務兵部左侍郎吳〔兌〕鄭
洛巡撫右僉都御史高〔文薦〕
巡撫大同右僉都御史賈〔應〕
元
燿武脩文化興髦士巡鹽
punctuated: 伏，奚言之不可已也如是！無寧以一廢百乎哉？昔者晉獻嘉禾，史書諸策，惟是爲王者之瑞，而大鹵之金、垂棘之璧、汾之鼎不與焉，晉之乘可攷已。爾多士以昌言進，則爲嘉禾，由此而爲馨香，有司庶可藉手；否則違言而爲莠稗，豈惟爾多士之羞？其在《詩》曰：「先民是程。」多士勉矣！是役也，總督軍務兵部左侍郎吳〔兌〕、鄭洛，巡撫右僉都御史高〔文薦〕，巡撫大同右僉都御史賈〔應〕元，燿武脩文，化興髦士；巡鹽
translation_en: …remain hidden; how could it be that words are this indispensable! Would one rather discard a hundred things on account of a single flaw? In antiquity, when the state of Jin presented auspicious grain, the scribes recorded it on bamboo slips, for only this was deemed the auspicious portent of a true king, whereas the metal of Dalu, the jade disk of Chuiji, and the tripods of the Fen River were not counted among them—this can be verified in the historical annals of Jin. If you many scholars advance through flourishing words, you will be that auspicious grain, and from this become a fragrant offering, so that the authorities may have something to present on your behalf. Otherwise, if you speak perversely and become weeds and tares, would that be a disgrace to you many scholars alone? As it is said in the Book of Odes (Shi): "Take the ancients as your model." May you many scholars exert yourselves! In this undertaking, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs and Left Vice Minister of War Wu Dui 吳兌 and Zheng Luo 鄭洛, Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Gao Wenjian 高文薦, and Grand Coordinator of Datong and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief Jia Yingyuan 賈應元 displayed martial prowess and cultivated civil virtue, their transforming influence inspiring eminent scholars; Salt-Control…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰予欲無言子貢曰子如不言則小子
何述焉子曰天何言哉四時行焉百物
生焉天何言哉
好學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎勇知
斯三者則知所以脩身知所以脩身則
知所以治人知所以治人則知所以治
天下國家矣
乃若其情則可以爲善矣乃所謂善也若
夫爲不善非才之罪也
===
易
象曰地中有水師君子以容民畜衆
改邑不改井乃以剛中也
神而明之存乎其人
聖人之大寶曰位何以守位曰仁何以聚
人曰財理財正辭禁民爲非曰義
書
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「予欲無言。」子貢曰：「子如不言，則小子何述焉？」子曰：「天何言哉？四時行焉，百物生焉，天何言哉？」

好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。知斯三者，則知所以脩身；知所以脩身，則知所以治人；知所以治人，則知所以治天下國家矣。

乃若其情，則可以爲善矣，乃所謂善也。若夫爲不善，非才之罪也。

易

象曰：地中有水，師，君子以容民畜衆。

改邑不改井，乃以剛中也。

神而明之，存乎其人。

聖人之大寶曰位，何以守位曰仁，何以聚人曰財，理財正辭、禁民爲非曰義。

書
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said, "I wish to do without speaking." Zigong 子貢 said, "If you do not speak, Master, then what shall we, your disciples, have to transmit?" The Master said, "Does Heaven speak? The four seasons pursue their courses, and the hundred things are brought forth. Does Heaven speak?"

To be fond of learning is near to wisdom; to practice with vigor is near to benevolence; to know shame is near to courage. He who knows these three things knows how to cultivate his person; knowing how to cultivate his person, he knows how to govern other men; knowing how to govern other men, he knows how to govern the Empire, its states, and its families.

As for his genuine feelings, they are capable of becoming good; this is what I mean by calling human nature good. As for a man's becoming not good, that is not the fault of his natural endowment.

Book of Changes (Yi 易)

The Image says: In the middle of the earth there is water: the image of the Army (Shi 師). Thus the noble man generously accommodates the people and nurtures the multitude.

"The town may be changed, but the well is not changed": this is because of the firm line in the center.

To carry this out with spirit-like efficacy and make it manifest depends on the right person.

The great treasure of the sage is called position. How to guard position is called benevolence. How to gather men is called wealth. Regulating wealth, rectifying speech, and prohibiting the people from doing wrong is called righteousness.

Book of Documents (Shu 書)

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
帝曰咨汝二十有二人欽哉惟時亮天功
三載考績三考黜陟幽明庶績咸熙
厥賦惟上上錯厥田惟中中
嚴恭寅畏天命自度
功崇惟志業廣惟勤惟克果斷乃罔後艱
詩
琴瑟在御莫不靜好
或降于阿或飲于池或寢或訛爾牧來思
何蓑何笠或負其餱三十維物爾牲則具
===
之綱之紀燕及朋友百辟卿士媚于天子
不解于位民之攸塈
日就月將學有緝熙于光明佛時仔肩示
我顯德行
春秋
丙戌公會鄭伯盟于武父〔桓公十有二年〕
夏齊侯衛侯胥命于蒲〔桓公三年〕楚屈完
來盟于師盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕
punctuated:
「帝曰：『咨！汝二十有二人，欽哉！惟時亮天功。』三載考績，三考，黜陟幽明，庶績咸熙。」
「厥賦惟上上錯，厥田惟中中。」
「嚴恭寅畏，天命自度。」
「功崇惟志，業廣惟勤，惟克果斷，乃罔後艱。」
《詩》：
「琴瑟在御，莫不靜好。」
「或降于阿，或飲于池，或寢或訛。爾牧來思，何蓑何笠，或負其餱。三十維物，爾牲則具。」
「之綱之紀，燕及朋友。百辟卿士，媚于天子，不解于位，民之攸塈。」
「日就月將，學有緝熙于光明。佛時仔肩，示我顯德行。」
《春秋》：
「丙戌，公會鄭伯，盟于武父。」〔桓公十有二年〕
「夏，齊侯、衛侯胥命于蒲。」〔桓公三年〕「楚屈完來盟于師，盟于召陵。」〔僖公四年〕
translation_en:
"The Emperor said: 'Ah, you twenty-two men! Be reverent, and thereby aid in the work of Heaven!' Every three years there was an examination of merits, and after three examinations the undeserving were degraded and the deserving promoted,whereby all accomplishments brightly flourished."
"Its revenue was of the highest class, the first grade, with admixtures; its fields were of the middle class, the middle grade."
"Grave, humble, reverently fearful, he measured himself by the Mandate of Heaven."
"Merit becomes lofty through resolution; enterprise becomes broad through diligence. Only when one is able to be decisive will there be no subsequent difficulties."

Classic of Poetry (Shijing):
"The zithers and lutes are in your hands; there is nothing not tranquil and good."
"Some descend from the hills, some drink at the pools; some lie down, some move about. Your herdsmen come, carrying raincoats and bamboo hats, or bearing their dry provisions on their backs. Counting by thirties according to their colors, your sacrificial victims are fully provided."
"Giving law and order to all, he brings peace to his friends. The hundred rulers and ministerial officers hold the Son of Heaven dear; never remiss in their positions, they are those through whom the people find rest."
"With daily progress and monthly advance, I will learn until there is continuous brightness toward illumination. Assist me in bearing this heavy burden on my shoulders, and show me the manifest conduct of virtue."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"On the bingxu day, the Duke met the Earl of Zheng and made a covenant at Wufu." [Twelfth year of Duke Huan]
"In summer, the Marquis of Qi and the Marquis of Wei exchanged pledges at Pu." [Third year of Duke Huan] "Qu Wan of Chu came to make a covenant with the army, and made a covenant at Shaoling." [Fourth year of Duke Xi]

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
公會晉侯宋公陳侯衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子
邾子滕子薛伯齊世子光吳人鄫人于
戚〔襄公五年〕
冬公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯莒子邾子滕
子薛伯杞伯小邾子齊世子光伐鄭十
有二月己亥同盟于戲〔襄公九年〕公會
晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾
子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭會于蕭
魚〔襄公十有一年〕夏公會齊侯于夾谷
公至自夾谷　齊人來歸鄆讙龜陰田
〔俱定公十年〕
===
禮記
爵人於朝與士共之
故天不愛其道地不愛其寶人不愛其情
論倫無患樂之情也欣喜歡愛樂之官也
中正無邪禮之質也莊敬恭順禮之制
也
仁者人也道者義也
punctuated:
公會晉侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、齊世子光、吳人、鄫人于戚。〔襄公五年〕
冬，公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊世子光伐鄭。十有二月己亥，同盟于戲。〔襄公九年〕公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。會于蕭魚。〔襄公十有一年〕夏，公會齊侯于夾谷。公至自夾谷。齊人來歸鄆、讙、龜陰田。〔俱定公十年〕

《禮記》
爵人於朝，與士共之。
故天不愛其道，地不愛其寶，人不愛其情。
論倫無患，樂之情也；欣喜歡愛，樂之官也。中正無邪，禮之質也；莊敬恭順，禮之制也。
仁者，人也；道者，義也。
translation_en:
The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the people of Wu, and the people of Zeng at Qi. [Fifth year of Duke Xiang]
In winter, the Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Heir Apparent Guang of Qi in attacking Zheng. In the twelfth month, on the jihai day, they jointly made a covenant at Xi. [Ninth year of Duke Xiang] The Duke joined the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu in attacking Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu. [Eleventh year of Duke Xiang] In summer, the Duke met the Marquis of Qi at Jiagu. The Duke arrived back from Jiagu. The people of Qi came to restore the lands of Yun, Huan, and Guiyin. [All from the tenth year of Duke Ding]

Record of Rites (Liji)
Conferring ranks upon men in the court is to share the decision with the officers.
Therefore Heaven does not begrudge its Way, Earth does not begrudge its treasures, and Man does not begrudge his feelings.
To discourse on human relationships without anxiety is the essential nature of music; joy, delight, and loving affection are the functions of music. Centrality and uprightness without perversity are the substance of ritual; solemnity, reverence, respect, and compliance are the regulations of ritual.
Benevolence is to be human; the Way is righteousness.

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
第貳場
論
明主游心帝王之術
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令二千石勉勸農桑詔〔建初元年〕
擬唐以李泌同平章事誥〔貞元三年〕
擬以禮部左侍郎兼翰林院學士薛瑄從
祀孔子廟庭子孫謝表〔隆慶六年〕
判語〔五條〕
===
隱匿費用稅糧課物
公差人員欺凌長官
文書應給驛而不給
原告人事畢不放回
有司官吏不住公廨
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問古帝王之學動息有養其勒於箕簴盤
盂戶楹矛劒者已燦然可睹矣乃猶不
punctuated:
第貳場
論
明主游心帝王之術

詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢令二千石勉勸農桑詔〔建初元年〕
擬唐以李泌同平章事誥〔貞元三年〕
擬以禮部左侍郎兼翰林院學士薛瑄從祀孔子廟庭子孫謝表〔隆慶六年〕

判語〔五條〕
隱匿費用稅糧課物
公差人員欺凌長官
文書應給驛而不給

有司官吏不住公廨

第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：古帝王之學，動息有養，其勒於箕簴、盤盂、戶楹、矛劒者，已燦然可睹矣。乃猶不
translation_en:
Second Session
Discourse
"An enlightened ruler lets his mind roam in the arts of Emperors and Kings."

Edicts, Mandates, and Memorials [One required among these]
Imitative Han edict ordering two-thousand-bushel officials to encourage and promote agriculture and sericulture [first year of the Jianchu era (76 CE)]
Imitative Tang mandate appointing Li Mi 李泌 as Jointly Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery [third year of the Zhenyuan era (787 CE)]
Imitative memorial of thanks from the descendants of Xue Xuan 薛瑄, Left Vice Minister of Rites concurrently Hanlin Academician, upon his enshrinement for sacrifice in the Temple of Confucius [sixth year of the Longqing era (1572)]

Legal Judgments [Five items]
Concealing and expending tax grain and levy goods
Personnel on official errands bullying and insulting superior officials
Failing to provide postal relay service for official documents that should be provided with it
Failing to release the plaintiff to return home after a case is concluded
Competent authorities—officials and subofficial functionaries—not residing in their official quarters

Third Session
Policy Questions [Five items]
Question: In the learning of the ancient Emperors and Kings, their self-cultivation continued whether in activity or at rest. That which was inscribed upon bell-stands, basins and bowls, doors and pillars, and spears and swords can already be seen in resplendent clarity. Yet they still did not…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
自滿假而作箴以致儆其義何居而其
制何昉歟載稽往牒夏商史甲之箴尚
矣他如訓民生以在勤納箴御而悔過
者亦能彷彿其遺意歟嗣是以來代各
有作有獻大寶箴而旌其直者有獻丹
扆箴而褒其忠者又有獻獄官箴於建
中獻勸講箴於慶曆而並蒙嘉納者果
皆益於規誡之實歟抑猶有遺憾歟恭
惟我
===
皇上天縱神明稽古典學頃於
便殿集圖書爲
燕息之所特取義周雅以
雝肅名之復
命輔臣作箴揭書
御屛時
賜省覽於皇哉
懿範英聲增光載籍蓋眞與古帝王心法同
符而近世所稱說方斯蔑矣諸士生際
punctuated: 自滿假，而作箴以致儆，其義何居，而其制何昉歟？載稽往牒，夏商史甲之箴尚矣；他如訓民生以在勤、納箴御而悔過者，亦能彷彿其遺意歟？嗣是以來，代各有作：有獻《大寶箴》而旌其直者，有獻《丹扆箴》而褒其忠者，又有獻《獄官箴》於建中、獻《勸講箴》於慶曆而並蒙嘉納者，果皆益於規誡之實歟，抑猶有遺憾歟？恭惟我皇上天縱神明，稽古典學，頃於便殿集圖書爲燕息之所，特取義周《雅》，以「雝肅」名之，復命輔臣作箴，揭書御屛，時賜省覽。於皇哉！懿範英聲，增光載籍，蓋眞與古帝王心法同符，而近世所稱說方斯蔑矣。諸士生際
translation_en: …complacent, and composed admonitions (zhen 箴) to instill vigilance—what is the meaning behind this, and when did this practice originate? Examining past records, the admonitions of the scribes and of Tai Jia 太甲 [?] in the Xia and Shang dynasties are of the highest antiquity; as for others, such as instructing that the people's livelihood depends on diligence, or accepting admonitions from attendants and repenting of faults, were they also able to approximate that legacy? Thereafter, each era produced its own works: there was one who presented the Admonition on the Great Treasure (Dabao zhen 大寶箴) and was honored for his uprightness; one who presented the Admonition for the Cinnabar Screen (Danyi zhen 丹扆箴) and was praised for his loyalty; and others who presented the Admonition for Prison Officials (Yuguan zhen 獄官箴) during the Jianzhong reign (780–783) and the Admonition Encouraging Imperial Lectures (Quanjiang zhen 勸講箴) during the Qingli reign (1041–1048), both receiving gracious acceptance. Were all of these truly beneficial to the substance of remonstrance and warning, or did they still leave room for regret? Reverently considering our Emperor: heaven-endowed with divine intelligence, he examines antiquity and devotes himself to learning. Recently, in a side palace, he gathered books and charts to make a place for leisure and rest, specially drawing meaning from the Odes (Ya 雅) of Zhou to name it "Harmonious Reverence" (Yongsu 雝肅). He further commanded the Grand Secretaries to compose admonitions, posting them written upon the imperial screen and frequently bestowing his inspection upon them. How glorious! His admirable model and illustrious reputation add luster to the historical records; truly, he tallies with the method of the mind (xinfa 心法) of the ancient emperors and kings, and what has been praised in recent ages is nothing compared to this. You scholars, born in an era of…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
昌熙聞風感奮得無有願攄誠竭悃期裨
聖學於萬一者乎夫臣子效忠靡間踈逖堯舜
時雖稷契敷謨皐夔納誨乃芻蕘邇言
弗弃也其悉意陳之毋但諉曰箴之說
具備矣
問教化國家之先務廉恥士人之美節昔
譚尚之矣在昔成周盛時學校有教選
舉有制考課有章所爲陶淑士類共惇
行誼者法綦備矣厥科條成效具在方
策可得而指言與抑有不盡於法者與
===
秦漢而降教化寖微廉恥道喪即有稱
傑才者憑技用力亦能策勳爍譽播人
耳目然考衷度中其節果足稱與
明興法周爲治首崇教化凡所爲廣厲學官討
偕有司與夫三年大察之典品式周備
率有原本以故士人薰濡其間者爭淬
勵濯磨以嘗
上意迹其所樹茂德芳猷庬炳後先者曾不興
punctuated:
昌熙，聞風感奮，得無有願攄誠竭悃，期裨聖學於萬一者乎？夫臣子效忠，靡間踈逖。堯、舜時，雖稷、契敷謨，皐、夔納誨，乃芻蕘邇言弗弃也。其悉意陳之，毋但諉曰箴之說具備矣。

問：教化，國家之先務；廉恥，士人之美節，昔譚尚之矣。在昔成周盛時，學校有教，選舉有制，考課有章，所爲陶淑士類、共惇行誼者，法綦備矣。厥科條成效，具在方策，可得而指言與？抑有不盡於法者與？秦、漢而降，教化寖微，廉恥道喪。即有稱傑才者，憑技用力，亦能策勳爍譽，播人耳目，然考衷度中，其節果足稱與？明興，法周爲治，首崇教化。凡所爲廣厲學官、討偕有司，與夫三年大察之典，品式周備，率有原本。以故士人薰濡其間者，爭淬勵濯磨以嘗上意。迹其所樹，茂德芳猷，庬炳後先者，曾不興
translation_en:
… a flourishing and prosperous era, and upon hearing of this moral influence are moved and inspired—could there not be among you those who wish to pour forth your utmost sincerity and devotion, hoping to contribute one ten-thousandth to His Majesty's sagely learning? Indeed, when subjects and sons offer their loyalty, there is no distinction between the distant and the humble. In the time of Yao and Shun, although Hou Ji and Xie set forth counsels and Gao Yao and Kui presented admonitions, even the humble words of grass- and firewood-gatherers were not discarded. Set forth your thoughts in full, and do not merely excuse yourselves by saying that the doctrines of the admonitions are already complete.

Question: Moral transformation through education is the foremost duty of the state, and a sense of integrity and shame is the admirable virtue of the literati; discourses of the past have long esteemed them. In antiquity, during the flourishing era of the Zhou dynasty, schools had their teachings, selection and recommendation had their systems, and official evaluations had their regulations. The methods for molding and cultivating the literati so that all would earnestly uphold righteous conduct were utterly complete. Their detailed provisions and achievements are all recorded in the classics and historical documents—can you point to them and discuss them? Or was there something that went beyond mere laws and regulations? From the Qin and Han dynasties onward, moral transformation gradually declined and the way of integrity and shame was lost. Even when there were men acclaimed as outstanding talents who, relying on skill and exertion, were able toinscribe meritorious deeds and win shining renown that spread to people's ears and eyes, if we examine their inner motives and measure their hearts, was their moral integrity truly worthy of praise? When the Ming arose, it modeled its governance on the Zhou, placing first the veneration of moral transformation through education. All its measures for broadly encouraging the schools, instructing and uniting the authorities [? 討偕有司], and conducting the triennial Great Evaluation are comprehensive in their standards and forms, and all derive from fundamental principles. Consequently, literati who were steeped in this environment vied to temper and polish themselves in order to meet [? 嘗] His Majesty's intentions. Tracing what they established—their flourishing virtue and fragrant counsels shining richly one after another—did they not rival [? 曾不興] …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
鎬京辟廱之盛若錄在理學名臣者可
考而知也爰及今日士學之本原文止
藻績言務矜詡行闕真實甚則陽章逢
而陰駔儈獵經生之名而躬穿窬之行
方且目廉恥爲曲謹焉茲果教化之不
足恃與抑武文具實徵不足以風士與
夫挽風會之流以追蹤古昔當事責也
不洞於俗觵然物表者士人責也諸生
夙負豪傑諒有驗於中矣試言之以卜
===
出處事業
問三晉河山之勝寓內稱雄焉地靈人傑
所從來遠矣后稷以粒民率育龍逢以
直諫顯名傳說以同心匡辟斯固丘匱
十亂之儔已三代以還節士才卿接迹
而起無暇劇論姑掇其最著者與諸士
評之有矢志受遺竭力股肱者有從龍
定國屏迹綿山者有身任立孤下報十
年之後若均之一死而孰輕於鴻毛有
punctuated:
鎬京辟廱之盛，若錄在理學、名臣者，可考而知也。爰及今日，士學之本原，文止藻績，言務矜詡，行闕真實；甚則陽章逢而陰駔儈，獵經生之名而躬穿窬之行，方且目廉恥爲曲謹焉。茲果教化之不足恃與？抑武文具實徵，不足以風士與？夫挽風會之流以追蹤古昔，當事責也；不洞於俗，觵然物表者，士人責也。諸生夙負豪傑，諒有驗於中矣。試言之，以卜出處事業。

問：三晉河山之勝，寓內稱雄焉。地靈人傑，所從來遠矣。后稷以粒民率育，龍逢以直諫顯名，傳說以同心匡辟，斯固丘匱、十亂之儔已。三代以還，節士才卿接迹而起，無暇劇論，姑掇其最著者與諸士評之：有矢志受遺、竭力股肱者，有從龍定國、屏迹綿山者，有身任立孤、下報十年之後若，均之一死，而孰輕於鴻毛？有
translation_en:
…the flourishing of the Biyong royal academy in the capital of Hao; as for those recorded among the masters of Neo-Confucianism (lixue) and eminent ministers, they can be examined and known. Coming down to the present day, as for the fundamental source of scholars' learning [or: scholars ignore the fundamental source of learning], their writing stops at ornate embellishment, their words strive for boastfulness, and their conduct lacks authenticity. In extreme cases, they wear the robes of scholars on the outside while secretly acting as market brokers on the inside, hunting for the reputation of classical scholars while personally engaging in the conduct of burglars who bore through walls, all the while regarding integrity and a sense of shame as petty scrupulousness. Is this truly because moral transformation through education cannot be relied upon? Or is it that [we] merely follow empty formalities without substantial verification [?], which is insufficient to inspire the scholars? Now, to turn back the tide of prevailing customs so as to follow in the footsteps of antiquity is the responsibility of those in authority; not to be swept along by vulgar customs, but to stand resolute and upright above the material world, is the responsibility of scholars. You students have long aspired to be outstanding heroes, and surely have verified this within yourselves. Try to set it forth in words, so that we may divine your future conduct in taking or leaving office and your achievements.

Question: The grandeur of the rivers and mountains of the Three Jin region [Shanxi] is renowned as preeminent within the realm. That its numinous terrain produces outstanding heroes has been so since remote antiquity. Hou Ji nourished all the people by providing them with grain, Guan Longfeng won fame through forthright remonstrance, and Fu Yue assisted his sovereign with a united heart—these were truly the peers of the Five Ministers [?] and the Ten Worthies. From the Three Dynasties onward, men of integrity and talented ministers arose one after another in close succession. There is no leisure to discuss them all exhaustively, so let us provisionally gather the most prominent among them and evaluate them with you gentlemen: There was one who swore an oath upon receiving a testamentary charge and exhausted his strength as a trusted aide [Xun Xi]; there was one who followed his lord to establish the state and then withdrew from the world to Mount Mian [Jie Zitui]; and there was one who personally took on the responsibility of establishing the orphan and went below to report in the afterlife more than ten years later [Cheng Ying]. They all shared equally in dying, yet whose death was lighter than a swan's feather? There was…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
抗俗遺榮叟却秦兵者有見幾篤行無
愧蔡碑者有上策著書託迹河汾之澌
者均之一隱而孰裨於世用或圖功麟
閣或取日虞淵輿入相中國走卒知名
者事功同也而行不無純駁或才稱命
世或序重洪都與博極羣書昌黎齊名
者文章同也而品不無優劣之數君子
可悉指而軒輊之與其於后稷逢說亦
有庶幾焉否也夫高山仰止景行行止
士君子將友天下以進於古人矧鄉之
先哲乎九原可作諸士將誰與歸也
問學以致道道一而已矣乃先王立教分
小學大學焉道果有二致乎內則稱十
歲學書記十三學樂誦詩舞勺及射御
二十學禮舞大夏則小學之教習藝其
急矣至孔子論志道據德依仁非成德
事耶乃游藝與之並稱何也載考周官
保氏敎國子以六藝則五禮六樂五射
punctuated:
抗俗遺榮、叟却秦兵者，有見幾篤行、無愧蔡碑者，有上策著書、託迹河汾之澌者，均之一隱，而孰裨於世用？或圖功麟閣，或取日虞淵，與入相中國、走卒知名者，事功同也，而行不無純駁；或才稱命世，或序重洪都，與博極羣書、昌黎齊名者，文章同也，而品不無優劣。之數君子，可悉指而軒輊之與？其於后稷、逢、說，亦有庶幾焉否也？夫高山仰止，景行行止，士君子將友天下以進於古人，矧鄉之先哲乎？九原可作，諸士將誰與歸也？

問：學以致道，道一而已矣。乃先王立教，分小學、大學焉，道果有二致乎？《內則》稱：十歲學書記，十三學樂、誦詩、舞《勺》及射御，二十學禮、舞《大夏》，則小學之教，習藝其急矣。至孔子論「志道、據德、依仁」，非成德事耶？乃「游藝」與之並稱，何也？載考《周官》，保氏敎國子以六藝，則五禮、六樂、五射、
translation_en:
…there was one who defied vulgar convention and cast aside honors, yet as an elder repelled the troops of Qin [?]; there was one who perceived the subtle signs of the times and practiced earnest conduct, worthy of the stele inscription by Cai Yong; and there was one who presented policy proposals and authored books, betaking himself to the banks of the Yellow and Fen Rivers—all alike went into reclusion, yet which of them proved most beneficial to the practical needs of the world? Again, whether it be the one whose meritorious portrait was painted in the Unicorn Pavilion, or the one who retrieved the sun from the Abyss of Yu, together with the one who entered the court as Grand Councilor of the Central State and whose name was known even to foot soldiers—their achievements in statecraft were the same, yet their personal conduct was not without differences in purity and flaw. Or whether it be the one whose talent was hailed as epoch-making, or the one whose preface was prized at Hongdu, together with the one who read exhaustively through all books and shared equal fame with Han Yu (Changli)—their literary accomplishments were the same, yet their moral character was not without gradations of superiority and inferiority. Can you identify each of these several gentlemen in full and weigh their relative merits? And among them, were there any who came close to Hou Ji, Guan Longfeng, and Fu Yue, or not? Now, "the high mountain is looked up to, the great bright road is traveled." Gentlemen-scholars seek to befriend the virtuous of the whole world so as to advance toward the ancients—how much more so the former worthies of their own native province! If the dead could be raised from the Nine Springs, with whom would you gentlemen cast your lot?

Question: Learning is the means to attain the Way, and the Way is simply one. Yet when the former kings established their system of instruction, they divided it into Lesser Learning and Greater Learning—does the Way indeed have two divergent paths? The "Pattern of the Family" (Neize) chapter states that at ten years of age one learns writing and calculation, at thirteen one learns music, recites poetry, dances the Shao, and practices archery and charioteering, and at twenty one learns ritual and dances the Daxia; thus in the instruction of the Lesser Learning, practicing the arts was the urgent priority. When Confucius discussed "setting the heart on the Way, basing oneself on virtue, and relying on humanity," were these not matters of perfected virtue? Why then did he mention "sojourning in the arts" alongside them? Furthermore, if we examine the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan), the Guardian (baoshi) taught the sons of the state the Six Arts, namely the five categories of ritual, the six kinds of music, the five techniques of archery,…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
五御六書九數是已蓋古人以爲日用
不可缺者其名物可指言否後世禮樂
闕而御不傳射與書數又等諸伎倆而
不屑然則六藝者豈其無關世用可廢
而不講與大學之敎曾氏書尚矣士類
能譚說顧出入口耳則易體會身心則
難至眞文忠行之丘文莊又補之厥旨
暢矣今二書具在其槩可陳與學者每
薄六藝而明德親民又以爲家人言耳
漫不殫心居胡以脩身出胡以應世也
諸士平生從事謂何盍共質之
===
問設官分職計在牧寧烝民謀成治化也
是故爲之守令以拊其內爲之將帥以
捍其外三代而上亡論已漢世守令如
潁川東郡扶風南陽吏治蒸蒸然顯於
神爵五鳳間矣將帥則出上谷出鴈門
出代與隴西能窮龍成狼望之王庭固
皆其袞然者孰爲優與山西襟喉三關
punctuated:
五御、六書、九數是已。蓋古人以爲日用不可缺者，其名物可指言否？後世禮樂闕而御不傳，射與書數又等諸伎倆而不屑。然則六藝者，豈其無關世用，可廢而不講與？《大學》之敎，曾氏書尚矣，士類能譚說。顧出入口耳則易，體會身心則難。至眞文忠行之，丘文莊又補之，厥旨暢矣。今二書具在，其槩可陳與？學者每薄六藝，而明德、親民又以爲家人言耳，漫不殫心。居胡以脩身？出胡以應世也？諸士平生從事謂何？盍共質之。

問：設官分職，計在牧寧烝民，謀成治化也。是故爲之守令以拊其內，爲之將帥以捍其外。三代而上亡論已，漢世守令，如潁川、東郡、扶風、南陽，吏治蒸蒸然，顯於神爵、五鳳間矣；將帥則出上谷，出鴈門，出代與隴西，能窮龍成、狼望之王庭。固皆其袞然者，孰爲優與？山西襟喉三關，
translation_en:
… the five techniques of charioteering, the six categories of script, and the nine branches of mathematics—these are they. Indeed, the ancients considered them indispensable for daily use; can their specific names and objects be pointed out and explained? In later ages, rites and music fell into deficiency and charioteering ceased to be transmitted, while archery, calligraphy, and mathematics were equated with mere petty skills and disdained. That being so, could it be that the Six Arts have no bearing on practical use in the world, and may be abandoned without being studied? As for the teachings of the Great Learning (Daxue), Master Zeng's book is of the highest antiquity, and scholars are generally able to discuss it. Yet letting it merely go in the ear and out the mouth is easy, whereas embodying and comprehending it in one's person and mind is difficult. When Zhen Wenzhong [Zhen Dexiu 真德秀] elaborated upon it [in the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi)], and Qiu Wenzhuang [Qiu Jun 丘濬] further supplemented it [in the Supplement to the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi bu)], its purport was fully elucidated. Today both books are extant in their entirety; can their general outlines be set forth? Scholars often slight the Six Arts, while regarding "manifesting luminous virtue" and "renewing the people" as mere commonplace household talk, casually failing to devote their whole hearts to them. In private life, how then can one cultivate the self? Going forth into office, how can one respond to the needs of the world? What have you gentlemen devoted yourselves to throughout your lives? Why not examine and verify this together?

Question: The purpose of establishing offices and dividing responsibilities lies in shepherding and pacifying the multitude of the people, and in planning the accomplishment of transformative governance. Therefore, Grand Administrators and Magistrates (shouling) are appointed to comfort and soothe the interior, while generals and commanders (jiangshuai) are appointed to defend against the exterior. Leaving aside the Three Dynasties and earlier, in the Han dynasty, under Grand Administrators and Magistrates such as those in Yingchuan, Dong Commandery, Fufeng, and Nanyang, administrative governance flourished and distinguished itself during the Shenjue (61–58 BCE) and Wufeng (57–54 BCE) eras. As for generals and commanders, they marched out from Shanggu, out from Yanmen, and out from Dai and Longxi, able to press all the way to the royal courts of the Xiongnu at Longcheng and Langwang. All of these were truly preeminent figures; which of them were superior? Shanxi forms a strategic throat at the Three Passes…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
關而右爲內地太平澤潞之間煙爨雞
犬相逮相聞所待理於賢守令者至切
也今之郡縣吏孰與漢循關左地逼虜
酋虜情叵測弱則黨強則跳梁即納款
通市率亦羈縻未可忘戰
當宁者嘗拊髀思將矣不識今之邊帥視在元
朔元光間者足竝程功能否耶夫內地
重牧外地重將固矣議者復責成守令
嚴城堡繕甲兵不專於內而籌邊事者
===
每欲調才望有司於附塞增厥秩祿需
以歲月勉之拊循士著爲邊鄙重抑果
有見與夫五內四肢身兼所愛安內攘
外切治不殊其勢相成其機諒有當先
者不識果何居乎爾多士志在匡時願
畢經濟勿獨使漢將吏擅美竹帛也
punctuated: 關而右爲內地，太平、澤、潞之間，煙爨雞犬相逮相聞，所待理於賢守令者至切也；今之郡縣吏孰與漢循？關左地逼虜酋，虜情叵測，弱則黨，強則跳梁，即納款通市，率亦羈縻，未可忘戰，當宁者嘗拊髀思將矣；不識今之邊帥視在元朔、元光間者，足竝程功能否耶？夫內地重牧，外地重將，固矣。議者復責成守令，嚴城堡、繕甲兵，不專於內；而籌邊事者，每欲調才望有司於附塞，增厥秩祿，需以歲月，勉之拊循士著，爲邊鄙重，抑果有見與？夫五內四肢，身兼所愛；安內攘外，切治不殊。其勢相成，其機諒有當先者，不識果何居乎？爾多士志在匡時，願畢經濟，勿獨使漢將吏擅美竹帛也。
translation_en: …To the right of the passes lies the interior, where across the region of Taiping, Zezhou, and Lu'an cooking smoke and the sounds of chickens and dogs reach and are heard by one another, and where the need for governance by worthy prefects and magistrates is most urgent; how do the prefectural and county officials of today compare with the model officials of the Han? To the left of the passes, the land presses close upon the caitiff chieftains. The dispositions of the caitiffs are unfathomable: when weak they band together, and when strong they balk and rampage; even when they submit to tribute terms and open border markets, this is generally no more than a loose-rein arrangement, so we must not forget warfare. His Majesty on the throne has at times slapped his thigh in longing for capable generals; I do not know whether our present frontier commanders, compared with those of the Yuanshuo (128–123 BCE) and Yuanguang (134–129 BCE) eras, are able to match them in measuring功 merits and abilities? Now, it is certainly true that in the interior we emphasize civil shepherds and in the exterior we emphasize military generals. Yet policy discussants further hold prefects and magistrates responsible for securing walled fortifications and repairing armor and weapons, not confining them solely to internal administration; meanwhile, those who plan frontier affairs often wish to transfer local officials of talent and reputation to posts adjacent to the frontier barriers, increasing their rank and emoluments, allowing them years and months to do their work, and encouraging them to comfort and care for the native inhabitants[?] so as to lend weight to the frontier marches—is there indeed real insight in this? Now, the five internal organs and the four limbs are both cherished by the body; pacifying the interior and repelling the exterior do not differ in their urgency for good governance. Their dynamics complement one another, yet in their strategic timing there surely is one that should take precedence—I do not know where that priority truly lies? You many scholars set your ambitions on rectifying the age; I hope you will set forth in full your statecraft, and not allow the generals and officials of the Han alone to monopolize beauty in the historical records!

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰予欲無言子貢曰子如不言則小子
何述焉子曰天何言哉四時行焉百物
生焉天何言哉
李永培
同考試官教諭朱　批〔聖人欲無言與談天自況意俱在言外作者類支離煩冗此篇冲雅渾融語意逼真宜錄以式〕
考試官教諭王　批〔沉鬱典重意更完足〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔理精調雅〕
===
聖人發至教於門人而因明以天也夫天不言
而化成至教也聖人之教猶天然何謂無述哉
且聖人無行而不與則有言非顯也無言非隱
也顧人之默識何如耳乃學者多泥於言也夫
子儆之曰予於二三子固嘗以言教矣繼自今
其殆欲無言乎而無樂乎贊詞也已子貢之學
未超乎言語之外者乃疑而問曰學夫子之道
者述夫子之言焉耳子如不言則小子何述焉
punctuated:
第壹場
四書

子曰：「予欲無言。」子貢曰：「子如不言，則小子何述焉？」子曰：「天何言哉？四時行焉，百物生焉，天何言哉？」

李永培
同考試官教諭朱　批〔聖人欲無言，與談天自況，意俱在言外。作者類支離煩冗，此篇冲雅渾融，語意逼真，宜錄以式。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔沉鬱典重，意更完足。〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔理精調雅。〕

聖人發至教於門人，而因明以天也。夫天不言而化成，至教也。聖人之教猶天然，何謂無述哉？且聖人無行而不與，則有言非顯也，無言非隱也，顧人之默識何如耳，乃學者多泥於言也。夫子儆之曰：「予於二三子，固嘗以言教矣；繼自今，其殆欲無言乎，而無樂乎贊詞也已。」子貢之學，未超乎言語之外者，乃疑而問曰：「學夫子之道者，述夫子之言焉耳。子如不言，則小子何述焉？」
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

The Master said: "I would prefer not to speak." Zigong 子貢 said: "If you, Master, do not speak, then what shall we, your disciples, have to transmit?" The Master said: "Does Heaven speak? The four seasons pursue their courses, and the hundred things are continually being produced, but does Heaven say anything?"

Li Yongpei 李永培
Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhu 朱 comments: [Both the Sage's wish not to speak and his comparison of himself through discussing Heaven carry their meaning beyond words. Writers addressing this topic typically fall into fragmentation and tedious verbosity, whereas this essay is serene, elegant, and seamlessly integrated, capturing the exact spirit of the passage. It should be recorded as a model.]
Examiner, Instructor Wang 王 comments: [Profound, dignified, and even more complete in its conception.]
Examiner, Instructor Zhao 趙 comments: [Refined in principle and elegant in tone.]

The Sage reveals the ultimate teaching to his disciples, and therefore illustrates it by reference to Heaven. Now, Heaven does not speak and yet transformation is accomplished—this is the ultimate teaching. Since the teaching of the Sage is just like that of Heaven, how could one say there is nothing to transmit? Moreover, the Sage does nothing that he does not share with his disciples; thus, speaking is not making things manifest, and not speaking is not keeping things hidden. It simply depends on how well a person silently comprehends it, yet learners mostly remain fixated on words. The Master admonished them, saying: "Toward you, my disciples, I have indeed previously taught through words; from now on, perhaps I would prefer not to speak, taking no pleasure in superfluous verbiage." Because Zigong's learning had not yet transcended the realm of words and speech, he doubted and asked: "Those who study the Master's Way simply transmit the Master's words. If you, Master, do not speak, then what shall we, your disciples, have to transmit?"

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
夫子於此有難於自明者遂以天曉之曰教以
明道也道出於天也使天道果俟於言則予何
慚焉自今觀之天何言哉而其妙有不容祕者
旋而爲四時是天之氣機也吾見其行焉闔闢
者常運而常新也散而爲百物是天之法象也
吾見其生焉小大者自形而自色也夫時非天
不行物非天不生故觀乎其用而見天道之化
然其行也以無言其生也以無言故探乎其蘊
而見天道之神運乾元於於穆而理自彰斂天
===
載於無聲而機自著此天之至教也善觀天者
即此有餘述矣吾道之默不能藏也獨與天異
乎哉賜也可無泥於言矣抑聖人果無言則六
經不必作矣何諄諄也蓋觸目皆眞超然妙悟
惟幾於神化者能之若資非上智功非眞積而
遽望其自得於語言之外不爲重誣人哉嗚呼
此六經之教與聖人身教竝行曾不若禪學之
頓悟也已
好學近乎知力行近乎仁知恥近乎勇〔知〕
punctuated:
夫子於此有難於自明者，遂以天曉之曰：「教以明道也，道出於天也。使天道果俟於言，則予何慚焉？自今觀之，天何言哉？而其妙有不容祕者。旋而爲四時，是天之氣機也；吾見其行焉，闔闢者常運而常新也。散而爲百物，是天之法象也；吾見其生焉，小大者自形而自色也。夫時非天不行，物非天不生，故觀乎其用，而見天道之化；然其行也以無言，其生也以無言，故探乎其蘊，而見天道之神。運乾元於於穆，而理自彰；斂天載於無聲，而機自著。此天之至教也。善觀天者，即此有餘述矣。吾道之默不能藏也，獨與天異乎哉？賜也可無泥於言矣！」抑聖人果無言，則六經不必作矣，何諄諄也？蓋觸目皆眞，超然妙悟，惟幾於神化者能之。若資非上智，功非眞積，而遽望其自得於語言之外，不爲重誣人哉？嗚呼！此六經之教與聖人身教竝行，曾不若禪學之頓悟也已。
好學近乎知，力行近乎仁，知恥近乎勇。〔知〕
translation_en:
At this point, the Master found it difficult to explain himself directly, and so he enlightened him by reference to Heaven, saying: "Teaching is to clarify the Way, and the Way originates from Heaven. If the Way of Heaven indeed depended upon words, why should I hesitate to speak? Yet looking at it now, what does Heaven say? Still, its wondrous workings cannot be kept hidden. Revolving to form the four seasons—this is the vital mechanism of Heaven; we see them proceed, as closing and opening constantly cycle and constantly renew. Dispersing to form the hundred things—these are the manifest forms of Heaven; we see them come into life, as small and great naturally take shape and color. Now, the seasons do not proceed without Heaven, and things do not come into life without Heaven; thus, by observing its function, one sees the transformations of the Way of Heaven. Yet their proceeding happens without words, and their coming into life happens without words; thus, by probing its depths, one sees the spirit-like subtlety of the Way of Heaven. Operating the primal power of Heaven in profound solemnity, principle naturally becomes manifest; gathering the workings of Heaven in soundlessness, its mechanism naturally becomes evident. This is the supreme teaching of Heaven. For one who is good at observing Heaven, this alone provides more than enough to transmit. The fact that my Way in its silence cannot be concealed—how could it alone differ from Heaven? Ci, you need no longer be fixated on words!" Yet if the sage truly had no words, then the Six Classics would not have needed to be composed; why was he so earnest and tireless in teaching? Indeed, seeing truth in everything that meets the eye and achieving transcendent, wondrous enlightenment is something only those approaching spirit-like transformation can do. If one's natural endowment is not of the highest wisdom and one's effort is not genuinely accumulated, yet one rashly hopes for them to grasp the truth on their own beyond words, would that not be gravely misleading people? Alas! That is why the teaching of the Six Classics goes hand in hand with the sage's teaching by personal example, and is nothing like the sudden enlightenment of Chan Buddhism.

"To be fond of learning is near to wisdom; to practice with vigor is near to humanity; to know shame is near to courage. [To know]…"

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
斯三者則知所以脩身知所以脩身則
知所以治人知所以治人則知所以治
天下國家矣
苗希益
同考試官教諭莊　批〔此題不難於敷衍難於融鍊詞〕
不費而旨躍然是作得之
考試官教諭王　批〔刋落浮詞獨存神骨〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔瑩潔精妥〕
聖人論德所由幾因推其治所由達也夫德本
===
固有彊學則幾矣明此以脩身其於治乎何有
夫子嘗謂君者若曰君人一身天德王道之會
也推昧於入德之方則身且不脩矣如王道何
故當思達德不遠於吾身企而及之存乎自勉
耳茲所求乎智未能也吾從而好學焉則愚去
而知可幾矣所求乎仁未能也吾從而力行焉
則私去而仁可幾矣所求乎勇未能也吾從而
知恥焉則仁智進而勇可幾矣之三者聚而爲
德則身法建措而爲政則治法行人患不知耳
punctuated:
斯三者，則知所以脩身；知所以脩身，則知所以治人；知所以治人，則知所以治天下國家矣。」

苗希益

同考試官教諭莊　批：〔此題不難於敷衍，難於融鍊，詞〕不費而旨躍然，是作得之。
考試官教諭王　批：〔刋落浮詞，獨存神骨。〕
考試官教諭趙　批：〔瑩潔精妥。〕

聖人論德所由幾，因推其治所由達也。夫德本固有，彊學則幾矣。明此以脩身，其於治乎何有？夫子嘗謂君者，若曰：君人一身，天德王道之會也。推昧於入德之方，則身且不脩矣，如王道何？故當思達德不遠於吾身，企而及之，存乎自勉耳。茲所求乎智，未能也；吾從而好學焉，則愚去而知可幾矣。所求乎仁，未能也；吾從而力行焉，則私去而仁可幾矣。所求乎勇，未能也；吾從而知恥焉，則仁智進而勇可幾矣。之三者，聚而爲德，則身法建；措而爲政，則治法行。人患不知耳。
translation_en:
…these three things, then he knows how to cultivate his person. Knowing how to cultivate his person, he knows how to govern others. Knowing how to govern others, he knows how to govern the empire, its states, and its families."

By Miao Xiyi 苗希益

Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhuang 莊, comments: 〔With this topic, the difficulty lies not in elaboration, but in synthesis and refinement. The words〕 are unstrained while the meaning leaps forth; this composition has achieved it.
Examiner, Instructor Wang 王, comments: 〔Stripping away superficial verbiage, it preserves only the spirit and bone.〕
Examiner, Instructor Zhao 趙, comments: 〔Lustrous, pure, precise, and apt.〕

The Sage discusses how the virtues are approximated, and thereby extends his reasoning to how governance is achieved. Now, virtue is originally inherent in us; through strenuous learning, one comes close to it. If one understands this as the means to cultivate one's person, what difficulty is there in governance?

What the Master once said of the ruler is as if to say: The person of one who rules over others is the convergence of heavenly virtue and the kingly way. Only [reading 推 as 惟?] if he is blind to the method of entering into virtue, even his own person will go uncultivated—what then can he do regarding the kingly way? Therefore, he ought to reflect that the universal virtues are not far from his own person; to reach for and attain them rests simply in self-exertion.

Here, what is sought in wisdom is not yet attained; if I accordingly love learning, then ignorance is dispelled and wisdom may be approximated. What is sought in humanity is not yet attained; if I accordingly practice with vigor, then selfishness is dispelled and humanity may be approximated. What is sought in courage is not yet attained; if I accordingly possess a sense of shame, then humanity and wisdom advance and courage may be approximated.

When these three are gathered together to form virtue, the standard for the person is established; when they are applied as government, the standard for governance is put into practice. Man's only affliction is failing to know them.…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
苟能知此則知之盡行之至而入德無遺力斯
德以備道以凝而脩身有全功由是而及人則
知人亦吾身也出吾德以區畫之人可從而理
也由是而及於天下國家則知天下國家亦吾
身也擴吾德以運量之天下國家可從而理也
何也治身之緒也以三近而脩身故其化溥德
身之維也以三近而入德故其本端德以脩身
身以圖治是在彊勉而已雖然功有三近而無
欲其要也欲之在人能使人錮蔽而失其本眞
一或汨焉三者亡矣況能拓萬化哉是惟戒愼
恐懼培此眞機擇善固執要諸純粹此堯舜精
一之傳而文武周公之家法也故曰無欲之君
可與言王道旨哉
乃若其情則可以爲善矣乃所謂善也若
夫爲不善非才之罪也
陳震
同考試官教諭侯　批〔評理精透體裁嚴整發性情才〕
三字出是知性者
punctuated:
苟能知此，則知之盡、行之至，而入德無遺力；斯德以備、道以凝，而脩身有全功。由是而及人，則知人亦吾身也，出吾德以區畫之，人可從而理也；由是而及於天下國家，則知天下國家亦吾身也，擴吾德以運量之，天下國家可從而理也。何也？治，身之緒也，以三近而脩身，故其化溥；德，身之維也，以三近而入德，故其本端。德以脩身，身以圖治，是在彊勉而已。雖然，功有三近，而無欲其要也。欲之在人，能使人錮蔽而失其本眞，一或汨焉，三者亡矣，況能拓萬化哉？是惟戒愼恐懼，培此眞機；擇善固執，要諸純粹。此堯舜精一之傳，而文武周公之家法也。故曰「無欲之君，可與言王道」，旨哉！
乃若其情，則可以爲善矣，乃所謂善也。若夫爲不善，非才之罪也。
陳震
同考試官教諭侯　批〔評理精透，體裁嚴整。發「性」、「情」、「才」〕三字出，是知性者。
translation_en:
If one can know these three things, then knowledge is exhausted and practice reaches its utmost, leaving no effort spared in entering into virtue; thus virtue is made complete, the Way is consolidated, and self-cultivation achieves its full efficacy. Extending from this to other people, one knows that governing others also stems from one's own person; by bringing forth one's virtue to order and plan for them, others can thereby be governed. Extending from this to the empire, the state, and the family, one knows that the empire, the state, and the family also stem from one's own person; by expanding one's virtue to encompass and manage them, the empire, the state, and the family can thereby be governed. Why is this? Governance is the extension of the self; because one cultivates the self through the three things that come near to the virtues, its transforming influence is widespread. Virtue is the mainstay of the self; because one enters into virtue through those three things, its foundation is upright. Using virtue to cultivate the self, and using the self to plan for governance—this lies simply in strenuous effort. Even so, while effort lies in the three things that come near, being free of selfish desires is the essential point. When desires reside in a person, they can make him obstructed and blinded so that he loses his original genuineness; if he is once submerged in them, the three virtues are lost—how much less could he expand into the myriad transformations? Therefore, one must only be cautious and apprehensive to nurture this genuinevital spring, and choose what is good and hold fast to it, pursuing it to pure perfection. This is the transmission of refinement and single-mindedness from Yao and Shun, and the family method of King Wen, King Wu, and the Duke of Zhou. Thus it is said, "With a ruler free of desires, one can speak of the Kingly Way." Profound indeed!

"As for one's feelings (qing), they are such that one can do good; this is what I mean by saying that human nature is good. If a man does what is not good, that is not the fault of his natural endowment (cai)."

By Chen Zhen 陳震.
Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Hou 侯 comments: 〔The analysis of principle is precise and penetrating, and the structure is rigorous and orderly. In bringing out the three terms "human nature" (xing), "feelings" (qing), and "natural endowment" (cai)〕, he shows himself to be one who truly understands human nature.

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭王　批〔精而不鑿鍊而不削〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔峻潔明爽〕
大賢道性善自情與才而決之也蓋情與才皆
性出也觀情善而才無不善焉性善不有徵乎
孟子曉公都子若曰天下率言性而不求其自
然之故則其說之紛紛無惑也自今言之性一
而已矣發而爲情運而爲才者皆是也使情與
才而有不善焉則性可以不善言矣乃若其情
則感而遂通常至順而不拂觸之斯應恒至正
===
而無邪情效天下之動而其用未鑿者天理之
流行也固可以爲善也則知性立天下之有而
其體未漓者天眞之各足也乃所以謂善也蓋
性不可見而見諸情因其所可見以遡其所不
可見則性之本體可識矣若夫爲不善豈天之
降才爾殊哉物至而化始乖其順應之常蔽交
則遷遂失其用和之正才隨性具而習或移之
容有濟惡者矣此實人爲耳良能之妙用不如
是也性與才凝而欲或汩之容有悖道者矣此
punctuated:
考試官教諭王　批：〔精而不鑿，鍊而不削。〕
考試官教諭趙　批：〔峻潔明爽。〕
大賢道性善，自情與才而決之也。蓋情與才皆性出也。觀情善而才無不善焉，性善不有徵乎？孟子曉公都子若曰：天下率言性，而不求其自然之故，則其說之紛紛無惑也。自今言之，性一而已矣，發而爲情、運而爲才者皆是也。使情與才而有不善焉，則性可以不善言矣。乃若其情，則感而遂通，常至順而不拂；觸之斯應，恒至正而無邪。情效天下之動而其用未鑿者，天理之流行也，固可以爲善也；則知性立天下之有而其體未漓者，天眞之各足也，乃所以謂善也。蓋性不可見而見諸情，因其所可見以遡其所不可見，則性之本體可識矣。若夫爲不善，豈天之降才爾殊哉？物至而化，始乖其順應之常；蔽交則遷，遂失其用和之正。才隨性具而習或移之，容有濟惡者矣，此實人爲耳，良能之妙用不如是也；性與才凝而欲或汩之，容有悖道者矣，此
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: [Precise without being forced; refined without being pared down.]
Examiner and Instructor Zhao comments: [Lofty, pure, clear, and brisk.]

When the great worthy spoke of human nature as good, he determined this from the emotions and the natural capacities. For both the emotions and the capacities issue from human nature. When one observes that the emotions are good and that in the capacities there is nothing that is not good, is there not proof that human nature is good?

Mencius enlightened Gongduzi as if to say: Everyone in the world speaks of human nature, yet if they do not seek the basis of its natural spontaneity, then it is no wonder that their doctrines are so confused and varied. Speaking of it now, human nature is simply one; what issues forth as emotions and operates as capacities is all this same nature. Suppose that in the emotions and the capacities there were something not good; then human nature could be spoken of as not good.

As for the emotions, when stirred they immediately penetrate, always remaining supremely compliant and unresistant; when touched they respond at once, constantly remaining supremely upright and without perversity. That the emotions pattern themselves on the movements of the world while their functioning remains uncontrived is the flowing operation of Heavenly principle; thus one can indeed do good. From this one knows that human nature establishes the realities of the world while its substance remains unadulterated, the Heavenly truth being complete in each; and this is why it is called good. For human nature cannot be seen, yet it is seen in the emotions; if on the basis of what can be seen one traces back to what cannot be seen, then the original substance of human nature can be recognized.

As for someone doing what is not good, how could the capacities endowed by Heaven be so different? Only when external things arrive and one is transformed by them does one first depart from the constancy of compliant response; when obscurations intermingle and one shifts along with them, one thereupon loses the correctness of harmonious functioning. Capacities are complete along with human nature, yet habit may alter them, so that there may be cases of aiding evil; this is in fact merely human artifice—the marvelous functioning of innate ability is not like this. Human nature and capacities coalesce together, yet desires may submerge them, so that there may be cases of going against the Way; this…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
實人謀耳眞機之順動不如是也何可罪夫才
耶要之方至靜之中則所性渾淪不知有情也
亦不知有才也而其善已具及有觸之際則所
性感動情胥此出也才亦胥此出也而其善始
形吾之道性善而衆論不惑也以是耳子又何
疑焉雖然上智下愚有生不移清濁厚薄分限
各異人性果皆善乎嗚呼此氣質之性也性本
無二顧天命之性附於形氣二五雜揉故不得
而齊耳彼三說者彷彿氣質而未窺天命非孟
===
子辭而闢之性學幾晦矣
易
象曰地中有水師君子以容民畜衆
張　美
同考試官教諭朱　批　題本正大但作者類剿陳言委
厲可厭練達新警無踰此篇
考試官教諭王　批　體莊詞瞻
考試官教諭趙　批　典雅可觀
象傳發師義見寓兵於農之政焉夫兵非治世
punctuated:
實人謀耳，眞機之順動不如是也，何可罪夫才耶？要之，方至靜之中，則所性渾淪，不知有情也，亦不知有才也，而其善已具；及有觸之際，則所性感動，情胥此出也，才亦胥此出也，而其善始形。吾之道性善，而衆論不惑也，以是耳，子又何疑焉？雖然，上智下愚，有生不移，清濁厚薄，分限各異，人性果皆善乎？嗚呼！此氣質之性也。性本無二，顧天命之性附於形氣，二五雜揉，故不得而齊耳。彼三說者，彷彿氣質而未窺天命，非孟子辭而闢之，性學幾晦矣。

易
象曰：「地中有水，師；君子以容民畜衆。」
張美
同考試官教諭朱批：題本正大，但作者類剿陳言，委厲可厭，練達新警，無踰此篇。

《象傳》發《師》義，見寓兵於農之政焉。夫兵，非治世
translation_en:
… is in truth merely human contrivance; the compliant movement of the true mechanism of nature is not like this. How can one blame natural endowment (cai)? In sum, when in a state of utmost tranquility, one's nature is an undifferentiated whole: one knows neither of feelings (qing) nor of endowment, yet its goodness is already complete. When it is stirred by contact with things, one's nature is moved to respond: feelings all issue forth from this, and endowment likewise issues forth from this, and only then does its goodness take form. That I speak of human nature as good and am not perplexed by the multitude of theories is simply because of this. What further doubts can you have? Even so, the highest wise and the lowest愚 (foolish) cannot be changed from birth, and the allotments of clear and turbid, thick and thin, each differ—is human nature really all good? Alas! This is the nature of psychophysical stuff (qizhi zhi xing). Nature is originally not twofold, yet the Heaven-ordained nature is attached to physical form and vital energy; the two modes (yin and yang) and Five Agents mingle and blend, and therefore they cannot be uniform. Those three theories vaguely glimpsed the psychophysical nature without peering into the Mandate of Heaven; had Mencius not refuted them with his words, the learning of human nature would almost have been obscured.

Book of Changes (Yi)

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
之所諱也君子觀象於師而寓諸農焉其爲天
下慮遠矣夫子傳師之象以爲王者以德綏天
下而不能去夫兵者凡以宣德威也此卦之象
下坎水而上坤地水畜於地而其用常不測地
容夫水而其體常至靜玩斯象也若天下之有
師然君子體此謂恃承平而去武備勢必弛外
黎庶而詰戎兵法必擾非善衛國者也於是以
天下之利養天下之民以天下之民足天下之
兵民方以生聚恬我而吾爲之足其財凡以撫
===
之也然其生厚則其勇自充一訓練焉而折衝
禦侮之士在茲矣民方以養恬恃我而吾爲之
薄其賦凡以保之也然其養素則其忠自奮一
倡率焉而尊君親上之衆在茲矣無事則羣然
樂業惟是比閭焉耳族黨州鄉焉耳而可使卽
戎也何民非兵有事則翕然用命惟是伍兩焉
耳卒旅軍師焉耳而常寓於農也何兵非民此
之謂天下之大慮此之謂天下之大政而與象
之地中有水者何異哉吁君子之於師也深矣
punctuated: 之所諱也，君子觀象於《師》，而寓諸農焉，其爲天下慮遠矣。夫子傳《師》之象，以爲王者以德綏天下，而不能去夫兵者，凡以宣德威也。此卦之象，下坎水而上坤地。水畜於地，而其用常不測；地容夫水，而其體常至靜。玩斯象也，若天下之有師然。君子體此，謂恃承平而去武備，勢必弛；外黎庶而詰戎兵，法必擾，非善衛國者也。於是以天下之利，養天下之民；以天下之民，足天下之兵。民方以生聚恬我，而吾爲之足其財，凡以撫之也；然其生厚則其勇自充，一訓練焉，而折衝禦侮之士在茲矣。民方以養恬恃我，而吾爲之薄其賦，凡以保之也；然其養素則其忠自奮，一倡率焉，而尊君親上之衆在茲矣。無事則羣然樂業，惟是比閭焉耳、族黨州鄉焉耳，而可使卽戎也，何民非兵？有事則翕然用命，惟是伍兩焉耳、卒旅軍師焉耳，而常寓於農也，何兵非民？此之謂天下之大慮，此之謂天下之大政，而與象之地中有水者何異哉！吁！君子之於師也深矣。
translation_en:
… is avoided. When the superior man contemplates the image in the Shi (The Army) hexagram and lodges the military within the peasantry, his concern for the realm reaches far indeed.

In transmitting the Image of the Shi hexagram, the Master held that while a true king pacifies the realm through virtue, the reason he cannot dispense with military force is altogether to proclaim both his virtue and his majesty. In the image of this hexagram, Kan (water) is below and Kun (earth) is above. Water is stored within the earth, and its function is ever unfathomable; the earth contains the water, and its substance is ever utterly tranquil. When one ponders this image, it is just like the realm's possession of an army. Embodying this, the superior man recognizes that to rely on lasting peace and cast aside military preparedness will inevitably lead to laxity, whereas to set aside the common people while marshaling troops and weapons will inevitably throw the laws into disorder—neither is the way of one skilled at defending the state. Therefore, he uses the profits of the realm to nourish the people of the realm, and uses the people of the realm to supply the troops of the realm.

When the people look to us in peace for their livelihood and gathering together, we make their wealth sufficient simply in order to comfort them; yet once their livelihood is generous, their courage naturally fills out, so that as soon as they are trained, warriors who can repel enemy thrusts and ward off aggression are to be found right here. When the people rely on us for their tranquil nourishment, we lighten their taxes simply in order to protect them; yet once they have been steadily nourished, their loyalty naturally stirs to action, so that as soon as they are led forward, multitudes who honor their ruler and feel affection for their superiors are to be found right here.

In times of peace, they all rejoice in their livelihoods together: there are only the five-family neighborhoods and twenty-five-family villages, the hundred-family clans, five-hundred-family quarters, two-thousand-five-hundred-family districts, and twelve-thousand-five-hundred-family regiones—and yet they can be made to take up arms at once. What peasant is not a soldier? In times of crisis, they harmoniously obey orders in unison: there are only the squads of five and platoons of twenty-five, the companies of a hundred, battalions of five hundred, regiments of two thousand five hundred, and armies of twelve thousand five hundred—and yet they are permanently lodged among the peasantry. What soldier is not a peasant? This is what is meant by the great foresight for the realm; this is what is meant by the great governance of the realm. And how does it differ from the image of water within the earth? Ah, profound indeed is the superior man's understanding of the army!

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
蓋古人寓兵於農必井田必封建必舉井邑丘
甸之衆隷於司徒而有事始授司馬故能省供
億轉輸之勞而民不稱病自兵民判而天下始
多失所之民矣嗚呼古制不可復矣開屯田練
土兵寛民之力玆非明王馭世之長策哉
聖人之大寳曰位何以守位曰仁何以聚
人曰財理財正辭禁民爲非曰義
李永培
同考試官敎諭朱　批〔聖人功業塲中發者率多冗浮〕
===
此篇眞切瑩暢可以式矣
考試官敎諭王　批〔冠裳雅練〕
考試官敎諭趙　批〔調古詞精〕
大傳舉位重於聖人而功業弘焉蓋聖人之業
非位不彰也居大君之位而功業弘於天下矣
大傳論卦爻吉凶而及於聖人也若謂生物固
在於天地而賛化實待於聖人此皆易理也夫
聖人者肖天之易法地之簡豈不大德哉顧必
作之君師而後可建功立業於天下則所謂大
punctuated:
蓋古人寓兵於農，必井田，必封建，必舉井邑丘甸之衆隷於司徒，而有事始授司馬，故能省供億轉輸之勞，而民不稱病。自兵民判，而天下始多失所之民矣。嗚呼！古制不可復矣。開屯田，練土兵，寛民之力，玆非明王馭世之長策哉？

聖人之大寳曰位。何以守位？曰仁。何以聚人？曰財。理財正辭、禁民爲非曰義。
李永培
同考試官敎諭朱　批〔聖人功業，塲中發者率多冗浮，〕此篇眞切瑩暢，可以式矣。
考試官敎諭王　批〔冠裳雅練。〕
考試官敎諭趙　批〔調古詞精。〕

《大傳》舉位重於聖人，而功業弘焉。蓋聖人之業，非位不彰也；居大君之位，而功業弘於天下矣。《大傳》論卦爻吉凶而及於聖人也，若謂：生物固在於天地，而賛化實待於聖人，此皆《易》理也。夫聖人者，肖天之易，法地之簡，豈不大德哉？顧必作之君師，而後可建功立業於天下，則所謂大
translation_en:
For when the ancients lodged soldiers among the farmers, there had to be the well-field system, there had to be feudal enfeoffment, and the multitudes of the wells, hamlets, districts, and tracts had to be placed under the Minister of Education (situ), only being handed over to the Minister of War (sima) when emergencies arose. Therefore, they were able to spare the populace the toil of provisioning and transport, and the people did not complain of hardship. Ever since soldiers and civilians were separated, the realm began to have many displaced people. Alas! The ancient system cannot be restored. Opening military state farms, training local troops, and sparing the strength of the people—is this not a long-term strategy for an enlightened ruler governing the world?

"The great treasure of the sage is called position. How does one guard position? Through benevolence [note: standard text reads 'men' (人), as echoed in the essay below]. How does one gather men? Through wealth. Regulating wealth, rectifying words, and forbidding the people from doing wrong is called righteousness."

Li Yongpei 李永pei

Associate Examiner and Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhu comments: 〔Those in the examination compound who expounded upon the achievements and enterprise of the sage were mostly verbose and superficial;〕 this essay is genuine, incisive, lucid, and fluent—it can serve as a model.
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: 〔Dignified, elegant, and well-crafted.〕
Examiner and Instructor Zhao comments: 〔Antiquarian in tone and refined in diction.〕

The Great Commentary (Dazhuan) highlights the importance of position to the sage, whereby his achievements and enterprise are made vast. For the enterprise of the sage does not become manifest without position; only when he occupies the position of the great sovereign are his achievements and enterprise broadened throughout the realm. When the Great Commentary discusses the auspiciousness and inauspiciousness of hexagrams and lines and extends to the sage, it is as if to say: Generating things indeed lies with Heaven and Earth, yet assisting their transformations truly awaits the sage—all of this is the principle of the Changes (Yi). Now, the sage resembles the ease of Heaven and models himself on the simplicity of Earth; is this not great virtue? Yet he must be made ruler and teacher before he can establish achievements and found an enterprise in the world. Thus, what is called the great…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
寶者位是已位實於聖人非固利之實惟資之
也然天位惟艱孰與守之曰人焉耳人爲邦本
人附而國隨之矣民心至渙何以聚之曰財焉
耳財爲民命財散而民附之矣若夫聚民之財
能勿理乎訓民之辭能勿正乎民之日入於非
也能勿禁乎此皆聖人因天下之勢而爲之者
其要維何亦曰義而已矣行而宜之之謂義是
王道之紀而化裁天下之微權也聖人奉此以
理財而民可富矣奉此以正辭而民可淑矣奉
===
此以禁民非而民不底於頗僻矣蓋斟酌有道
則其政平劑量得中則其化順此所以功業參
天地而於大寶之位爲無負也不然於位奚取
焉夫聖人之功業天地萬物賴之而卦爻吉凶
實配之易書功用之大固如此雖然天下不可
一日無聖人而聖人實未嘗計功於天下彼其
一念兢兢動稽諸道卽官天地洽六合功業綦
隆自聖人視之以爲分所當然而此心無有焉
盛德之至也故聖人之業益易簡而聖人之德
punctuated: 寶者，位是已。位實於聖人，非固利之，實惟資之也。然天位惟艱，孰與守之？曰：人焉耳。人爲邦本，人附而國隨之矣。民心至渙，何以聚之？曰：財焉耳。財爲民命，財散而民附之矣。若夫聚民之財，能勿理乎？訓民之辭，能勿正乎？民之日入於非也，能勿禁乎？此皆聖人因天下之勢而爲之者。其要維何？亦曰義而已矣。行而宜之之謂義，是王道之紀，而化裁天下之微權也。聖人奉此以理財，而民可富矣；奉此以正辭，而民可淑矣；奉此以禁民非，而民不底於頗僻矣。蓋斟酌有道，則其政平；劑量得中，則其化順。此所以功業參天地，而於大寶之位爲無負也。不然，於位奚取焉？夫聖人之功業，天地萬物賴之，而卦爻吉凶實配之。《易》書功用之大，固如此。雖然，天下不可一日無聖人，而聖人實未嘗計功於天下。彼其一念兢兢，動稽諸道，卽官天地、洽六合，功業綦隆，自聖人視之，以爲分所當然，而此心無有焉，盛德之至也。故聖人之業益易簡，而聖人之德
translation_en: … treasure is none other than position. As for what position truly means to the sage, he certainly does not treat it as personal profit, but rather relies upon it as a resource. Yet the Heavenly position is arduous; with what shall one guard it? The answer is: simply with people. People are the foundation of the state; when the people attach themselves to it, the state follows. The hearts of the people are easily scattered; with what shall one gather them? The answer is: simply with wealth. Wealth is the lifeblood of the people; when wealth is distributed, the people attach themselves to him. Now, as for the wealth that gathers the people, can one fail to regulate it? As for the words that instruct the people, can one fail to rectify them? As the people daily slip into wrongdoing, can one fail to prohibit them? All of these are what the sage does by adapting to the circumstances of the world. What is their essential principle? It is simply called righteousness. To carry things out appropriately is called righteousness; this is the guiding thread of the Kingly Way and the subtle authority for transforming and regulating the world. When the sage upholds this to regulate wealth, the people can be enriched; when he upholds this to rectify words, the people can be made virtuous; when he upholds this to prohibit the people from wrongdoing, the people will not sink into perversity and depravity. Indeed, when deliberation follows the Way, governance is equitable; when adjustment hits the mean, transformation is smooth. This is how his achievements and enterprises form a triad with Heaven and Earth, and how he proves worthy of the position of the great treasure. Otherwise, what would there be to value in position? Now, Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things rely upon the achievements and enterprises of the sage, and the auspiciousness and inauspiciousness of the hexagrams and lines truly correspond to them. So great indeed is the functional efficacy of the Book of Changes (Yi)! Even so, while the world cannot go a single day without the sage, the sage has truly never calculated his merit in the world. With every thought cautious and reverent, and every action examined against the Way, even when he orders Heaven and Earth and harmonizes the six directions so that his achievements and enterprises are supremely grand, from the sage's own perspective he regards this merely as his natural duty, and retains nothing of it in his mind—this is the ultimate of abundant virtue. Therefore, the enterprise of the sage becomes ever more easy and simple, and the virtue of the sage…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
書
帝曰咨汝二十有二人欽哉惟時亮天功
三載考績三考黜陟幽明庶績咸熙
苗希益
同考試官教諭莊　批　莊重謹嚴且發虞廷人法妙任
之旨透徹無遺
考試官教諭王　批　詞精確而意圓融
考試官教諭趙　批　整飭雅練
===
聖世御臣有道治之所以隆也夫治必待人而
舉也聖帝嚴飭而綜核之焉御待其道矣治之
隆也以此在昔大猷之世君雖聖未嘗不任乎
臣臣雖良未嘗不厲以法是故法以馭人人以
立政君哉舜也用是道耳觀其於岳牧則已詢
咨於九官則已分任至此又總之以命而合衆
職之兼咨所以申其意也勅之以欽而俾天工
之寅亮所以作其勤也此其飭臣之詞亦既嚴
矣然又以爲圖治固在任人考成不可無法於
punctuated:
《書》

「帝曰：『咨！汝二十有二人，欽哉，惟時亮天功。』三載考績，三考，黜陟幽明，庶績咸熙。」

苗希益
同考試官教諭莊　批：莊重謹嚴，且發虞廷人法妙任之旨，透徹無遺。
考試官教諭王　批：詞精確而意圓融。
考試官教諭趙　批：整飭雅練。

聖世御臣有道，治之所以隆也。夫治必待人而舉也，聖帝嚴飭而綜核之焉，御待其道矣，治之隆也以此。在昔大猷之世，君雖聖，未嘗不任乎臣；臣雖良，未嘗不厲以法。是故法以馭人，人以立政。君哉舜也，用是道耳。觀其於岳、牧，則已詢咨；於九官，則已分任。至此又總之以命，而合衆職之兼咨，所以申其意也；勅之以欽，而俾天工之寅亮，所以作其勤也。此其飭臣之詞，亦既嚴矣。然又以爲圖治固在任人，考成不可無法。於
translation_en:
Classic of Documents (Shu)

"The Emperor said: 'Ah! You twenty-two men, be reverent! Aid in the timely accomplishments of Heaven.' Every three years there was an examination of merits, and after three examinations the undeserving were degraded and the deserving promoted, whereby all the achievements were fully resplendent."

Miao Xiyi 苗希益
Associate Examiner, County Director of Studies Zhuang, comments: Solemn and rigorous; furthermore, it brings out the purport of how the court of Yu wonderfully employed both men and laws, thoroughly and without omission.
Examiner, County Director of Studies Wang, comments: The diction is precise and the meaning is well-rounded and harmonious.
Examiner, County Director of Studies Zhao, comments: Well-ordered, refined, and practiced.

When a sacred age governs its ministers according to the proper Way, this is whereby governance flourishes. Now, governance must await the right men in order to be raised up; when the sage emperor strictly admonishes them and comprehensively verifies their performance, governing and treating them achieves its proper Way, and it is through this that governance flourishes. In the ages of great plans in antiquity, although the ruler was sagely, he never failed to rely upon his ministers; although the ministers were worthy, they were never not spurred on by laws. Therefore, laws were used to direct men, and men were used to establish administration. What a true ruler was Shun! He simply used this Way. Observe how toward the Four Peaks and the Twelve Pastors, he had already inquired and consulted; toward the Nine Officials, he had already apportioned responsibilities. Coming to this point, he further summed it up with a general charge, combining all the various offices in a collective consultation, which was how he reiterated his intention; he admonished them to be reverent, causing them respectfully to assist in the work of Heaven, which was how he roused their diligence. Thus his words in admonishing his ministers were already strict indeed. Yet he also considered that while planning for governance certainly lies in employing men, examining their accomplishments cannot be without laws. Thereupon…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
是試以三載則勤惰得其大端而考績之典立
焉積之三考則幽明定於久任而黜陟之典行
焉此其勵臣之法亦旣精矣由是旌別詳明人
心因之以競勸精神鼓舞治具由之以畢張觀
績於九官則紀綱振舉咸熙於朝廷之上矣觀
績於岳牧則化理恢弘咸熙於邦國之間矣至
此則臣職盡明天功巳亮而二十二人斯無負
君命哉然亦孰非舜之圖任者先之也吁玆有
虞之治所以不可及也巳世稱唐虞多才舜始
===
任法豈風會至此不能不因時以立政與然觀
玄德在躬則其端拱穆清之上熙績光天之下
者固自有本也豈徒法之能爲耶後之務勵精
者不求其本而區區名實之綜覈以求小補之
末效亦巳過矣
嚴恭寅畏天命自度
党一經
同考試官教諭莊　批〔商王之無逸在敬天而敬在典〕
學之此文剔肯明朗而詞復雅練深得訓誨之體錄之
punctuated:
是試以三載，則勤惰得其大端，而考績之典立焉；積之三考，則幽明定於久任，而黜陟之典行焉。此其勵臣之法，亦旣精矣。由是旌別詳明，人心因之以競勸；精神鼓舞，治具由之以畢張。觀績於九官，則紀綱振舉，咸熙於朝廷之上矣；觀績於岳牧，則化理恢弘，咸熙於邦國之間矣。至此則臣職盡明，天功巳亮，而二十二人斯無負君命哉！然亦孰非舜之圖任者先之也？吁！玆有虞之治，所以不可及也巳。世稱唐虞多才，舜始任法，豈風會至此，不能不因時以立政與？然觀玄德在躬，則其端拱穆清之上，熙績光天之下者，固自有本也，豈徒法之能爲耶？後之務勵精者，不求其本，而區區名實之綜覈，以求小補之末效，亦巳過矣。

「嚴恭寅畏，天命自度。」
党一經
同考試官教諭莊　批〔商王之無逸在敬天，而敬在典學之[？]。此文剔肯明朗，而詞復雅練，深得訓誨之體。錄之。〕
translation_en:
…this, he tested them over three years, whereby the broad outlines of their diligence or negligence were ascertained, and the statute for evaluating merit was established; accumulating three such evaluations, the muddled and the enlightened were determined through long tenure, and the statute for demotion and promotion was put into practice. In this way, his method for encouraging his ministers was already refined. From this, distinctions of merit and demerit were detailed and clear, and men's minds were thereby spurred to compete in diligence; spirits were roused and inspired, and the instruments of governance were thereby fully deployed. Observing the achievements of the Nine Ministers, the foundational rules were invigorated and upheld, and all enterprises flourished within the royal court; observing the achievements of the Four Peaks and Twelve Pastors, transformative governance was broadened and enlarged, and all enterprises flourished among the feudal states. At this point, the duties of the ministers were completely fulfilled, the work of Heaven was already aided and made bright, and those twenty-two men thus did not fail their sovereign's command! Yet how was any of this not preceded by Shun's careful planning in appointing them? Alas! This is why the governance of the Lord of Yu could never be equaled. The world says that the eras of Tang and Yu abounded in talent, and that Shun was the first to rely on laws—could it be that as the trends of the times reached this point, one could not help but establish governance in accordance with the age? Yet when we observe that mysterious virtue resided in his own person, then his sitting with folded hands in serene majesty above while making achievements flourish beneath the glorious heavens certainly had its own root; how could it be something achieved by laws alone? When those in later ages who strive for vigorous governance do not seek this root, but busy themselves trivially with the comprehensive verification of names and realities in order to seek minor, supplementary, superficial effects, they have already gone too far.

"Grave, respectful, reverent, and fearful, he measured himself by the Mandate of Heaven."
Dang Yijing 党一經
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhuang 莊, comments: [The Shang king's avoidance of luxurious ease lay in revering Heaven, and his reverence lay in measuring himself (?) by it. This essay cuts to the crux with clarity and brightness, while its diction is moreover elegant and polished; it deeply grasps the style of instructional admonition. Selected for inclusion.]

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭王　批〔渾融雅健〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔詞簡義明〕
商王敬以律身而無所於逸也夫敬脩身之要
也商王以此自律尚何暇逸之有是宜周公舉
以訓成王也若曰君道之貴於無逸也惟其克
敬天命者得之也吾觀商王中宗而知其有進
於是矣彼天命之在人君非所自有者乎顧奉
之在身而凝之則在敬也以逸豫失之者多矣
其惟中宗莊重自居外無不嚴之貌矣又謙抑
===
於應感之間何其恭與欽肅是運內無不寅之
心矣又戒懼於宥密之地何其畏與存至敬於
淵衷而檢身常若不及約此躬於矩範而事天
眞若有臨動無不敬罔褻天也愈矜持則愈檢
束蓋由心之不敢褻者而自律焉其動無違理
矣乎靜無不敬罔弃天也日收斂則日防閑蓋
由心之不敢弃者而自飭焉其靜不過則矣乎
心與天相游衍是謂以敬勝不以怠勝也理與
身相周旋不惟不敢逸亦不暇逸也斯中宗之
punctuated:
考試官教諭王　批〔渾融雅健。〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔詞簡義明。〕

商王敬以律身，而無所於逸也。夫敬，脩身之要也，商王以此自律，尚何暇逸之有？是宜周公舉以訓成王也。若曰：君道之貴於無逸也，惟其克敬天命者得之也。吾觀商王中宗，而知其有進於是矣。彼天命之在人君，非所自有者乎？顧奉之在身，而凝之則在敬也，以逸豫失之者多矣。其惟中宗，莊重自居，外無不嚴之貌矣，又謙抑於應感之間，何其恭與！欽肅是運，內無不寅之心矣，又戒懼於宥密之地，何其畏與！存至敬於淵衷，而檢身常若不及；約此躬於矩範，而事天眞若有臨。動無不敬，罔褻天也，愈矜持則愈檢束，蓋由心之不敢褻者而自律焉，其動無違理矣乎！靜無不敬，罔弃天也，日收斂則日防閑，蓋由心之不敢弃者而自飭焉，其靜不過則矣乎！心與天相游衍，是謂以敬勝，不以怠勝也；理與身相周旋，不惟不敢逸，亦不暇逸也。斯中宗之
translation_en:
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: [Harmoniously integrated, elegant and vigorous.]
Examiner and Instructor Zhao comments: [Concise in wording and clear in meaning.]

The Shang king regulated himself with reverence, and thus had no occasion for idleness. Now reverence is the essential principle of cultivating the self; when the Shang king regulated himself by this, what leisure for idleness could there still be? It was therefore fitting that the Duke of Zhou cited him to instruct King Cheng. It is as if he said: That the Way of the ruler values avoidance of idleness is attained only by one who is able to revere the Mandate of Heaven. When I observe the Shang king Zhongzong, I know that he advanced in this respect. Is not the Mandate of Heaven that rests upon a ruler something that he naturally possesses in himself? Yet upholding it lies in one's person, while consolidating it lies in reverence; many are those who have lost it through idleness and pleasure. Only Zhongzong maintained himself with dignity, so that outwardly there was no aspect of his demeanor that was not grave; and furthermore, he was humble and restrained in responding to affairs—how respectful he was! Exercising reverent solemnity, inwardly there was no aspect of his mind that was not sincere; and furthermore, he was cautious and apprehensive in the quiet seclusion of his heart—how fearful he was! Preserving utmost reverence in the depths of his breast, he examined himself as if always falling short; binding his person within rules and standards, he served Heaven as if it were truly looking down upon him. In action he was never without reverence, never profaning Heaven; the more self-possessed he was, the more he restrained himself. Because he regulated himself from a mind that dared not profane it, did not his actions never violate principle? In stillness he was never without reverence, never forsaking Heaven; the more he gathered himself in day by day, the more he guarded himself day by day. Because he disciplined himself from a mind that dared not forsake it, did not his stillness never transgress the rule?
