In my humble opinion, although the affections celebrated in the ode "Cry of the Ospreys" (Guanju) are not unharmonious [? 爭, likely a misprint for 摯 "sincere" or 專 "devoted"], it is even more fitting to value the benefit of the queen's dawn admonitions, when she removes her hairpins and ear-ornaments, as in the ode "Cockcrow" (Jiming). Although the fraternal bond celebrated in the ode "Cherry Tree" (Changdi) is not uncordial, it is even more fitting to take warning from the playful indiscretions of carving a paulownia-leaf scepter in jest or sharing the imperial carriage.

In governing subordinates, he has never been stinting in grace; yet every frown and smile must be guarded, so that those who court favor by praising a fine tree or humoring a falcon on the arm are given no opportunity to practice their arts. In maintaining amity with imperial kinsmen, he has never been less than generous; yet the handle of sovereign authority must never shift, so that those who act with unbridled arrogance—like those of old who requested land from the Directorate for Imperial Manufactories (Kaogong) or seized the Qinyuan estate—are not permitted to run rampant. If this is done, then abundant affection will not become excessive intimacy, broad grace will not become excessive partiality, and harmony will never degenerate into laxity!

When gazing upon …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
廟貌之清閟宜凜然思堂構不易承仰
祖德之崇巍宜儼然思
謨烈不易守觀文始武功之舞宜思經營開創
之艱難睹
衣冠弓劒之陳宜思櫛風沐雨之勞苦如此
則祼獻非虛文烝嘗非故事而敬其無懈
矣乎雖然雝肅之爲用大矣發舒嚴凝則
天地之撰也張弛互用則文武之軌也中
正和平則禮樂之本也保合太和無逸乃
===
逸則壽命之原也致和以臻位育篤恭以
平天下則神化之極也豈特一在宮一在
廟之當兢兢哉
聖主識能
覽往喆之懿訓率理道之訏謨鏡保泰之長
策懷慎終之令圖由在
宮在
廟而達於無不在由能雝能肅而達於無不雝
無不肅以忠萬方以軼百代則太和充塞
punctuated: 廟貌之清閟，宜凜然思堂構不易承；仰祖德之崇巍，宜儼然思謨烈不易守；觀《文始》、《武功》之舞，宜思經營開創之艱難；睹衣冠、弓劒之陳，宜思櫛風沐雨之勞苦。如此，則祼獻非虛文，烝嘗非故事，而敬其無懈矣乎！雖然，雝肅之爲用大矣。發舒嚴凝，則天地之撰也；張弛互用，則文武之軌也；中正和平，則禮樂之本也；保合太和，無逸乃逸，則壽命之原也；致和以臻位育，篤恭以平天下，則神化之極也。豈特一在宮、一在廟之當兢兢哉！聖主誠能覽往喆之懿訓，率理道之訏謨，鏡保泰之長策，懷慎終之令圖，由在宮在廟而達於無不在，由能雝能肅而達於無不雝、無不肅，以惠萬方，以軼百代，則太和充塞
translation_en:
… the tranquil solemnity of the ancestral temple, one should reflect with awe that the foundation built by one's predecessors is not easily inherited; looking up at the lofty grandeur of ancestral virtue, one should reflect with gravity that their grand plans and glorious achievements are not easily preserved; watching the dances of "Civil Beginning" (Wenshi) and "Martial Merit" (Wugong), one should reflect on the hardships of planning and founding the dynasty; beholding the display of the ancestors' robes, caps, bows, and swords, one should reflect on the toil of their being combed by the wind and washed by the rain. If one acts thus, then libations and offerings will not be empty formalities, winter and autumn sacrifices will not be mere routine, and reverence will surely never slacken!

Even so, the function of harmony and reverence is vast indeed. Expansion and stern congealing are the operations of Heaven and Earth; the alternating use of tension and relaxation is the way of King Wen and King Wu; centrality, correctness, harmony, and peace are the foundations of rites and music; preserving Supreme Harmony in union and finding ease only through untiring diligence are the sources of longevity; extending harmony to achieve the proper ordering of heaven and earth and the nourishment of all things, and maintaining devout reverence to bring peace to the world, are the ultimate reach of spiritual transformation. How could it be merely a matter of being cautious in the palace on the one hand and in the ancestral temple on the other!

If the Sacred Sovereign can truly [reading 誠 for 識] peruse the admirable instructions of past sages, follow the great counsels of the principles of governance, take as a mirror the long-term strategies for preserving prosperity, and cherish the fine plans for being prudent to the end—extending from being in the palace and in the temple to being everywhere, and extending from being able to be harmonious and reverent to being harmonious and reverent in all things, thereby showing kindness [reading 惠 for 忠] to the myriad regions and surpassing a hundred generations—then Supreme Harmony will fill…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
於宇宙至敬昭假於神人諸福之物可致
之祥莫不畢集而無疆之大歷將功與造
化侔名與天壤俱矣愚何幸躬逢其盛
第二問
李永培
同考試官教諭朱　批〔欲端士習當崇本實此孔子從〕
先進意也策中融會成章不激不靡足占樹立矣取範多士
考試官教諭王　批〔寄思深遠吐詞慷慨〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔純正雅練〕
===
夫士之成習繇上嚮也而譚者每咎夫士
乃士罔應抑或飾其科條明其賞罰峻其
防範抹其頹靡謂士當束於功令振於督
責幡然改轍惟上所使也而士又罔應此
何以故哉蓋教化風俗兩者相待上以名
繩下而惡士之嚮於實上以末驅下而惡
士之闇於本此源未澄而求其流之潔也
無是理已易名以實抹末以本使天下日
薰濡其內淬勵濯磨以嚮上意而莫知其
punctuated:
於宇宙，至敬昭假於神人，諸福之物、可致之祥，莫不畢集，而無疆之大歷，將功與造化侔，名與天壤俱矣。愚何幸躬逢其盛！

第二問
李永培
同考試官教諭朱　批〔欲端士習，當崇本實，此孔子從〕先進意也。策中融會成章，不激不靡，足占樹立矣，取範多士。
考試官教諭王　批〔寄思深遠，吐詞慷慨。〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔純正雅練。〕

夫士之成習，繇上嚮也，而譚者每咎夫士，乃士罔應。抑或飾其科條，明其賞罰，峻其防範，抹其頹靡，謂士當束於功令，振於督責，幡然改轍，惟上所使也，而士又罔應。此何以故哉？蓋教化、風俗，兩者相待。上以名繩下，而惡士之嚮於實？上以末驅下，而惡士之闇於本？此源未澄而求其流之潔也，無是理已。易名以實，抹末以本，使天下日薰濡其內，淬勵濯磨，以嚮上意，而莫知其
translation_en:
… throughout the universe, and the utmost reverence will reach clearly to spirits and mortals alike. All auspicious things and attainable omens will gather in full, and in a boundless great reign, His achievements will rival the creative forces of nature and His fame will endure as long as heaven and earth. How fortunate am I to witness this flourishing age in person!

Second Question
Li Yongpei 李永pei
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhu 朱 comments: 〔To rectify literati customs, one ought to esteem what is fundamental and substantial; this is the intent of Confucius in following〕 "those of earlier times." In this policy essay, the ideas are thoroughly integrated into a coherent composition, neither overly strident nor florid, which suffices to foretell his personal standing. Selected as a model for the many scholars.
Examiner and Instructor Wang 王 comments: 〔The thought is profound and far-reaching; the diction is impassioned and spirited.〕
Examiner and Instructor Zhao 趙 comments: 〔Pure, correct, elegant, and practiced.〕

Now, the habits formed by the literati stem from the direction set by their superiors. Yet commentators always blame the literati, and the literati do not respond. Or perhaps superiors polish the regulations, clarify rewards and punishments, tighten preventive restrictions, and redress [抹 for 捄/救?] decadent tendencies, supposing that the literati will be bound by official statutes, roused by reproof, and suddenly change their course to follow whatever their superiors command—and still the literati do not respond. Why is this so? It is because moral transformation through teaching and popular customs depend upon one another. When superiors regulate inferiors by means of outward reputation, how can the literati turn toward solid reality? When superiors drive inferiors by means of superficialities, how can the literati not be blind to the fundamental? This is to seek a pure stream when the source has not yet been cleared—there is no such principle. If one replaces reputation with reality and redresses [?] superficialities with the fundamental, causing the world daily to be steeped and nurtured within it, tempering and polishing themselves to turn toward the intentions of their superiors without knowing …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
所自起則悖本尚實之徵也故曰朝廷有
教化則士人有廉恥士人有廉恥則天下
有風俗持此以揆可與端士習矣愚請探
古昔之所以盛察近代之所以靡而後陳
變易士習之略以俟夫執事之裁擇焉蓋
語士風之盛者莫如成周當其時兔罝詠
干城而棫樸歌髦士豈不謂郅盛哉至其
所繇致是者則家塾黨庠術序國學章其
教也族黨州鄉司徒司馬重其選也
===
六計弊羣吏八柄馭羣臣嚴考課也而又
關雎麟趾以式化之鳧鷖既醉以漸涵之
士之長本實而薄聲利有以也至秦以坑
焚銷士氣而刑餘法律之徒競矣漢以罵
溺折士鋒而販繒屠狗之輩顯矣唐宋以
還古道愈邈或致用而非儒或眞儒而莫
用則當時策勳爍譽之士固亦憑技用力
自效一時而考衷度中終乏完節教化之
隆替其關於士習之美惡固若此哉
punctuated: 所自起，則悖本尚實之徵也。故曰：「朝廷有教化，則士人有廉恥；士人有廉恥，則天下有風俗。」持此以揆，可與端士習矣。愚請探古昔之所以盛，察近代之所以靡，而後陳變易士習之略，以俟夫執事之裁擇焉。蓋語士風之盛者，莫如成周。當其時，《兔罝》詠干城，而《棫樸》歌髦士，豈不謂郅盛哉！至其所繇致是者，則家塾、黨庠、術序、國學，章其教也；族、黨、州、鄉、司徒、司馬，重其選也；六計弊羣吏，八柄馭羣臣，嚴考課也。而又《關雎》、《麟趾》以式化之，《鳧鷖》、《既醉》以漸涵之，士之長本實而薄聲利，有以也。至秦以坑焚銷士氣，而刑餘、法律之徒競矣；漢以罵溺折士鋒，而販繒、屠狗之輩顯矣。唐、宋以還，古道愈邈，或致用而非儒，或眞儒而莫用。則當時策勳爍譽之士，固亦憑技用力，自效一時，而考衷度中，終乏完節。教化之隆替，其關於士習之美惡，固若此哉！
translation_en:
… whence it arises, then this will be the sign of cultivating the fundamental [reading 敦 for 悖?] and prizing substance. Therefore it is said: "When the court possesses moral transformation through instruction, scholars possess a sense of integrity and shame; when scholars possess a sense of integrity and shame, the empire possesses sound customs." Holding to this as a standard of measure, one may speak of rectifying the habits of scholars. I venture to explore why antiquity flourished and examine why recent ages have declined into decadence, and thereafter set forth an outline for transforming scholars' habits, awaiting Your Excellency's judgment and selection.

Now, if we speak of the flourishing of scholarly ethos, nothing surpassed the perfected Zhou dynasty. At that time, the ode "Rabbit Snare" (Tuju) sang of "shields and ramparts," and the ode "Dense Oaks" (Yupu) chanted of "eminent scholars"—could this not be called supreme flourishing! As for the means by which this was brought about: family schools, village schools, district academies, and the Imperial University made illustrious their instruction; the heads of clans, villages, districts, and regions, along with the Minister of Education (situ) and the Minister of War (sima), gave weight to their selection; the Six الحسابات [Six Criteria of Evaluation] assessed the multitude of lesser officials, and the Eight Handles of statecraft governed the multitude of ministers, making strict their evaluation of merit. Moreover, the spirit of the odes "Cry of the Osprey" (Guanju) and "Hoof of the Unicorn" (Linzhi) served as a model to transform them, while "Wild Ducks" (Fuyi) and "Already Drunk with Wine" (Jizui) gradually steeped and nurtured them. That scholars grew in what was fundamental and substantial while despising mere reputation and profit had its reasons indeed.

When it came to the Qin dynasty, which eroded the morale of scholars by burning books and burying scholars alive, eunuchs and legalist functionaries competed for advancement; and the Han dynasty, which blunted the spirit of scholars by cursing them and urinating into their caps, silk-peddlers and dog-butchers rose to prominence. From the Tang and Song dynasties onward, the ancient Way grew ever more distant: either men were put to practical use who were not true Confucians, or they were true Confucians who were never put to use. Thus, although the men of those times who recorded meritorious deeds and shone in renown did indeed rely on their skills and exert their strength to render service for an age, yet if one examines their inner hearts and measures their true substance, in the end they lacked spotless integrity. How closely the flourishing and decline of moral instruction is bound up with the beauty or ugliness of scholars' habits—is it not truly like this!

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
明興法周爲治首重作人如陳常敷教廣厲學
官明經計偕續食勸駕考功課最三年大
察品式備矣且永宣成治之間理道淳龐
太朴未散朝有謇諤之臣卿有不貳之老
原本端矣當其時士讓爲大夫大夫讓爲
卿有德者顯榮無德者終身沉滯而毫無
覬覦至其貞白好脩之夫特立獨行之士
崛起中夏交映後先如河東薛瑄不憚權
貴士類襟裾餘干胡居仁雅意靜恬正學
===
矩矱陳獻章抗志於江門羅倫挺節於軒
冕莊杲蔡清勢利若遺陳眞晟鄒智沖澹
自適其清風可以激頹俗其大節可以維
世教顧不偉與夫何邇年以來士習漸漓
屢廑
皇上
德意嘉納輔臣議著爲
令甲布諸學宮至備也
明詔天下士釐正文體非明
punctuated: 明興，法周爲治，首重作人。如陳常敷教，廣厲學官；明經計偕，續食勸駕；考功課最，三年大察，品式備矣。且永、宣、成、治之間，理道淳龐，太朴未散，朝有謇諤之臣，卿有不貳之老，原本端矣。當其時，士讓爲大夫，大夫讓爲卿，有德者顯榮，無德者終身沉滯而毫無覬覦。至其貞白好脩之夫、特立獨行之士，崛起中夏，交映後先。如河東薛瑄，不憚權貴，士類襟裾；餘干胡居仁，雅意靜恬，正學矩矱；陳獻章抗志於江門，羅倫挺節於軒冕；莊杲、蔡清，勢利若遺；陳眞晟、鄒智，沖澹自適。其清風可以激頹俗，其大節可以維世教，顧不偉與？夫何邇年以來，士習漸漓，屢廑皇上德意，嘉納輔臣議，著爲令甲，布諸學宮，至備也；明詔天下士釐正文體，非明
translation_en: When the Ming arose, it modeled its governance on the Zhou, placing foremost importance on the cultivation of talent. Such measures as setting forth the constant norms to spread moral instruction and broadly encouraging the school officials; sending scholars versed in the Classics along with the local fiscal delegates to the capital, providing them rations along the way and urging them to set out; and evaluating merits to grade the highest performers while conducting a Great Evaluation every three years—all these regulations and forms were complete. Moreover, during the Yongle (1403–1424), Xuande (1426–1435), Chenghua (1465–1487), and Hongzhi (1488–1505) reigns, the way of governance was pure and generous, and the great simplicity had not yet dissipated. At court there were outspoken and upright officials, and among the high ministers there were elders of undivided loyalty; the fundamental source was upright indeed. At that time, scholars yielded in becoming grand masters, and grand masters yielded in becoming high ministers. Those with virtue rose to illustrious honor, while those without virtue remained in obscurity their whole lives without the slightest covetousness. As for pure, upright men fond of self-cultivation and scholars of independent mind and singular conduct, they rose up across the central lands, shining upon one another in succession. For instance, Xue Xuan 薛瑄 of Hedong 河東 did not fear the powerful and noble, serving as a model of deportment for the scholar class; Hu Juren 胡居仁 of Yugan 餘干 cherished a disposition of quiet tranquility, serving as a standard and measure for orthodox learning; Chen Xianzhang 陳獻章 upheld his lofty aspirations at Jiangmen 江門, while Luo Lun 羅倫 stood firm in his integrity amidst high officialdom; Zhuang Gao 莊杲 and Cai Qing 蔡清 cast aside power and profit as if forgetting them; and Chen Zhensheng 陳眞晟 and Zou Zhi 鄒智 were serene, unpretentious, and content in themselves. Their pure wind could rouse decadent customs, and their great integrity could uphold the moral teachings of the age—was this not magnificent? Why is it, then, that in recent years the habits of scholars have gradually grown thin and浇薄, repeatedly troubling His Majesty’s benevolent concern? He has graciously accepted the deliberations of his Grand Secretaries, codifying them into the foremost statutes and promulgating them to the school temples—this is most comprehensive; He has issued bright proclamations to the scholars of the realm to rectify literary style, so that those who do not elucidate…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
先聖之經習
當世之法者弗錄至切也三年大察簡求卓異
之臣
褒美風厲有蕩於檢束者如法至著也士人
遘
維新之化動丕變之思卓然樹立用期無負
者亦旣蒸蒸矣而亦有不盡然者非不崇
學術也畔六藝之教而譚玄老莊舍易簡
之理而馳心縱橫則學無統矣非不能文
章也絺章繪句秖醨道眞古字奇篇罔裨
實用則文空飾矣述道必孔孟而口耳贅
疣歟猷必伊呂而施爲跛躄則曲士之竊
言也廉附巢由而蹈攫金之轍直負逢干
而甘巽牀之陋則鄙夫之稗行也以闚瞰
爲精神以向背爲通變權之所集奔如歸
市勢之旣謝去若脫遺執事所謂陽章逢
而陰騷儈獵經生之名而躬穿窬之行者
誠有之矣士風至此豈教化之不足恃耶
punctuated: 先聖之經、習當世之法者弗錄，至切也。三年大察，簡求卓異之臣，褒美風厲，有蕩於檢束者如法，至著也。士人遘維新之化，動丕變之思，卓然樹立、用期無負者，亦旣蒸蒸矣。而亦有不盡然者：非不崇學術也，畔六藝之教而譚玄老、莊，舍易簡之理而馳心縱橫，則學無統矣；非不能文章也，絺章繪句，秖醨道眞，古字奇篇，罔裨實用，則文空飾矣。述道必孔、孟而口耳贅疣，歟猷必伊、呂而施爲跛躄，則曲士之竊言也；廉附巢、由而蹈攫金之轍，直負逢、干而甘巽牀之陋，則鄙夫之稗行也。以闚瞰爲精神，以向背爲通變，權之所集，奔如歸市，勢之旣謝，去若脫遺。執事所謂「陽章逢而陰騷儈，獵經生之名而躬穿窬之行」者，誠有之矣。士風至此，豈教化之不足恃耶？
translation_en: … the Classics of the former sages and are not versed in the laws of the present age shall not be selected—this is most earnest. In the triennial great evaluation, outstanding officials are sought out and selected, praised to inspire others, while those who cast off restraint are dealt with according to the law—this is most manifest. Scholars who encounter this renewing transformation, are stirred by thoughts of great change, and stand tall to establish themselves in hopes of not failing expectations, are already flourishing in great numbers. Yet there are also those who are not entirely so: It is not that they do not esteem scholarly learning, but by rebelling against the teachings of the Six Arts to discourse on the mysteries of Laozi 老子 and Zhuangzi 莊子, and abandoning simple and easy principles to let their minds gallop after the School of Alliances and Coalitions, their learning loses its coherent thread. It is not that they are incapable of literary composition, but by embroidering chapters and painting phrases they merely dilute the truth of the Way, and with archaic characters and bizarre essays they offer no benefit to practical use, so that their writing becomes empty ornament. When discoursing on the Way they invariably invoke Confucius 孔子 and Mencius 孟子, yet it is mere ear-and-mouth excrescence; when praising [?] statesmanship they invariably cite Yi Yin 伊尹 and Lü Shang 呂尚, yet their actual deeds are lame and crippled—these are the stolen words of narrow-minded scholars. In integrity they attach themselves to Chao Fu 巢父 and Xu You 許由, yet tread in the tracks of gold-snatchers; in uprightness they claim the mantle of Guan Longfeng 關龍逢 and Bi Gan 比干, yet gladly stoop to the base obsequiousness of cringing beneath the bed—these are the petty deeds of vulgar men. They take spying for opportunity as mental vigor, and shifting allegiance as adaptability. Where power gathers, they rush as if to a marketplace; once influence fades, they abandon it as if casting off something forgotten. What Your Excellency refers to as "outwardly wearing the robes of a Confucian scholar while inwardly acting as a vulgar broker, hunting the reputation of a classicist while personally practicing the deeds of a wall-boring thief"—such men truly exist! That the ethos of the literati has come to this—could it be that moral transformation through education is insufficient to rely upon? …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
抑風厲激勸之術尚未盡耶蓋聖人貴中
行而思狂狷至無非無刺之鄉愿豈不逼
忠信而肖廉潔哉乃仲尼列諸狂狷之下
且目爲稂莠目爲鄭聲而不欲其入室豈
聖人峻絕人哉爲其似德而亂德曾不若
狂狷之志節可抑可策而入堯舜之道故
其所取不在彼而在此也孟子亦曰君子
反經而已矣經正則庶民興庶民興斯無
邪慝矣嗚呼狂狷可進經正可興則章軌
===
率士之道可知已竊嘗思起敝維風之術
大端有四一曰崇正學蓋康莊坦夷而人
趨曲徑者利其捷也吾道中正而士騖曲
學者利其便也善教者以綱常爲準身先
爲範六經爲訓周孔爲鵠舉一切空虛無
實之譚縱横捭闔之術極力屛絕而勿使
之塗耳目蠱心志士有不趨於正者否也
二曰重節義蓋商山四老迹出安劉桐江
一絲扶漢九鼎節義之士守正而不阿秉
punctuated:
抑風厲激勸之術尚未盡耶？蓋聖人貴中行而思狂狷，至無非無刺之鄉愿，豈不逼忠信而肖廉潔哉？乃仲尼列諸狂狷之下，且目爲稂莠、目爲鄭聲，而不欲其入室。豈聖人峻絕人哉？爲其似德而亂德，曾不若狂狷之志節，可抑可策而入堯舜之道，故其所取不在彼而在此也。孟子亦曰：「君子反經而已矣。經正則庶民興，庶民興斯無邪慝矣。」嗚呼！狂狷可進，經正可興，則章軌率士之道可知已。

竊嘗思起敝維風之術，大端有四：

一曰崇正學。蓋康莊坦夷，而人趨曲徑者，利其捷也；吾道中正，而士騖曲學者，利其便也。善教者以綱常爲準，身先爲範，六經爲訓，周孔爲鵠，舉一切空虛無實之譚、縱横捭闔之術，極力屛絕，而勿使之塗耳目、蠱心志，士有不趨於正者否也？

二曰重節義。蓋商山四老，迹出安劉；桐江一絲，扶漢九鼎。節義之士，守正而不阿，秉
translation_en:
…or is it that the methods of encouragement, stimulation, and exhortation have not yet been fully exhausted? Now, the Sage valued those who walk the middle way and thought fondly of the ambitiously bold (kuang) and the scrupulously cautious (juan). As for the "village worthy" (xiangyuan), in whom nothing can be found to blame or criticize, does he not closely approximate loyalty and trustworthiness, and resemble integrity and purity? Yet Confucius ranked them below the bold and the cautious, and moreover regarded them as weeds among grain and as the lascivious music of Zheng, not wishing them to enter his chamber. Was the Sage harshly cutting people off? It was because they resemble virtue while confounding virtue, and are not even equal to the aspirations and integrity of the bold and the cautious, who can be restrained or spurred on to enter the Way of Yao and Shun. Therefore, what he chose lay not with the former, but with the latter. Mencius also said: "The gentleman simply returns to the constant standard (jing). When the constant standard is rectified, the common people are roused to virtue; when the common people are roused to virtue, there will be no perverse wickedness." Alas! If the bold and the cautious can be advanced, and if rectifying the constant standard can rouse the people, then the Way to manifest the proper tracks and lead the scholars can be known!

I have privately reflected that the methods for reviving what is decadent and upholding the moral wind have four main points:

The first is to exalt orthodox learning. Now, the great thoroughfare is level and smooth, yet people hurry down crooked bypaths because they profit from their shortness; our Way is central and upright, yet scholars chase after crooked learning because they profit from its convenience. Those who are skilled at teaching take the Three Bonds and Five Constant Virtues as their standard, personal example as their model, the Six Classics as their precept, and the Duke of Zhou and Confucius as their target. They take all empty and unsubstantiated talk, and all arts of sophistry and political maneuver, and exert every effort to reject and cut them off, not allowing them to smear the ears and eyes or bewitch the mind and will. Could there then be any scholars who do not hasten toward orthodoxy?

The second is to esteem moral integrity and righteousness. Indeed, when the Four Greybeards of Mount Shang emerged, their actions secured the Liu clan; a single fishing line on the Tong River propped up the Nine Tripods of the Han. Scholars of integrity and righteousness hold to what is upright without flattering, and grasp…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
道而不回安車可致而不可屈以勢玄纁
可聘而不可餌以利可貧可賤可生可殺
而不可使爲邪故能身綱常而維世道苟
舍此不重而取其頑頓隽詬輭愞易制者
以充任使平居無事賑賑然與時浮沉保
其祿位一旦緩急固將傳舍視其官國人
視其君矣又何賴焉此節義之當重也節
義重而奔競之風息矣三曰敦禮教禮之
於人非爵非賞而可以鼓衆志不罰不刑
===
而可以禁邪僻故法施已然之後而禮禁
未然之前禮以章教教以維風將士皆純
德而敗度者無有矣故禮教不可不敦也
四曰重師傅夫有學校則有師傅師傅者
表也士者景也表端則景直表枉則景曲
理也師傅之不擇而徒取衰寠駑輩充之日
歎畢嗟窮握籌計橐無已時借令問程課
幾何訓飭幾何彼固茫然莫對也以此備
員士將衙官目之矣安望其樹模範而執
punctuated: 道而不回，安車可致而不可屈以勢，玄纁可聘而不可餌以利，可貧可賤、可生可殺，而不可使爲邪。故能身綱常而維世道。苟舍此不重，而取其頑頓隽詬、輭愞易制者以充任使，平居無事，賑賑然與時浮沉，保其祿位；一旦緩急，固將傳舍視其官，國人視其君矣，又何賴焉？此節義之當重也。節義重而奔競之風息矣。三曰敦禮教。禮之於人，非爵非賞而可以鼓衆志，不罰不刑而可以禁邪僻。故法施已然之後，而禮禁未然之前。禮以章教，教以維風，將士皆純德，而敗度者無有矣。故禮教不可不敦也。四曰重師傅。夫有學校則有師傅。師傅者，表也；士者，景也。表端則景直，表枉則景曲，理也。師傅之不擇，而徒取衰寠駑輩充之，日歎畢嗟窮，握籌計橐無已時。借令問程課幾何、訓飭幾何，彼固茫然莫對也。以此備員，士將衙官目之矣，安望其樹模範而執
translation_en:
… to the Way without wavering. They may be summoned with a comfortable carriage, yet cannot be bent by power; they may be invited with black and crimson silks, yet cannot be baited by profit. They may be made poor or lowly, kept alive or put to death, yet cannot be made to do evil. Therefore they are able to embody the cardinal principles and sustain the moral order of the world. If we cast such men aside without esteeming them, and instead select obtuse, shameless, weak, and timid men who are easy to control to fill offices and commissions, in ordinary times of peace they will complacently drift with the current to preserve their emoluments and positions; once an emergency arises, they will surely regard their offices as mere post-station lodgings and view their ruler as a stranger—what reliance can be placed on them? This is why integrity and righteousness must be esteemed. When integrity and righteousness are esteemed, the custom of scrambling for advancement will cease.

The third is to cultivate ritual teaching. What ritual is to people is neither rank nor reward, yet it can rouse the will of the multitude; it is neither fine nor punishment, yet it can prohibit depravity and perversity. Thus, law is applied after a deed is done, whereas ritual prohibits it before it happens. When ritual illuminates teaching, and teaching sustains customs, scholars will all be of pure virtue, and there will be none who violate the moral norms. Therefore, ritual teaching must be cultivated.

The fourth is to esteem instructors. Where there are schools, there are instructors. The instructor is the gnomon; the scholar is the shadow. When the gnomon is upright, the shadow is straight; when the gnomon is crooked, the shadow is bent—this is natural principle. If instructors are not carefully selected, and we merely take decrepit, impoverished, and mediocre men to fill the posts, they will spend their days sighing over their destitution [? 歎畢嗟窮], clutching counting rods and calculating their purses without end. Suppose one were to ask how many graded exercises they have assigned or how much instruction and admonition they have given—they would certainly be at a loss and unable to reply. When posts are filled with such men, scholars will look upon them as mere petty functionaries; how can one hope for them to establish a model and hold fast to…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
章逢也此非所以令士類化也惟今銓
除掌教取諸乙榜而勿徒以衰篤尸位則
士有矜式而不敢自底頹僻此又一術也
脩此四者而又飭庠序之規嚴選舉之法
嚴考課之典使士人日範於禮度而饜飫
乎道真充其所至上之可以立德次之可
以立功下之可以立言將遠紹成周近淑
先進而矜詡藻績之習舉不足累之矣雖
然有造士者有士之所以自造者商俗披
靡無染於採薇晉俗清譚無改於運甓彼
其中素定也士能燭義利之辨鏡内外之
分無眩實以名無移本以末而持之以固
居之以恒舉富貴利達而無一足介其中
則執事所謂不溷於俗皭然物表者在我
矣蓋昔者墨子見素絲而悲曰入乎黃而
黃也入乎蒼而蒼也於乎物繇染異爲上
者愼勿爲習俗染哉
===
第三問
punctuated:
章逢也？此非所以令士類化也。惟今銓除掌教，取諸乙榜，而勿徒以衰篤尸位，則士有矜式，而不敢自底頹僻，此又一術也。脩此四者，而又飭庠序之規，嚴選舉之法，嚴考課之典，使士人日範於禮度，而饜飫乎道真。充其所至，上之可以立德，次之可以立功，下之可以立言，將遠紹成周，近淑先進，而矜詡藻績之習，舉不足累之矣。雖然，有造士者，有士之所以自造者。商俗披靡，無染於採薇；晉俗清譚，無改於運甓，彼其中素定也。士能燭義利之辨，鏡内外之分，無眩實以名，無移本以末，而持之以固，居之以恒，舉富貴利達，而無一足介其中，則執事所謂不溷於俗、皭然物表者，在我矣。蓋昔者墨子見素絲而悲，曰：「入乎黃而黃也，入乎蒼而蒼也。」於乎！物繇染異，爲上者愼勿爲習俗染哉！

第三問
translation_en:
… guide those who wear the scholar's cap and robes? This is not the way to bring about the transformation of the scholarly class. Only if present appointments of directors of studies are drawn from the supplementary list of the Metropolitan Examination (yibang) and the posts are not merely filled as sinecures by the decrepit and infirm, will scholars have models to revere and emulate and not dare sink into decadence and perversity. This is yet another method.

By cultivating these four measures—and furthermore tightening the regulations of the schools, strictly enforcing the laws of selection and recommendation, and rigorously implementing the statutes of evaluation—scholars will daily be molded by ritual and standards and thoroughly steeped in the truth of the Way. Carried to the fullest extent, at the highest level they will be able to establish virtue, at the next level establish meritorious service, and at the lowest level establish enduring words. They will inherit the traditions of the flourishing Zhou in the distant past and pattern themselves after the worthies of earlier generations in recent times, and the habits of boasting and ornate embellishment will all be powerless to encumber them.

Even so, there is that by which scholars are molded by others, and there is that by which scholars mold themselves. The customs of the Shang were decadent, yet they did not taint those who gathered薇 (ferns) on Mount Shouyang; the customs of the Jin were given over to "pure conversation" (qingtan), yet they did not alter the resolve of him who carried bricks for exercise—because what lay within them was already firmly settled. If a scholar can illuminate the distinction between righteousness and profit, clearly perceive the division between the internal and the external, neither confusing reality with reputation nor displacing the fundamental with the incidental, holding fast to this with firmness and dwelling in it with constancy so that among wealth, honor, profit, and advancement not a single thing is sufficient to disturb his mind, then what Your Excellency calls "not being muddied by vulgar customs and standing dazzlingly pure above the material world" will rest within ourselves. For in antiquity Mozi (墨子) wept upon seeingundyed silk, saying, "Put into yellow dye, it becomes yellow; put into blue dye, it becomes blue." Alas! Things become different through what dyes them—let those who aspire to the highest [or: "those above," reading 上 as 士/上] take heed not to be stained by prevailing customs!

Question Three

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
苗希益
〔評三晉人物而以才節學斷之識其大矣非士國譽髦耶〕
同考試官教諭莊　批
考試官教諭趙　批〔品隲精當具見學識〕
考試官教諭王　批〔雅調藻辭〕
古之人樹休當時蜚聲後世顧不易哉必
有高天下之節而後可以貞遇必有超天
下之才而後可以成能夫遇之不齊雖聖
人不能違也而守之不渝則志士所自樹
===
也是故重節至於廓清宇宙懋一代之丕
績玄覽古今勒一家之名言自非卓犖瑰
瑋之士未易能焉是故重才才與節合上
也各得其性之所近次也就二者而權之
則節尤急焉執是以尚論古人蓋莫有邀
情矣且古今生人多矣其卓然而表見著
惟才與節然有其節矣不兼之以才爲曲
之節也有其才矣不基之以節藻繢之才
也有節與才矣而非原於聖人中正之道
punctuated:
苗希益
〔評三晉人物，而以才、節、學斷之，識其大矣，非士國譽髦耶？〕同考試官教諭莊　批
考試官教諭趙　批〔品隲精當，具見學識。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔雅調藻辭。〕

古之人樹休當時，蜚聲後世，顧不易哉！必有高天下之節，而後可以貞遇；必有超天下之才，而後可以成能。夫遇之不齊，雖聖人不能違也；而守之不渝，則志士所自樹也，是故重節。至於廓清宇宙，懋一代之丕績；玄覽古今，勒一家之名言，自非卓犖瑰瑋之士，未易能焉，是故重才。才與節合，上也；各得其性之所近，次也。就二者而權之，則節尤急焉。執是以尚論古人，蓋莫有邀情矣。且古今生人多矣，其卓然而表見著，惟才與節。然有其節矣，不兼之以才，爲曲之節也；有其才矣，不基之以節，藻繢之才也。有節與才矣，而非原於聖人中正之道，
translation_en:
Miao Xiyi 苗希益
[Evaluating the eminent figures of the Three Jin (San Jin 三晉, i.e., Shanxi) and judging them by talent, integrity, and learning—he grasps what is fundamental! Is he not a celebrated talent of the state's scholars [? 士國 -> 王國]?] Comment by Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhuang 莊.
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Zhao 趙: [His critical appraisals are precise and apt, fully demonstrating his learning and insight.]
Comment by Examiner, Instructor Wang 王: [Refined tone and ornate diction.]

For the men of antiquity to establish glorious achievements in their own time and make their renown resound through later generations—surely this was no easy matter! One must possess integrity that towers above the world before one can hold firm in one's circumstances; one must possess talent that surpasses the world before one can bring one's abilities to fulfillment. Now, the unevenness of one's circumstances is something even a sage cannot evade; yet maintaining one's principles without wavering is what a man of high aspiration establishes for himself—for this reason, integrity is prized. As for sweeping clear the universe and achieving the great merit of an entire era, or peering deeply into antiquity and the present and inscribing the famous words of an independent school of thought—unless one is an extraordinary and magnificent scholar, one cannot easily accomplish this—for this reason, talent is prized. The union of talent and integrity is highest; attaining whichever is closer to one's nature comes next. If we weigh the two against each other, integrity is even more urgent. If one holds fast to this standard in evaluating the men of antiquity, none will be able to disguise their true character [? 邀情 -> 遁情]. Moreover, numerous indeed are the people who have lived in ancient and modern times, yet those who have stood out prominently and manifested themselves with distinction have done so solely through talent and integrity. Even so, if one possesses integrity without combining it with talent, it is the integrity of a narrow, one-sided sort [? 爲曲 -> 偏曲 / 鄉曲]; if one possesses talent without grounding it in integrity, it is the talent of mere ornamental embellishment. And if one possesses both integrity and talent, yet they do not spring from the impartial and upright Way of the sages, …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
則所謂節義事功文章者或未免於偏倚
駁雜之弊噫由聖人之道以善用其節與
才非遼於學者其孰能之今夫太虛不能
無氣氣不能不聚而爲萬物天地之正氣
孟子與氏之所謂浩然者也在天爲日星
在地爲河嶽在物爲鳳麟在人爲俊傑而
道德有諸身則節義事功文章出焉其品
不同以言其鍾天地之正氣則均也唐虞
三代之世風氣醇凝君臣道合不斳於工
===
文也而言立焉不斳於抗節也而節仰焉
不斳於立功也而功見焉卽道德性命之
微矣謨吐訓渾渾噩噩謂之文章可也卽
吁咈儆戒未嘗苟同謂之節義可也卽嘉
言之底績九德之采采謂之事功可也若
后稷以播穀垂勛龍逢以批鱗抗節傅說
以納誨沃心非三胥之産而皐夔伊周之
儔哉然亦自其所謂道德者發之爲節義
爲事功爲文章欲據其迹而析言之亦淺
punctuated: 則所謂節義、事功、文章者，或未免於偏倚駁雜之弊。噫！由聖人之道以善用其節與才，非遼於學者，其孰能之？今夫太虛不能無氣，氣不能不聚而爲萬物。天地之正氣，孟子與氏之所謂浩然者也。在天爲日星，在地爲河嶽，在物爲鳳麟，在人爲俊傑。而道德有諸身，則節義、事功、文章出焉。其品不同，以言其鍾天地之正氣，則均也。唐、虞、三代之世，風氣醇凝，君臣道合，不斳於工文也，而言立焉；不斳於抗節也，而節仰焉；不斳於立功也，而功見焉。卽道德性命之微，矣謨吐訓，渾渾噩噩，謂之文章可也；卽吁咈儆戒，未嘗苟同，謂之節義可也；卽嘉言之底績，九德之采采，謂之事功可也。若后稷以播穀垂勛，龍逢以批鱗抗節，傅說以納誨沃心，非三胥之産，而皐、夔、伊、周之儔哉？然亦自其所謂道德者，發之爲節義、爲事功、爲文章，欲據其迹而析言之，亦淺…
translation_en: …then what are called moral integrity, practical achievement, and literary composition may not avoid the flaws of bias and impurity. Alas! To follow the Way of the Sages so as to make good use of one's integrity and talent—who could do this unless they are profound in learning [reading 遼 as 邃]? Now, the Great Void cannot be without vital energy (qi), and vital energy cannot but gather to form the myriad things. The upright energy of Heaven and Earth is what Mencius (Meng Ziyushi [?; 孟子輿氏]) called the "flood-like" (haoran) energy. In Heaven it is the sun and stars; on Earth it is the rivers and sacred peaks; among creatures it is the phoenix and unicorn; among humans it is the outstanding heroes. When the Way and its Virtue are possessed within oneself, moral integrity, practical achievement, and literary composition issue forth from them. Though their manifestations differ, in terms of being endowed with the upright energy of Heaven and Earth, they are all the same. In the eras of Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties, customs and ethos were pure and solid, and rulers and ministers were united in the Way. They did not seek [reading 斳 as 蘄] to be skillful in literary composition, yet their words stood firm; they did not seek to exalt their integrity, yet their integrity was looked up to; they did not seek to establish achievements, yet their achievements were manifest. Even in the subtleties of the Way, Virtue, human nature, and destiny, when they set forth counsels and uttered instructions [?; 矣謨吐訓, reading 矣 as 矢], vast and unadorned, one could call this literary composition; when they voiced disapproval and admonition, never carelessly agreeing, one could call this moral integrity; when fine words were brought to fruition and the nine virtues were practiced in their affairs, one could call this practical achievement. Take Hou Ji, who handed down merit by sowing grain; Guan Longfeng, who upheld integrity by braving the dragon's scales; and Fu Yue, who enriched the ruler's heart by offering instruction—were they not born of the Three Jin (San Jin [?; 三胥, for 三晉]) and the peers of Gao Yao, Kui, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou? Yet these too issued forth from what is called the Way and its Virtue to become moral integrity, practical achievement, and literary composition. To wish to separate and speak of them merely on the basis of their outward traces is indeed a shallow…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
之乎尚論也已三代以還聖遠言湮風會
日下自夫人易久要於死生之際而計聲
利於尺寸之間僞作符命競陳功德於是
乎以身徇主以隱遺榮者出而節義名矣
自夫人以清譚廢國事以覆交博虛聲首
鼠兩端無當世用於是乎決策畊主排難
解紛者出而事功名矣自夫人之本彊椎
魯不學少文藉口於篆刻諱短於玄虛於
是乎屬書摛詞投藻揚芬者出而文章名
===
矣其在晉中太行河汾之所炳靈卽大鹵
之金鑛產之秉海內稱雄焉矧地靈人傑
久而愈盛者乎姑就執事所問者而折衷
之竭股肱之力而繼之以死使死者復生
生者不愧荀息所以報晉獻公也隱綿山
之上而焚林抱樹恥貪天功以爲巳力介
之推所以報晉文公也全袴中之兒而視
死如歸不以十五年而寒其盟程嬰所以
報趙朔也如以其迹均可以愧人臣之懷
punctuated: 之乎尚論也已。三代以還，聖遠言湮，風會日下。自夫人易久要於死生之際，而計聲利於尺寸之間，僞作符命，競陳功德，於是乎以身徇主、以隱遺榮者出，而節義名矣；自夫人以清譚廢國事，以覆交博虛聲，首鼠兩端，無當世用，於是乎決策畊主、排難解紛者出，而事功名矣；自夫人之本彊椎魯，不學少文，藉口於篆刻，諱短於玄虛，於是乎屬書摛詞、投藻揚芬者出，而文章名矣。其在晉中，太行、河、汾之所炳靈，卽大鹵之金、鑛產之秉，海內稱雄焉，矧地靈人傑，久而愈盛者乎？姑就執事所問者而折衷之：竭股肱之力，而繼之以死，使死者復生，生者不愧，荀息所以報晉獻公也；隱綿山之上，而焚林抱樹，恥貪天功以爲巳力，介之推所以報晉文公也；全袴中之兒，而視死如歸，不以十五年而寒其盟，程嬰所以報趙朔也。如以其迹，均可以愧人臣之懷
translation_en:
…in evaluating the ancients! Since the Three Dynasties, the sages have grown distant and their words have been obscured, while prevailing customs have declined day by day. Ever since people began breaking lifelong promises at the brink of life and death, calculating fame and profit down to the inch, forging auspicious mandates, and vying to proclaim merits and virtues, there emerged those who sacrificed their lives for their lords or cast aside glory by going into reclusion—and thus integrity and righteousness (jieyi) acquired a distinct name. Ever since people began neglecting affairs of state through "pure conversation" (qingtan), courting empty reputation through fickle associations, hesitating like a rat looking both ways, and proving useless to the world, there emerged those who formulated strategies to assist [?] their lords and resolved crises and entanglements—and thus practical achievement (shigong) acquired a distinct name. Ever since people who were by nature wooden, blunt, unlearned, and lacking in refinement began excusing themselves by dismissing writing as mere "seal-carving" or hiding their shortcomings behind abstruse emptiness, there emerged those who composed books, set forth phrases, cast forth florid prose, and spread fragrant renown—and thus literary composition (wenzhang) acquired a distinct name.

Here in the Jin region [Shanxi], made illustrious by the numinousvitality of the Taihang Mountains and the Yellow and Fen Rivers, even the salt of Dalu and the abundance of mineral resources are acclaimed as preeminent within the seas; how much more so its numinous terrain and outstanding men, which have only flourished the more with the passage of time! Let me tentatively take up the examples raised by Your Excellency and weigh them carefully: To exhaust the strength of one's limbs and follow it with death, so that "if the dead were to come back to life, the living would feel no shame"—this was how Xun Xi 荀息 repaid Duke Xian of Jin 晉獻公. To hide atop Mount Mian and clasp a tree as the forest burned, scorning to steal the credit of Heaven and claim it as his own effort—this was how Jie Zhitui 介之推 repaid Duke Wen of Jin 晉文公. To preserve the infant hidden in the trousers and regard death as returning home, not letting the passage of fifteen years chill his oath—this was how Cheng Ying 程嬰 repaid Zhao Shuo 趙朔. Judged by their outward deeds, all of them are enough to put to shame ministers who harbor…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
二心者矣然士固有一死或重於太山或
輕於鴻毛推之從難嬰之立孤業已成天
下士矣揆以聖人之道可以無死也死不
傷勇予若獻公逐申生而立奚齊息不以
正折之而徒以死殉之是其死輕於鴻毛
與之推程嬰尤不可同日論矣文侯造館
之日而鴻飛冥冥卒寢兵於强秦段干木
之行也燕雀駢首之朝而鳳翔千仞不愧
碑於中郎郭泰之行也獻策不用之後而
===
退隱河汾益見多於朱程王通之行也之
三子者蟬蛻囂埃之中自致寰區之外其
節可謂同矣然聖人之道非徒獨善其身
已也文侯以客禮遇干木迫斯可以見矣
踰垣而避之非聖道之中也泰有澄清之
志而非其時遂明哲以保其身雖收斂未
盡而志潔行廉庶幾有冉閔之風焉通擬
經不能無僭然多後人傅會之語至其中
說發明王道蓋誠有足多者故程子以隱
punctuated:
二心者矣。然士固有一死，或重於太山，或輕於鴻毛。推之從難，嬰之立孤，業已成天下士矣；揆以聖人之道，可以無死也，死不傷勇予？若獻公逐申生而立奚齊，息不以正折之，而徒以死殉之，是其死輕於鴻毛，與之推、程嬰尤不可同日論矣。

文侯造館之日，而鴻飛冥冥，卒寢兵於强秦，段干木之行也；燕雀駢首之朝，而鳳翔千仞，不愧碑於中郎，郭泰之行也；獻策不用之後，而退隱河汾，益見多於朱、程，王通之行也。之三子者，蟬蛻囂埃之中，自致寰區之外，其節可謂同矣。然聖人之道，非徒獨善其身已也。文侯以客禮遇干木，迫斯可以見矣，踰垣而避之，非聖道之中也。泰有澄清之志，而非其時，遂明哲以保其身，雖收斂未盡，而志潔行廉，庶幾有冉、閔之風焉。通擬經不能無僭，然多後人傅會之語；至其《中說》發明王道，蓋誠有足多者，故程子以隱…
translation_en:
… duplicitous hearts. Yet although a gentleman certainly has but one death to die, it may be heavier than Mount Tai or lighter than a swan's down. By following his lord through hardship, Jie Zhitui, and by establishing the orphan, Cheng Ying, had already proven themselves gentlemen of the realm. Measured against the Way of the Sages, they did not need to die—did their deaths not injure the principle of true courage [reading 予 as 乎]? As for Duke Xian driving out Shensheng and establishing Xiqi as heir, Xun Xi did not rebuke him with what was right, but merely followed him in death; thus his death was lighter than a swan's down, and can even less be mentioned in the same breath as those of Jie Zhitui and Cheng Ying.

When Marquis Wen visited his lodging, he soared away like a wild goose into the distant heavens, yet ultimately caused mighty Qin to call off its troops—such was the conduct of Duan Ganmu 段干木. At a court where swallows and sparrows craned their necks together, he soared like a phoenix to a thousand fathoms, proving worthy of the stele inscription by the Gentleman of the Interior (Cai Yong 蔡邕)—such was the conduct of Guo Tai 郭泰. After presenting strategies that were not adopted, he retired into seclusion between the Yellow and Fen rivers, winning ever greater praise from Zhu Xi 朱熹 and the Cheng brothers (Cheng Hao 程顥 and Cheng Yi 程頤)—such was the conduct of Wang Tong 王通. These three gentlemen shed the noisy dust of the world like cicadas and placed themselves beyond the bounds of the mortal realm; their integrity may be called the same. Yet the Way of the Sages is not merely a matter of cultivating one's own person in solitude. Marquis Wen treated Duan Ganmu with the courtesy due a guest; when pressed so earnestly, he could well have granted an audience, and climbing over a wall to avoid him fell short of the mean of the Sage's Way. Guo Tai possessed the ambition to cleanse and bring order to the world, but seeing it was not the right time, he exercised wise discernment to preserve his person; although his self-restraint was not yet complete, his aspirations were pure and his conduct incorrupt, nearly approaching the spirit of Ran Min (Ran Yong 冉雍 and Min Sun 閔損). In imitating the Classics, Wang Tong could not avoid the charge of presumption, though much of that consisted of words spuriously attached by later followers; as for his Discourses on the Mean (Zhongshuo 中說) elucidating the Kingly Way, there is truly much in it worthy of praise, which is why Master Cheng referred to him as a "gentleman in…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
君子稱之方之於泰亦無軒輊蓋二子之
才均裨世用若著述之弘通視泰爲猶賢
矣受遺秉政竟垂勛於麟閣非霍宣成乎
夏周爲唐獨取日於虞淵非狄梁公乎入
相宋室能寢謀於强虜非司馬溫公乎溫
公以文章名世而以忠義自結人主方神
哲兩朝可謂多故矣乃理財變法之議不
依阿濮邸以中執政之驩而與公著同心
輔治新法之蠹剔除殆盡固三晉人物之
===
冠冕也梁公以不激不隨之身徊翔女主
之朝卒能不危其身以濟其君非有超世
之才者不能質之溫公亦有光焉宣城擁
昭立宣始元地節之間漢祚危而復安者
光之伐也然不講於公孫顧膚之義用舍
進退輒以自便秉之迹其人品其在梁公
之下乎命世良史之才見稱劉向非司馬
遷乎落霞秋水之句推重南州非王勃乎
王珮瓊琚之文並美昌黎非柳宗元乎茲
punctuated:
君子稱之，方之於泰，亦無軒輊。蓋二子之才，均裨世用；若著述之弘，通視泰爲猶賢矣。
受遺秉政，竟垂勛於麟閣，非霍宣成乎？夏周爲唐，獨取日於虞淵，非狄梁公乎？入相宋室，能寢謀於强虜，非司馬溫公乎？溫公以文章名世，而以忠義自結人主。方神、哲兩朝，可謂多故矣，乃理財變法之議，不依阿濮邸，以中執政之驩；而與公著同心輔治，新法之蠹，剔除殆盡，固三晉人物之冠冕也。梁公以不激不隨之身，徊翔女主之朝，卒能不危其身以濟其君，非有超世之才者不能，質之溫公，亦有光焉。宣城擁昭立宣，始元、地節之間，漢祚危而復安者，光之伐也。然不講於公孫碩膚之義，用舍進退，輒以自便秉之。迹其人品，其在梁公之下乎！
命世良史之才，見稱劉向，非司馬遷乎？落霞秋水之句，推重南州，非王勃乎？玉珮瓊琚之文，並美昌黎，非柳宗元乎？茲
translation_en:
… gentleman.” Compared with Guo Tai 郭泰, neither is superior or inferior to the other. Indeed, the talents of both men were equally beneficial to the world; yet in the breadth of his writings, Wang Tong 王通 may be regarded as even worthier than Guo Tai.

Receiving the testamentary charge to hold the reins of government, and ultimately leaving his meritorious name in the Unicorn Pavilion (Lingge 麟閣)—was this not Huo Xuancheng 霍宣成 (Huo Guang 霍光, Marquis Xuancheng)? Transforming the Wu-Zhou 周 back into the Tang 唐, single-handedly retrieving the sun from the Abyss of Yu (Yuyuan 虞淵)—was this not Duke Liang of Di, Di Lianggong 狄梁公 (Di Renjie 狄仁傑)? Entering the court as Grand Councilor to the House of Song 宋, able to make powerful northern foes abandon their schemes—was this not Duke Wen of Sima, Sima Wengong 司馬溫公 (Sima Guang 司馬光)? Duke Wen was renowned in his generation for his literary writings, and bound himself to his sovereign through loyalty and rectitude. During the two reigns of Shenzong 神宗 and Zhezong 哲宗, the state could truly be called troubled by many crises. Yet in the debates over fiscal administration and institutional reform, and in refusing to flatter or pander in the matter of the Prince of Pu's 濮邸 title so as to curry favor with the chief ministers, he instead worked with Lü Gongzhu 呂公著 in shared devotion to assist in governance, eradicating almost completely the pernicious abuses of the New Policies (Xinfa 新法). Truly he is the crowning glory among the figures of the Three Jin (Sanjin 三晉, i.e., Shanxi)! Duke Liang, conducting himself in a manner neither rashly confrontational nor slavishly compliant, maneuvered through the court of a female ruler (Empress Wu Zetian 武則天), and in the end was able to rescue his sovereign without endangering his own person. None without transcendent talent could have achieved this; measured alongside Duke Wen, he too shines brightly. Marquis Xuancheng [written 宣城] upheld Emperor Zhao 昭帝 and enthroned Emperor Xuan 宣帝; between the Shiyuan 始元 (86–80 BCE) and Dijie 地節 (69–66 BCE) eras, that the fortune of the Han 漢 dynasty was imperiled and yet restored to stability was due to Huo Guang's meritorious achievement. However, he did not study the principle of the Duke of Zhou's humble and magnanimous yielding of power ("the Duke's grandson, of great and admirable composure," *Book of Odes* [公孫碩膚, misprinted as 公孫顧膚]); in appointing and dismissing, advancing and retiring officials, he always acted at his own convenience. Judging his personal character by his deeds, does he not rank below Duke Liang?

Possessing the talent of a great historian of the age, praised as such by Liu Xiang 劉向—was this not Sima Qian 司馬遷? Composing the lines on "setting rosy clouds and autumn waters" (*Preface to the Pavilion of Prince Teng*), esteemed throughout the southern regions—was this not Wang Bo 王勃? Writing prose like "jade pendants and gem-set girdle ornaments" [玉珮瓊琚, with 玉 printed as 王], matched in beauty with Han Yu 韓愈 (Han Changli 昌黎)—was this not Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元? These …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
皆勸成一家之言以俟後之君子者也然
器識未定勃來行儉之譏始進不重元附
叔文之黨則亦文人而已惟梓人橐駝傳
是足爲相天子牧斯民者法吾於柳州猶
有取焉馬遷發憤爲史使上下數千餘年
之事較如指掌亦已勤矣且其辯而不華
質而不俚褒然今古詞宗雖以敎陵賈禍
而不失爲友生急難之誼據其文品其在
柳之先乎是數君子者或以節義或以事
===
功或以文章均之爲晉傑矣然士君子非
節與才之難而善用之爲難故道德者所
以善其才與節者也要之係於學矣夫㮣
相豫章世之巨材也惟隆固挺直然後足
以供清廟明堂之需垂綏瑰琰世之美玉
也惟潤澤而栗然後足以勝圭璋瑚璉之
用節與才亦士之美也而非原於道德寧
能免於偏倚駁雜之弊乎哉甚矣學之不
可以已也故荀息推嬰節矣而不可以言
punctuated: 皆勸成一家之言，以俟後之君子者也。然器識未定，勃來行儉之譏；始進不重，元附叔文之黨，則亦文人而已。惟《梓人》、《橐駝》傳，是足爲相天子、牧斯民者法，吾於柳州猶有取焉。馬遷發憤爲史，使上下數千餘年之事較如指掌，亦已勤矣。且其辯而不華，質而不俚，褒然今古詞宗。雖以敎陵賈禍，而不失爲友生急難之誼。據其文品，其在柳之先乎？是數君子者，或以節義，或以事功，或以文章，均之爲晉傑矣。然士君子非節與才之難，而善用之爲難。故道德者，所以善其才與節者也；要之，係於學矣。夫㮣相、豫章，世之巨材也，惟隆固挺直，然後足以供清廟、明堂之需；垂綏、瑰琰，世之美玉也，惟潤澤而栗，然後足以勝圭璋、瑚璉之用。節與才，亦士之美也，而非原於道德，寧能免於偏倚駁雜之弊乎哉？甚矣，學之不可以已也！故荀息、推、嬰節矣，而不可以言
translation_en:
…all strove [?] to establish an independent school of thought to await gentlemen of later generations. However, with his vessel and discernment not yet settled, Wang Bo drew the criticism of Pei Xingjian 裴行儉; and lacking gravity at the start of his career, Liu Zongyuan attached himself to the faction of Wang Shuwen 王叔文—so they were merely men of letters. Only the biographies of the Master Carpenter (Ziren zhuan) and the Camel-Back Planter (Tuotuo zhuan) are sufficient to serve as models for assisting the Son of Heaven and shepherding the people; thus in Liu Zongyuan (Liuzhou 柳州) I still find something worth adopting. Sima Qian, spurred by indignation to write history, made the events of several thousand years past and present as clear as pointing to one's palm—he was diligent indeed. Moreover, his style is eloquent yet not flashy, unadorned yet not vulgar, standing preeminent as a master of prose past and present. Although he brought disaster upon himself by speaking up for [? 敎, likely a misprint for 救, saving] Li Ling 李陵, he did not fail in the righteousness of aiding a friend in distress. Judging both his writing and his character, does he not rank ahead of Liu Zongyuan?

These several gentlemen, whether through integrity and righteousness, through accomplishments in statecraft, or through literary compositions, were all alike outstanding heroes of Jin 晉 (Shanxi). Yet for a scholar-gentleman, it is not possessing integrity and talent that is difficult, but using them well that is difficult. Therefore, morality and the Way are the means by which one makes good use of one's talent and integrity; in essence, this depends upon learning. Now, giant timber [? 㮣相] and camphorwood (yuzhang 豫章) are the great woods of the world, yet only when they are stout, firm, and straight are they sufficient to supply the needs of the Ancestral Temple and the Mingtang 明堂 (Hall of Light); Chuiji [? 垂綏, for 垂棘] and precious gems (guiyan 瑰琰) are the fine jades of the world, yet only when they are lustrous and dense are they sufficient to bear the uses of ceremonial tablets (guizhang 圭璋) and sacrificial vessels (hulian 瑚璉). Integrity and talent are likewise the fine qualities of a scholar, yet if they do not spring from morality and the Way, how can they avoid the flaws of bias and impurity? Great indeed is the necessity that learning must never cease! Thus Xun Xi 荀息, Jie Zhitui 介之推, and Gongsun Chujiu 公孫杵臼 [and Cheng Ying 程嬰] possessed integrity, yet one cannot speak of them as…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
中馬遷王柳才矣而不可以言節均之乎
未聞道也王郭千木庶幾近道矣而事業
未著宣成庶幾立功矣而學術未優以梁
公之才而大節弗純朱子於綱目示貶焉
若夫濟之以節兼之以才其在朝也走卒
知名有寄謝司馬丞相無去朝廷之言其
入朝也遼人敕其邊吏有中國相司馬無
生邊事之語是學本於誠一而以中正之
道運其才節庶幾乎稷說龍逢者惟溫公
===
乎雖然策樹鴻勛以垂方來者古人之懿
範也鏡別羣材以定取舍者尚論之權衡
也是皆三代以下之人物也遡此而上龍
逢之忠烈矣然愿爲良臣毋爲忠臣古大
臣之用心固如此九原可作其惟稷與傅
說乎蓋其凝祥毓秀氣得中和懋學潛心
養歸純粹不得其時爲耒舉之相爲巖野
之耕節高天下而不必於仕也得時而駕
爲播穀之臣爲沃心之相才超天下而不
punctuated: 中；馬遷、王、柳才矣，而不可以言節；均之乎未聞道也。王、郭、千木庶幾近道矣，而事業未著；宣、成庶幾立功矣，而學術未優。以梁公之才，而大節弗純，朱子於《綱目》示貶焉。若夫濟之以節，兼之以才，其在朝也，走卒知名，有「寄謝司馬丞相無去朝廷」之言；其入朝也，遼人敕其邊吏，有「中國相司馬，無生邊事」之語。是學本於誠一，而以中正之道運其才節，庶幾乎稷、說、龍逢者，惟溫公乎！雖然，策樹鴻勛以垂方來者，古人之懿範也；鏡別羣材以定取舍者，尚論之權衡也。是皆三代以下之人物也。遡此而上，龍逢之忠，烈矣；然愿爲良臣，毋爲忠臣，古大臣之用心固如此。九原可作，其惟稷與傅說乎！蓋其凝祥毓秀，氣得中和，懋學潛心，養歸純粹。不得其時，爲耒舉之相，爲巖野之耕，節高天下而不必於仕也；得時而駕，爲播穀之臣，爲沃心之相，才超天下而不
translation_en: … the mean; Sima Qian 司馬遷, Wang Tong 王通, and Liu Zongyuan 柳宗元 possessed talent, yet one cannot speak of them as having integrity; all of them alike had not heard the Way. Wang Tong, Guo Tai 郭泰, and Duanmu Ci (Zixia) or Duangan Mu 段干木 came close to the Way, yet their achievements were not manifest; Emperor Xuan 宣 and Emperor Cheng 成 [or the generals under them, such as霍光 Huo Guang and 衛青 Wei Qing / 霍去病 Huo Qubing] nearly established meritorious deeds, yet their scholarly learning was not superior. Even with the talent of the Duke of Liang (Di Renjie 狄仁傑), because his fundamental integrity was not pure, Master Zhu (Zhu Xi 朱熹) indicated censure of him in the Outline and Details of the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian gangmu 通鑑綱目). As for one who aided his actions with integrity and combined it with talent: when he was at court, even running footmen knew his name, and there was the saying, "Send word to thank Grand Councilor Sima (Sima Guang 司馬光), do not leave the court"; when he entered the court, the Liao people instructed their border officials with the words, "China has made Sima its Chief Councilor; do not stir up trouble on the frontier." Thus, whose learning was rooted in sincere unity and who wielded his talent and integrity through the Way of centrality and correctness, coming close to Hou Ji 后稷, Fu Yue 傅說, and Guan Longfeng 關龍逢—was it not the Duke of Wen (Sima Guang) alone! Even so, planning and establishing great merit to hand down to the future is the admirable model of the ancients; mirroring and distinguishing the multitude of talents to determine whom to choose and whom to reject is the balance scale of evaluating historical figures. These are all figures from the Three Dynasties and later. Tracing back before this, the loyalty of Guan Longfeng was ardent indeed; yet wishing to be a good minister rather than a loyal martyr—such was truly the intention of the great ministers of antiquity. If the dead could be raised from the Nine Springs, would our models not be Hou Ji and Fu Yue alone! For they crystallized auspiciousness and nurtured excellence, their vital energy attaining equilibrium and harmony; they strove in learning and immersed their minds, their cultivation returning to pure essence. When they did not meet their time, they were ministers raised from the plow or farmers in the craggy wilds, their integrity towering above the world without insisting upon taking office; when they met their time and rode forth, they became the minister who sowed the hundred grains and the chief councilor who enriched the ruler's heart, their talent surpassing the world without…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
必於隱也自蒸民乃粒格於皇天可以言
事功與夔契伊周齊驅矣自益稷之篇說
命之篇渾渾灝灝可以言文章與皐謨伊
訓竝駕矣乃稷自爲兒時屹如巨人之志
與說之終始典學遜志時敏又皆致道德
之精微焉此固振古之傑而三晉之首出
者也即溫公且願執鞭矣景行先哲徵稷
說吾誰與歸
第四問
成以蒙
同考試官教諭謝　批〔小學大學本自一貫是作發揮〕
精邃而詞調雅飭足覺羣蒙矣
考試官教諭王　批〔篇終力排二氏是能自信者〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔明正的確〕
天下之道一而已矣有徇象之敝而後有
探本之論此道器之說所由始也君子之
學致一而已矣有逐末之敝而後有務本
之論此德藝之說所由始也夫道之與器
punctuated:
必於隱也。自「蒸民乃粒」格於「皇天」，可以言事功，與夔、契、伊、周齊驅矣；自《益稷》之篇、《說命》之篇，渾渾灝灝，可以言文章，與《皐謨》、《伊訓》竝駕矣。乃稷自爲兒時，屹如巨人之志，與說之「終始典學，遜志時敏」，又皆致道德之精微焉。此固振古之傑，而三晉之首出者也。即溫公且願執鞭矣，景行先哲，徵稷、說，吾誰與歸？

第四問
成以蒙
同考試官教諭謝　批：〔小學大學，本自一貫，是作發揮〕精邃，而詞調雅飭，足覺羣蒙矣。
考試官教諭王　批：〔篇終力排二氏，是能自信者。〕
考試官教諭趙　批：〔明正的確。〕

天下之道，一而已矣。有徇象之敝，而後有探本之論，此道、器之說所由始也。君子之學，致一而已矣。有逐末之敝，而後有務本之論，此德、藝之說所由始也。夫道之與器，
translation_en:
… necessarily insist on living in seclusion. From "allowing all the multitude of the people to have grain to eat" to "reaching up to Mighty Heaven," one can speak of their achievements as keeping pace with those of Kui, Xie, Yi Yin, and the Duke of Zhou. From the "Yi and Ji" (Yi Ji) chapter and the "Charge to Yue" (Yue Ming) chapters, vast and boundless in style, one can speak of their literary expression as running neck and neck with the "Counsels of Gao Yao" (Gao Mo) and the "Instructions of Yi" (Yi Xun). Moreover, Hou Ji's towering ambition like that of a great man even from childhood, along with Fu Yue's "fixing his thoughts on learning from first to last, keeping a humble mind and being ever diligent," both attained the subtlest essence of moral virtue. Truly these were heroes for all antiquity, and the foremost figures to emerge from the Three Jin region [Shanxi]. Even Sima Guang [Wengong] would have gladly served as their charioteer! Looking up to follow the great worthies of the past, if not Hou Ji and Fu Yue, to whom else should I turn?

Fourth Policy Question
Cheng Yimeng
Associate Examiner and Instructor Xie comments: [Elementary learning and Great Learning originally form a single continuous thread; this essay expounds on it] with profound depth, and its phrasing and tone are elegant and disciplined—enough to awaken the unenlightened multitude.
Examiner and Instructor Wang comments: [At the end of the piece he vigorously refutes the two heterodox sects (Buddhism and Daoism); this shows someone of genuine self-conviction.]
Examiner and Instructor Zhao comments: [Clear, upright, and precise.]

The Way of all under heaven is simply one. Only after the abuse of clinging to outward phenomena arose was there discourse on investigating the root; this is how the doctrine of the Way (dao) and concrete vessels (qi) began. The learning of the gentleman is simply to achieve oneness. Only after the abuse of pursuing secondary branches arose was there discourse on attending to the root; this is how the doctrine of moral virtue (de) and the arts (yi) began. Now, as for the Way and concrete vessels, …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
固以形而上形而下言矣苟離之爲二吾
恐形上之理舍器則無所附麗也德之與
藝固以成而上成而下言矣苟偏有所事
吾恐成德之君子舍藝亦無所寄其精神
心術之運也然則天下之道固一而已矣
君子之學亦一而已矣執事發策而以先
王之教下問承學是將以有德有造惠諸
生而望其有脩身應世之具甚盛心也敢
因明問而復之夫道未嘗有小大也而先
===
王之教胡以有小學大學之分耶小學之
爲教也蓋因小子之學而名之也其所習
則禮樂之文爲射御書數之法焉如內則
之所稱是已大學之爲教也蓋因大人之
學而名之也其所學則格致誠正以脩己
也齊家治國平天下以治人也如曾氏之
所傳是已夫曾氏之傳家譚戶說夫人能
道之矣乃六藝雖列之小學而多闕失不
傳其名物之僅存於周官保氏者以五禮
punctuated:
固以形而上、形而下言矣，苟離之爲二，吾恐形上之理，舍器則無所附麗也。德之與藝，固以成而上、成而下言矣，苟偏有所事，吾恐成德之君子，舍藝亦無所寄其精神心術之運也。然則天下之道，固一而已矣；君子之學，亦一而已矣。執事發策，而以先王之教下問承學，是將以有德有造惠諸生，而望其有脩身應世之具，甚盛心也！敢因明問而復之。

夫道未嘗有小大也，而先王之教，胡以有小學、大學之分耶？小學之爲教也，蓋因小子之學而名之也。其所習，則禮樂之文爲射御書數之法焉，如《內則》之所稱是已。大學之爲教也，蓋因大人之學而名之也。其所學，則格致誠正以脩己也，齊家治國平天下以治人也，如曾氏之所傳是已。夫曾氏之傳，家譚戶說，夫人能道之矣；乃六藝雖列之小學，而多闕失不傳。其名物之僅存於《周官》保氏者：以五禮，
translation_en:
… are indeed spoken of in terms of "what is above physical form" and "what is below physical form"; yet if one separates them into two, I fear that the principle above physical form, were it to abandon concrete implements, would have nothing to which to attach itself. Virtue and the arts are indeed spoken of in terms of "what is above upon achievement" and "what is below upon achievement"; yet if one engages in them one-sidedly, I fear that the gentleman of accomplished virtue, were he to abandon the arts, would likewise have nowhere to lodge the workings of his spirit and mind. This being so, the Way of the world is indeed simply one, and the learning of the gentleman is likewise simply one. That Your Honor has issued this policy question, inquiring of us junior scholars about the teachings of the former kings, shows that you intend to favor us students by making us men of virtue and accomplishment, hoping that we shall possess the wherewithal to cultivate our persons and respond to the world—a most generous intention indeed! I venture to reply by following your enlightened inquiry.

Now, the Way has never had "lesser" or "greater"; why then did the teachings of the former kings have a distinction between Lesser Learning (Xiaoxue) and Greater Learning (Daxue)? As a teaching, the Lesser Learning was so named because it was the learning for youths. What they practiced were the refinements of rites and music and [為, read as 與?] the methods of archery, charioteering, calligraphy, and mathematics, just as described in the Pattern of the Family (Neize). As a teaching, the Greater Learning was so named because it was the learning for adults. What they studied was investigating things, extending knowledge, making the intentions sincere, and rectifying the mind in order to cultivate the self; and regulating the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world in order to govern others—just as transmitted by Master Zeng (Zengshi). Now, what Master Zeng transmitted is discussed in every family and household; everyone is able to speak of it. Yet although the Six Arts were listed under the Lesser Learning, much of them has been lost and not transmitted. As for their names and details that barely survive under the Master of Instruction (Baoshi) in the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan): with respect to the Five Rites, …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
則吉凶軍賓嘉也以六樂則雲門大咸大
韶大夏大濩大武也以五射則白矢參連
剡注襄尺井儀也以五御則鳴和鸞逐水
曲過君表舞交衢逐禽左也以六書則象
形會意轉注指事假借諧聲也以九數則
方田粟米差分少廣商功均輸贏朒方程
句股也此六藝之實也夫自六藝以藝名
而世儒者徒聞聖人道器德藝之言而不
得其所以言也於是有高譚玄妙以求所
===
謂形而上者而自附於德成之君子一涉
於名物器數則曰此藝耳此藝耳愚竊以
爲大謬不然也大學之所貴非適用乎譬
之衣焉需以禦寒布帛其常也如必求其
華而美也則錦衣狐裘殆不可以易致然
猶曰是眞愈於布帛矣以爲猶不足貴而
求天孫雲錦之裳果有得於禦寒否乎譬
之食焉求以濟饑菽粟其常也如必求其
甘而美也則珍果膏粱殆不可以易得然
punctuated: 則吉、凶、軍、賓、嘉也；以六樂，則《雲門》、《大咸》、《大韶》、《大夏》、《大濩》、《大武》也；以五射，則白矢、參連、剡注、襄尺、井儀也；以五御，則鳴和鸞、逐水曲、過君表、舞交衢、逐禽左也；以六書，則象形、會意、轉注、指事、假借、諧聲也；以九數，則方田、粟米、差分、少廣、商功、均輸、贏朒、方程、句股也。此六藝之實也。夫自六藝以藝名，而世儒者徒聞聖人道器、德藝之言，而不得其所以言也。於是有高譚玄妙，以求所謂形而上者，而自附於德成之君子；一涉於名物器數，則曰：「此藝耳，此藝耳。」愚竊以爲大謬不然也。大學之所貴，非適用乎？譬之衣焉，需以禦寒，布帛其常也。如必求其華而美也，則錦衣狐裘，殆不可以易致，然猶曰是眞愈於布帛矣；以爲猶不足貴，而求天孫雲錦之裳，果有得於禦寒否乎？譬之食焉，求以濟饑，菽粟其常也。如必求其甘而美也，則珍果膏粱，殆不可以易得，然
translation_en:
… are auspicious rites, mourning rites, military rites, guest rites, and festive rites; as for the Six Musics, they are Yunmen (Cloud Gate), Daxian (Great All-Embracing), Dashao (Great Succession), Daxia (Great Xia), Dahuo (Great Protection), and Dawu (Great Martial); as for the Five Archeries, they are white arrow (baishi), triple connection (sanlian),feather-downward shot (yanzhu), yielding a foot (xiangchi), and well-pattern (jingyi); as for the Five Charioteerings, they are harmonizing the bells (ming heluan), following the bends of watercourses (zhu shuiqu), passing the ruler's markers (guo junbiao), wheeling at intersections (wu jiaoqu), and driving game to the left (zhu qinzuo); as for the Six Scripts, they are pictographs (xiangxing), compound ideographs (huiyi), derivative cognates (zhuanzhu), simple indicatives (zhishi), phonetic loans (jiajie), and phono-semantic compounds (xiesheng); as for the Nine Computations, they are rectangular fields (fangtian), millet and rice (sumi), proportional distribution (chafen), diminishing breadths (shaoguang), consultations on engineering works (shanggong), equitable taxation and transport (junshu), excess and deficit (yingnu), rectangular arrays (fangcheng), and base and altitude (gougu). These are the substance of the Six Arts.

Ever since the Six Arts were designated as "arts," conventional scholars have merely heard the sages' words concerning the Way and concrete vessels, or virtue and the arts, without grasping what they meant by those words. Consequently, some engage in lofty talk of abstruse mysteries in pursuit of what is called that which is "above physical form," counting themselves among gentlemen of accomplished virtue; yet the moment they touch upon names, objects, vessels, and numbers, they say, "This is merely an art, this is merely an art!" I privately consider this to be gravely mistaken and not so. Is not what the Great Learning values its practical application? Take clothing as an analogy: when needed to ward off the cold, linen and silk are the norm. If one insists on seeking what is splendid and fine, then brocade robes and fox furs can scarcely be easily obtained, though one might still say these are truly superior to linen and silk; yet if one deems even these not precious enough and seeks a skirt of cloud-brocade woven by the Celestial Granddaughter, would that really be of any avail in warding off the cold? Or take food as an analogy: when sought to relieve hunger, beans and grain are the norm. If one insists on seeking what is sweet and delicious, then rare fruits and rich meats and fine grains can scarcely be easily acquired, though…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
猶曰是眞勝於菽粟矣以爲猶不足羨而
思甘露醴泉之飲果有得於濟饑否乎今
夫外器而求道也舍藝而論德也是棄布
帛菽粟而求雲錦之裳甘露醴泉之飲者
也匪直艱得無可得之理矣善哉先王之
設教乎自成童以至弱冠凡教民誦詩舞
勺習禮習射御者未嘗廢焉豈以徒藝溺
其民也蓋以六藝之爲教皆實用之不可
缺而妙道精義又無不寓於其中故使童
===
而習之俟其既長而與之相忘則卽器而
道存卽藝而成德雖至耄耋亦是學也此
古之人才體用合一有非後世所可及也
歟然則六藝之不爲徒器與藝也此固其
一驗矣至哉吾夫子之論學乎自志道以
至依仁無非成德之事而游藝之稱蓋與
之竝焉豈欲以藝士成其名也蓋以道德
仁之理無不散見於禮樂名物之間而禮
樂名物之迹固皆道德仁至理之所寓故
punctuated: 猶曰是眞勝於菽粟矣。以爲猶不足羨，而思甘露醴泉之飲，果有得於濟饑否乎？今夫外器而求道也，舍藝而論德也，是棄布帛菽粟，而求雲錦之裳、甘露醴泉之飲者也。匪直艱得，無可得之理矣。善哉，先王之設教乎！自成童以至弱冠，凡教民誦詩、舞勺、習禮、習射御者，未嘗廢焉。豈以徒藝溺其民也？蓋以六藝之爲教，皆實用之不可缺，而妙道精義又無不寓於其中。故使童而習之，俟其既長而與之相忘，則卽器而道存，卽藝而成德，雖至耄耋，亦是學也。此古之人才體用合一，有非後世所可及也歟！然則六藝之不爲徒器與藝也，此固其一驗矣。至哉，吾夫子之論學乎！自志道以至依仁，無非成德之事，而游藝之稱，蓋與之竝焉。豈欲以藝士成其名也？蓋以道德仁之理，無不散見於禮樂名物之間，而禮樂名物之迹，固皆道德仁至理之所寓。故
translation_en:
…one might still say that these are truly superior to beans and grain. Yet if one considers even these not worthy of admiration, and longs instead for a drink of sweet dew and sweet spring water, would that actually be of any help in relieving hunger? Now, to cast aside concrete vessels in seeking the Way, or to abandon the arts in discussing virtue, is like discarding cloth, silk, beans, and grain to seek garments of cloud-brocade and drinks of sweet dew and sweet spring water. Not only are they difficult to obtain, there is in principle no way they can be obtained.

How excellent was the establishment of education by the former kings! From the age of fifteen up to the capping age of twenty, in all their instruction of the people—reciting the Odes, dancing the Shao, practicing ritual, and practicing archery and charioteering—none of these was ever neglected. Was this merely to immerse the people in empty arts? Rather, it was because the teachings of the Six Arts were all indispensable for practical use, and subtle ways and refined principles were without exception lodged within them. Therefore, they made them practice these in youth, waiting until they had grown up and become completely natural in them; then, right within the concrete vessels the Way was preserved, and right within the arts virtue was perfected. Even into their eighties and nineties, it was still this learning. Is this not why the men of talent in antiquity united substance and function in a way that later generations cannot match? Thus, that the Six Arts are not mere concrete vessels and arts—this is certainly one proof of it.

How supreme was our Master's discussion of learning! From setting the will on the Way to cleaving to humanity, all are matters of perfecting virtue, and yet the mention of "taking recreation in the arts" is placed right alongside them. Did he wish for men to establish their reputations merely as masters of technical arts? Rather, it was because the principles of the Way, virtue, and humanity are all manifested throughout the specifics of rites, music, names, and objects, and the outward traces of rites, music, names, and objects are indeed the very places where the ultimate principles of the Way, virtue, and humanity reside. Therefore…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
朝夕游焉使其內外兩忘則體卽道用卽
義雖至不踰矩亦此學也此聖人之學道
器一貫有非世人之所可及也歟而六藝
之不爲徒器與藝也此又其一驗矣遠稽
先王之教載觀夫子之訓則六藝之爲教
也果無當於用而不必習者耶抑切於用
而不可廢者耶夫其謂之小學者以童子
之知識則未廣也以才力則未充也教之
之法當自此始耳非謂其學之小也所謂
===
藝成而下者則指執技事上者言之蓋祝
史射御醫卜百工之流專執一技以事上
所謂不貳事不移官者而非君子之學也
今厭小學之名而不爲則將何以爲大學
藝成之說而不習則將何以爲德是欲陟
九層之臺不由其階不循其級而思一蹴
至也吾不知其術矣噫王道衰而實學廢
聖教遠而異說興名物器數旣鄙薄以爲
小學而不爲乃明德親民又徒取其於出
punctuated: 朝夕游焉，使其內外兩忘，則體卽道、用卽義，雖至不踰矩，亦此學也。此聖人之學，道器一貫，有非世人之所可及也歟！而六藝之不爲徒器與藝也，此又其一驗矣。遠稽先王之教，載觀夫子之訓，則六藝之爲教也，果無當於用而不必習者耶？抑切於用而不可廢者耶？夫其謂之「小學」者，以童子之知識則未廣也，以才力則未充也，教之之法當自此始耳，非謂其學之小也。所謂「藝成而下」者，則指執技事上者言之。蓋祝史、射御、醫卜、百工之流，專執一技以事上，所謂「不貳事、不移官」者，而非君子之學也。今厭小學之名而不爲，則將何以爲大學？藝成之說而不習，則將何以爲德？是欲陟九層之臺，不由其階、不循其級，而思一蹴至也，吾不知其術矣！噫！王道衰而實學廢，聖教遠而異說興，名物器數旣鄙薄以爲小學而不爲，乃明德親民，又徒取其於出
translation_en:
…if one immerses oneself in them morning and evening until the distinction between inner and outer is forgotten, then substance is the Way and function is righteousness; even reaching the stage of not overstepping the bounds is still this very learning. Such is the learning of the Sage, in which the Way and concrete vessels form a single thread—something beyond the reach of ordinary people of the world! That the Six Arts are not mere vessels and technical skills is once again demonstrated here.

If we look back far into the teachings of the former kings and examine again the precepts of the Master, then as a form of instruction, are the Six Arts really unsuited for practical use and unnecessary to practice? Or are they pertinent to practical use and indispensable? Now, the reason this is called "Lesser Learning" (xiaoxue) is simply that a youth's knowledge is not yet broad and his abilities and strength are not yet full, so the method of teaching him must begin from here—not that the learning itself is petty. As for the saying "the completion of an art is inferior," that refers to those who serve their superiors by practicing a specialized skill. People such as invocators, scribes, archers, charioteers, physicians, diviners, and the hundred artisans devote themselves exclusively to a single skill in order to serve their superiors—those who, as the saying goes, "do not take on double duties and do not change offices"—and this is not the learning of the gentleman.

Nowadays, if people disdain the name of "Lesser Learning" and refuse to engage in it, then by what means will they engage in the Great Learning (daxue)? And if [because of] the saying about "the completion of an art" they refuse to practice the arts, then by what means will they cultivate virtue? This is like wanting to ascend a nine-tiered terrace without using the stairs or following the steps, hoping to reach the top in a single bound—I do not know what art could accomplish that!

Alas! As the Kingly Way declined, practical learning was abandoned; as the Sage's teachings receded, heterodox doctrines arose. Names, objects, vessels, and numbers are already disdained as "Lesser Learning" and left unpracticed, while illuminating luminous virtue and renewing the people are merely reduced to what enters…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
入口耳之間是何學術之壞至後世而極
也宋儒真德秀氏有見於天下之道盡於
大學一書從而衍其義焉始以帝王爲治
之序繼以帝王爲學之本而明道術辨人
才審治體察民情者則格物致知之要也
崇敬畏戒逸欲則誠意正心之要也謹言
行正威儀則脩身之要也重妃匹嚴內治
定國本教戚屬則齊家之要也首以聖賢
之明訓參以往古之事蹟以爲四者之道
===
既得則治國平天下者在其中矣至我
朝丘濬氏復倣其體裁而補其闕焉先之審
幾微以誠正之所未周繼之十二要以
補治平之所未及而其所自爲序則又謂
眞氏之書主於理故所衍之義大而簡也
之所補者主於事故所衍之義細而詳也
嗚呼是二公者志則勤矣執事致意二書
且惓惓以脩身應世之學望諸生豈不以
二書竝有功於大學竝有裨於致用固不
punctuated: 入口耳之間，是何學術之壞至後世而極也！宋儒真德秀氏，有見於天下之道盡於《大學》一書，從而衍其義焉。始以帝王爲治之序，繼以帝王爲學之本。而明道術、辨人才、審治體、察民情者，則格物致知之要也；崇敬畏、戒逸欲，則誠意正心之要也；謹言行、正威儀，則脩身之要也；重妃匹、嚴內治、定國本、教戚屬，則齊家之要也。首以聖賢之明訓，參以往古之事蹟，以爲四者之道既得，則治國平天下者在其中矣。至我朝丘濬氏，復倣其體裁而補其闕焉。先之「審幾微」，以誠正之所未周；繼之「十二要」，以補治平之所未及。而其所自爲序，則又謂眞氏之書主於理，故所衍之義大而簡；也之所補者主於事，故所衍之義細而詳也。嗚呼，是二公者，志則勤矣！執事致意二書，且惓惓以脩身應世之學望諸生，豈不以二書竝有功於《大學》，竝有裨於致用，固不
translation_en: …merely what passes between the mouth and the ear—how utterly has scholarship deteriorated in later ages! The Song-dynasty Confucian scholar Zhen Dexiu 真德秀 perceived that the Way of all under heaven is fully contained within the single book of the Great Learning (Daxue), and accordingly he extended its meanings. He began with the sequence of governance for emperors and kings, and continued with the foundation of learning for emperors and kings. Clarifying the Way and its methods, distinguishing men of talent, examining the substance of governance, and investigating the conditions of the people—these are the essentials of investigating things and extending knowledge. Revering awe and respect, and guarding against idleness and desires—these are the essentials of making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind. Being cautious in speech and conduct, and rectifying one's dignified demeanor—these are the essentials of cultivating the person. Valuing imperial consorts, strictly ordering the inner court, establishing the dynastic foundation, and instructing imperial relatives—these are the essentials of regulating the family. Heading each section with the clear instructions of the sages and worthies and cross-referencing them with the historical deeds of antiquity, he held that once the Way of these four is attained, ordering the state and bringing peace to all under heaven are already encompassed therein. When it came to Qiu Jun 丘濬 of our own dynasty, he again imitated its format and supplemented what was lacking. He placed "Examining the Subtle Incipiencies" first, in order to [supply] what was not yet comprehensive in making the intentions sincere and rectifying the mind; and he followed this with the "Twelve Essentials," in order to supplement what had not yet been reached in ordering the state and bringing peace to all under heaven. In the preface that he wrote himself, he further stated that Master Zhen's book focuses on principle (li), so the meanings it elaborates are broad and concise; whereas what he himself [reading 也 as 己?] supplemented focuses on practical affairs (shi), so the meanings it elaborates are detailed and thorough. Alas, how diligent were the intentions of these two gentlemen! When Your Excellency directs your attention to these two books, and earnestly hopes that we students will pursue the learning of cultivating the person and responding to the world, is it not because both books have rendered meritorious service to the Great Learning and both are beneficial to practical application, so that one certainly cannot…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
容以人有古今而可畧也愚生以爲不獨
二書也即先王大學小學之教則大學主
於理小學主於事固脩身應世之至切者
也彼於其事旣廢而不講於其所遺之經
傳又出入口耳而不知體焉則又何有於
眞氏之衍義又何有於文莊之補哉噫學
術之壞未有甚於後世者也是有說焉而
愚生姑舉其槩請無罪焉可乎三代而上
二氏之言未行於中國固其學一出於實
===
士生其時所聞者實理也所習者實事也
即未能融道器德藝而一貫之亦不失爲
致用之才三代而下二氏之說寖行而未
世儒者又多竊附之說故其學盡出於虛
聰明才智之士所樂聞者玄妙之言也所
喜譚者幽渺之論也舉一切應世之務而
掃滌之故以之致用多礙矣士習之敝端
在於此然則今之論學姑未暇及於一貫
姑未暇及於語上也而務實勝者其救時
punctuated: 容以人有古今而可畧也？愚生以爲不獨二書也，即先王大學、小學之教，則大學主於理，小學主於事，固脩身應世之至切者也。彼於其事旣廢而不講，於其所遺之經傳，又出入口耳而不知體焉，則又何有於眞氏之《衍義》？又何有於文莊之《補》哉？噫！學術之壞，未有甚於後世者也！是有說焉，而愚生姑舉其槩，請無罪焉，可乎？三代而上，二氏之言未行於中國，固其學一出於實。士生其時，所聞者實理也，所習者實事也，即未能融道器、德藝而一貫之，亦不失爲致用之才。三代而下，二氏之說寖行，而未世儒者又多竊附之說，故其學盡出於虛。聰明才智之士，所樂聞者玄妙之言也，所喜譚者幽渺之論也，舉一切應世之務而掃滌之，故以之致用多礙矣。士習之敝，端在於此。然則今之論學，姑未暇及於一貫，姑未暇及於語上也，而務實勝者，其救時…
translation_en: …allow either to be neglected on the grounds that their authors belong to the past or the present? I, your humble student, believe that this applies not only to these two books. Even in the Former Kings' teachings of the Greater Learning (Daxue) and the Lesser Learning (Xiaoxue), the Greater Learning focuses on principle while the Lesser Learning focuses on practical affairs—both being utterly essential for cultivating the self and responding to the world. When people abandon those practical affairs and fail to study them, and when they treat the surviving classics and commentaries merely as matters passing from ear to mouth without knowing how to embody them, what use have they for Master Zhen's Extended Meaning (Yanyi), and what use have they for Wenzhuang's [Qiu Jun's] Supplement (Bu)? Alas! The corruption of scholarship has never been worse than in later ages! There is a reason for this; may I, your humble student, provisionally outline its general course and beg not to be faulted for it? During the Three Dynasties and before, the teachings of the Two Sects [Buddhism and Daoism] had not yet spread in China, so learning derived entirely from what was substantive. For scholars born in those times, what they heard were substantive principles, and what they practiced were substantive affairs; even if they could not yet fuse the Way and concrete vessels, or virtue and the arts, into a single thread, they still did not fail to become talents fit for practical application. After the Three Dynasties, the doctrines of the Two Sects gradually gained currency, and Confucian scholars of later ages [reading 未 as 末] frequently borrowed and attached themselves to those doctrines; thus their learning came entirely from emptiness. What scholars of intelligence and talent delighted in hearing were abstruse and mysterious words, and what they loved to discuss were obscure and remote theories. They took all affairs of responding to the world and swept them away, and thus when they tried to apply their learning in practice, they met with many obstacles. The corruption of literati customs lies precisely in this. Therefore, in discussing learning today, we do not yet have the leisure to speak of a single unifying thread, nor do we yet have the leisure to speak of the highest things; rather, striving for substantive results is the [most urgent task] for saving the times…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
反本之急務者
第五問
施重光
同考試官教諭李　批〔選將擇吏兩者安攘大計子先內後外之論洞燭時宜至末段意更緊切未可以書生目之〕
考試官教諭王　批〔蓄威昭德五事鑿鑿可行〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔區畫詳確〕
蓋聞經國芘民之道若養身然善養身者
先其五內後其四支而衛生周矣善爲國
===
者始於內脩終於外攘而衛國備矣腹心
未固而手足之是謀不知類者也不知類
者其究必蹶盭戶口未實而疆圉之是庀
不知務者也不知務者其究必杌隉察內
外之宜循先後之序俾揆武之略寓於脩
文折衝之謀定於樽俎安居乎區中而威
行乎方外此蓋臣之訏謨哲王之上務也
且安攘之計大矣其大權在朝廷其分職
宣猷者在守令將帥守令握章綰綬撫摩
punctuated:
反本之急務者。

第五問
施重光
同考試官教諭李　批〔選將擇吏，兩者安攘大計。子先內後外之論，洞燭時宜。至末段，意更緊切，未可以書生目之。〕
考試官教諭王　批〔蓄威昭德，五事鑿鑿可行。〕
考試官教諭趙　批〔區畫詳確。〕

蓋聞經國芘民之道，若養身然。善養身者，先其五內，後其四支，而衛生周矣；善爲國者，始於內脩，終於外攘，而衛國備矣。腹心未固，而手足之是謀，不知類者也；不知類者，其究必蹶盭。戶口未實，而疆圉之是庀，不知務者也；不知務者，其究必杌隉。察內外之宜，循先後之序，俾揆武之略寓於脩文，折衝之謀定於樽俎，安居乎區中，而威行乎方外，此蓋臣之訏謨，哲王之上務也。且安攘之計大矣，其大權在朝廷，其分職宣猷者在守令、將帥。守令握章綰綬，撫摩
translation_en:
…the urgent task of returning to fundamentals.

Fifth Policy Question
Shi Chongguang 施重光
Associate Examiner, Instructor Li, comments: [Selecting generals and choosing officials are both grand strategies for pacifying the interior and repelling external threats. Your argument of putting the interior first and the exterior second thoroughly illuminates the needs of the times. By the final section, the meaning grows even more urgent and incisive—one cannot view the author as a mere bookish scholar.]
Examiner, Instructor Wang, comments: [Accumulating martial awe and manifesting virtue—the five measures are concrete and practicable.]
Examiner, Instructor Zhao, comments: [The planning is detailed and precise.]

I have heard that the Way of governing the state and sheltering the people is like nourishing the body. One who is skilled at nourishing the body puts his five internal organs first and his four limbs second, and thus the preservation of life is complete; one who is skilled at governing a state begins with internal cultivation and ends with repelling external threats, and thus the defense of the state is fully prepared. When the heart and belly are not yet secure, to plan only for the hands and feet is to fail to understand relative categories; one who fails to understand relative categories will in the end surely stumble and go awry. When households and population are not yet full, to attend only to the frontiers is to fail to understand priorities; one who fails to understand priorities will in the end surely fall into perilous instability. To examine what is appropriate for the interior and exterior, to follow the sequence of what comes first and what comes after, so that the strategy for managing martial affairs is lodged within the cultivation of civil governance, and plans for repelling enemy assaults are settled among the wine goblets of the court—dwelling securely within the central realm while martial awe extends beyond the borders—this is indeed the grand counsel of a loyal minister [reading 蓋臣 as 藎臣] and the supreme task of a wise king.

Moreover, the grand strategy of pacifying the interior and repelling external threats is vast indeed. Its supreme authority rests with the imperial court, while those who divide the duties and carry out the plans are the prefects and magistrates, and the generals and commanders. Prefects and magistrates grasp their seals and bind on their ribbons, soothing and comforting…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
一方責在安內而休養元元實北保障則
所係固不專於內也將帥秉鉞仗旄司命
三軍責在𨶒外而百萬貔貅仰給編氓則
又未嘗不托重於內也此守令將帥相待
爲理之說也古稱守令之盛者莫如漢五
鳳神爵之間宣帝長於閭閻習民疾苦故
其時重守令有治效異等者天子使使持
璽書勞之增秩賜金九卿有闕者不次徵
用一時循吏如潁川黄霸敎化式崇東郡
===
韓延壽禮讓樹軌尹翁歸振潔於扶風召
信臣播澤於南陽斯其選已而時方操切
獨用寛和覇尤爲夐出焉古稱將帥之盛
者莫如漢元朔元光之間武帝逞其雄材
鋭意邊功故其時重將帥有出塞得當者
襁褓者皆得拜爵一時猛將如衛青出上
天子不吝數千戸封之剖符錫劵子弟在
谷而窮追龍城霍去病出隴西而遠絶狼
望李廣奮臂於鴈門公孫敖鞅掌於出代
punctuated:
一方，責在安內，而休養元元，實北保障，則所係固不專於內也。將帥秉鉞仗旄，司命三軍，責在𨶒外，而百萬貔貅，仰給編氓，則又未嘗不托重於內也。此守令、將帥相待爲理之說也。
古稱守令之盛者，莫如漢五鳳、神爵之間。宣帝長於閭閻，習民疾苦，故其時重守令。有治效異等者，天子使使持璽書勞之，增秩賜金，九卿有闕者，不次徵用。一時循吏，如潁川黄霸敎化式崇，東郡韓延壽禮讓樹軌，尹翁歸振潔於扶風，召信臣播澤於南陽，斯其選已。而時方操切，獨用寛和，覇尤爲夐出焉。
古稱將帥之盛者，莫如漢元朔、元光之間。武帝逞其雄材，鋭意邊功，故其時重將帥。有出塞得當者，襁褓者皆得拜爵，一時猛將如衛青出上天子不吝數千戸封之，剖符錫劵，子弟在谷而窮追龍城，霍去病出隴西而遠絶狼望，李廣奮臂於鴈門，公孫敖鞅掌於出代，
translation_en:
…a region; their responsibility lies in pacifying the interior, yet resting and nourishing the common people actually makes strong [?] the defensive bulwark—thus what depends on them is certainly not confined solely to the interior. Generals and commanders wield the battle-axe and hold the command standard, controlling the fate of the Three Armies; their responsibility lies in repelling external foes, yet a million fierce troops depend for their provisions upon the registered commoners—thus they, too, have never failed to rely heavily upon the interior. This is the principle that Grand Administrators and Magistrates on the one hand, and generals and commanders on the other, depend upon each other to achieve good governance.

In antiquity, those who spoke of the flourishing of Grand Administrators and Magistrates found no era comparable to the Wufeng (57–54 BCE) and Shenjue (61–58 BCE) reign periods of the Han. Emperor Xuan grew up among the common lanes and villages and was familiar with the hardships of the people; therefore, in his time great weight was placed on Grand Administrators and Magistrates. When there were those whose administrative achievements were of extraordinary grade, the Son of Heaven sent envoys bearing imperial letters under the玺 seal to reward and comfort them, increasing their salary ranks and bestowing gold upon them; when there were vacancies among the Nine Ministers, they were summoned for appointment out of the regular sequence. Upright officials of the time—such as Huang Ba 黄霸 in Yingchuan, who exalted moral transformation; Han Yanshou 韓延壽 in Dong Commandery, who established models of ritual propriety and yielding; Yin Wenggui 尹翁歸, who displayed integrity in Fufeng; and Shao Xinchen 召信臣, who spread beneficence in Nanyang—these were the finest choices. And at a time when governance tended toward strictness and urgency, Ba alone employed leniency and harmony, standing out far above the rest.

In antiquity, those who spoke of the flourishing of generals and commanders found no era comparable to the Yuanshuo (128–123 BCE) and Yuanguang (134–129 BCE) reign periods of the Han. Emperor Wu gave free rein to his heroic talents and set his mind keenly on frontier achievements; therefore, in his time great weight was placed on generals and commanders. When there were those who went beyond the frontier passes and matched the enemy successfully, [note: two columns transposed in transcription] the Son of Heaven did not begrudge enfeoffing them with several thousand households, splitting tallies and bestowing iron certificates of investiture, so that even their sons and younger brothers still in swaddling clothes all received noble ranks. Fierce generals of the time—such as Wei Qing 衛青 going out from Shanggu and pursuing the enemy all the way to Longcheng; Huo Qubing 霍去病 going out from Longxi and crossing far beyond the Langwang mountains; Li Guang 李廣 baring his arms in Yanmen; and Gongsun Ao 公孫敖 laboring busily in going out from Dai…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
斯其傑巳而恩著柎循士樂爲用李將軍
尤稱偉焉總之武帝襲文景之富庶故任
將征討以快其好大喜功之心而海内虛
耗此務外而不務内之明鑒也宣帝懲孝
武之敝轍故選賢任用以佐其與民休息
之化而呼韓款塞此内順治而外威嚴之
明效也繇斯以譚三晉之事可得而衡度
矣葢山西幅幀千里襟喉三關循關而右
則煙爨相逺雞犬相聞者太平澤潞之内
===
地也内地重守令今之郡縣守令氷檗自
勵鸞鳳自許者固亦有之寧無以察爲明
以刻爲威者乎寧無貪墨𣫍斂朘剝脂膏
者乎寧無趾踈草野之閭目絶蔀屋之下
者乎即不然亦惟是簿書期會焉耳飭廚
饌盛供具當使客意焉耳此亡論追蹤漢
循即視近代悃愊之吏亦懸絶矣生民何
賴焉故關南之務擇吏其急也循關而左
則斥堠聯絡什伍團結者大同一帶之邊
punctuated:
斯其傑巳。而恩著柎循，士樂爲用，李將軍尤稱偉焉。總之，武帝襲文景之富庶，故任將征討，以快其好大喜功之心，而海内虛耗，此務外而不務内之明鑒也；宣帝懲孝武之敝轍，故選賢任用，以佐其與民休息之化，而呼韓款塞，此内順治而外威嚴之明效也。繇斯以譚，三晉之事可得而衡度矣。

葢山西幅幀千里，襟喉三關。循關而右，則煙爨相逺，雞犬相聞者，太平、澤、潞之内地也。内地重守令。今之郡縣守令，氷檗自勵、鸞鳳自許者，固亦有之；寧無以察爲明，以刻爲威者乎？寧無貪墨𣫍斂，朘剝脂膏者乎？寧無趾踈草野之閭，目絶蔀屋之下者乎？即不然，亦惟是簿書期會焉耳，飭廚饌、盛供具，當使客意焉耳。此亡論追蹤漢循，即視近代悃愊之吏，亦懸絶矣，生民何賴焉？故關南之務，擇吏其急也。循關而左，則斥堠聯絡，什伍團結者，大同一帶之邊
translation_en:
…these were the outstanding ones. Yet in showing kindness by comforting and caring for the troops so that the soldiers were glad to be of service, General Li (Li Guang 李廣) was especially praised as great. In sum, Emperor Wu (Wudi 武帝) inherited the wealth and populousness of the reigns of Emperors Wen (Wendi 文帝) and Jing (Jingdi 景帝), and therefore he employed generals to undertake punitive expeditions to gratify his fondness for grandiose achievements, whereby the realm within the seas was left depleted and exhausted—this is a clear warning against attending to external affairs while neglecting internal ones. Emperor Xuan (Xuandi 宣帝) took warning from the ruinous course of the filial Emperor Wu, and therefore selected and employed worthy men to assist in his transformation of giving rest and recuperation to the people, whereby Huhan (Huhanye Chanyu 呼韓邪單于) came knocking at the frontier passes in submission—this is the clear efficacy of having harmonious governance within and awe-inspiring authority without. Discussing the matter from this perspective, the affairs of the Three Jin (Shanxi 山西) can be weighed and measured.

Indeed, Shanxi stretches across a thousand li in territory, with the Three Passes serving as its strategic collar and throat. Following the passes to the right (south/interior), where cooking smoke stretches far and wide and the sounds of chickens and dogs can be heard from one village to the next, lies the interior region of Taiping 太平, Ze (Zezhou 澤州), and Lu (Luzhou 潞州). In the interior region, importance is placed on Prefects and Magistrates.
