Among the Prefects and Magistrates of commanderies and counties today, there are of course those who spur themselves on with icy purity and bitter austerity, and who hold themselves to the standard of phoenixes. Yet could there be none who mistake fault-finding for perceptiveness and harshness for authority? Could there be none who are corrupt and rapaciously extractive, scraping away the fat and lifeblood of the people? Could there be none whose footsteps rarely reach the rustic villages, and whose eyes never look beneath the roofs of humble huts? And even if they are not like this, they merely occupy themselves with account books and scheduled deadlines, or merely put in order kitchen delicacies and lavishly prepare provisions and utensils to please the wishes of visiting emissaries and guests. Not to mention following in the footsteps of the virtuous officials of the Han, even when compared to the sincere and unpretentious officials of recent times, they are worlds apart! On what, then, can the common people rely? Therefore, in the affairs south of the passes, selecting capable officials is the most urgent task. Following the passes to the left (north/frontier), where watchtowers are linked in a network and squads of five and ten are banded together, lies the frontier region around Datong 大同…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
地也邊地重將帥令之治邊將領貔虎
褭揚威虎帳者豈其無之不有出身紈袴
翁鈴莫辨者乎不有起家債帥頑頓無恥
者乎不有譚甲兵則縮頸而股慄聽鼙鼓
則掩耳而疾走者乎即不然亦惟是樹威
黷貨焉耳貿邊釁冒首功遷秩幕府焉耳
此亡論媲美漢將即視近代虎賁之臣有
餘愧矣邊庭何賴焉故關北之務選將其
急也然此皆一隅之論非聖王先內而後
===
外之良謨也蓋天下有不可易之紀綱有
不可忽之根本天保以上治內採薇以下
治外外分不得相侵職不得相越守令將帥
各事其事者不易之紀綱也然內可以兼
外而外不可以兼內羆范守雲中而匈奴
遠塞張巡守睢陽而保障江淮以守令之
責兼將帥之事是不可忽之根本也故爲
守令者其飭武備之術有二惇榭民之實
有三一曰完城堡蓋論天下之形勝則九
punctuated:
地也。邊地重將帥。令之治邊將領，貔虎褭，揚威虎帳者，豈其無之？不有出身紈袴、翁鈴莫辨者乎？不有起家債帥、頑頓無恥者乎？不有譚甲兵則縮頸而股慄，聽鼙鼓則掩耳而疾走者乎？即不然，亦惟是樹威黷貨焉耳，貿邊釁、冒首功、遷秩幕府焉耳。此亡論媲美漢將，即視近代虎賁之臣，有餘愧矣，邊庭何賴焉？故關北之務，選將其急也。

然此皆一隅之論，非聖王先內而後外之良謨也。蓋天下有不可易之紀綱，有不可忽之根本。《天保》以上治內，《採薇》以下治外，外分不得相侵，職不得相越，守令將帥各事其事者，不易之紀綱也。然內可以兼外，而外不可以兼內。羆范守雲中而匈奴遠塞，張巡守睢陽而保障江淮，以守令之責兼將帥之事，是不可忽之根本也。故爲守令者，其飭武備之術有二，惇榭民之實有三：一曰完城堡。蓋論天下之形勝，則九
translation_en:
… region. In border regions, emphasis is placed on generals and commanders. Among today's [reading 令 as 今] border-defense generals and commanders, how could there not be those who are like fierce beasts and fine steeds [貔虎驍褭?], displaying their martial awe from the tiger-skin command tent? Yet are there not also those who come from privileged backgrounds in fine silks and cannot even distinguish between basic military texts [reading 翁鈴 as 韜鈐]? Are there not those who rise to their posts as debt-ridden commanders, obtuse and shameless? Are there not those who shrink their necks and tremble in the legs at the mere mention of armor and weapons, or cover their ears and flee at the sound of war drums? Even if they are not like this, they merely establish personal authority and greedily amass wealth, or provoke border clashes, falsely claim credit for enemy heads, and seek promotion through the military headquarters. Setting aside any comparison with the great generals of the Han dynasty, even when measured against the valiant warrior-ministers of recent times, they should be more than ashamed! What can the frontier rely upon? Therefore, in the affairs north of the passes, selecting generals is the most urgent task.

Yet all of these are arguments addressing only one corner of the problem, not the sagely kings' sound strategy of prioritizing the interior before the exterior. Indeed, the empire has unchangeable governing principles and fundamental roots that cannot be neglected. In the Book of Odes, the poems from "Tianbao" (Heaven Protects) and earlier govern the interior, while those from "Caiwei" (Plucking Bracken) and later govern the exterior. Their spheres [reading 外分 as 名分 or 內外之分] must not infringe upon one another, and their offices must not overstep one another; that prefects and magistrates on the one hand and generals and commanders on the other each attend to their own affairs is an unchangeable governing principle. Nevertheless, the interior can encompass the exterior, whereas the exterior cannot encompass the interior. When Wei Shang and Lian Fan [reading 羆范 as 魏范] guarded Yunzhong, the Xiongnu stayed far from the frontier; when Zhang Xun 张巡 defended Suiyang, he safeguarded the Jiang and Huai regions. Combining the affairs of generals and commanders with the responsibilities of prefects and magistrates—this is the fundamental root that cannot be neglected. Therefore, for those who serve as prefects and magistrates, there are two methods for putting military preparedness in order, and three substantive measures for earnestly nurturing [reading 榭 as 撫] the people. The first is to repair walled forts. When discussing the strategic terrain of the empire, the Nine…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
邊爲險論三晉之形勝則三關爲險論郡
縣之形勝則城堡爲險城堡者民之緩急
保聚而恃以無恐者也及今雉堞欲完以
固湯池欲濬以深平居民樂安堵一旦事
出倉卒而吾備已先從容應之矣此設險
守國之道也二曰繕甲兵夫甲兵之繕非
徒厲戈鍛矛貯諸府庫已也據保甲之法
民自爲衛家自爲兵此不可以施訓練乎
顧有司不視爲故事則用以擾民亡益也
===
所貴乎賢守令者除尺籍丁壯外簡城夫
驍勇聯以什伍統以領率授以長短之兵
旬月比試而軒輊之初賞其儁久益賞罰
行焉如是而民不閑於武略者否也此所
謂除戎器而戒不虞也且鄒魯家譚政事
首務足食春秋書城築不時重用民力貴
拊循也故爲守令者守羔羊之節敦素絲
之儉課來牟之勤挽蟋蟀之風以阜民財
而民可富矣勿勞以營建勿役以三時勿
punctuated: 邊爲險；論三晉之形勝，則三關爲險；論郡縣之形勝，則城堡爲險。城堡者，民之緩急保聚而恃以無恐者也。及今雉堞欲完以固，湯池欲濬以深。平居民樂安堵，一旦事出倉卒，而吾備已先，從容應之矣。此設險守國之道也。二曰繕甲兵。夫甲兵之繕，非徒厲戈鍛矛、貯諸府庫已也。據保甲之法，民自爲衛，家自爲兵，此不可以施訓練乎？顧有司不視爲故事，則用以擾民，亡益也。所貴乎賢守令者，除尺籍丁壯外，簡城夫驍勇，聯以什伍，統以領率，授以長短之兵，旬月比試而軒輊之，初賞其儁，久益賞罰行焉。如是，而民不閑於武略者，否也。此所謂「除戎器而戒不虞」也。且鄒魯家譚政事，首務足食；《春秋》書城築不時，重用民力，貴拊循也。故爲守令者，守《羔羊》之節，敦《素絲》之儉，課來牟之勤，挽《蟋蟀》之風，以阜民財，而民可富矣；勿勞以營建，勿役以三時，勿…
translation_en:
…Frontiers serve as the strategic barriers; if we speak of the strategic topography of the Three Jin [Shanxi], the Three Passes serve as the strategic barriers; if we speak of the strategic topography of the prefectures and counties, the walled towns and forts serve as the strategic barriers. Walled towns and forts are where the people gather for protection in emergencies and what they rely upon to be free from fear. Right now, the parapets should be repaired to make them solid, and the moats should be dredged to make them deep. In times of peace, the people rejoice in living undisturbed; should an emergency suddenly arise one day, our preparations will already be in place, and we can respond to it with composure. This is the way to establish strategic barriers to defend the state.

The second is to repair armor and weapons. Now, the repairing of armor and weapons does not merely consist of sharpening halberds and forging spears to store them away in armories. According to the mutual-security (baojia) system, the people act as their own guards and each household acts as its own soldiers—can this not be used to conduct training? Yet local officials either treat it as a mere formality or use it to harass the people, which is of no benefit. What is valued in worthy Prefects and Magistrates is that, in addition to the able-bodied men on the military registers, they select the brave and strong among the town laborers, organize them into squads of five and ten, place them under leaders, equip them with long and short weapons, and test and rank them every ten days or every month—at first rewarding the outstanding, and over time implementing both rewards and punishments. If this is done, could it be that the people would not become versed in military skills? Not so. This is what is meant by "repairing military equipment to guard against the unexpected."

Furthermore, when the masters of Zou and Lu [Mencius and Confucius] discussed governance, they made sufficient food the primary task; when the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) recorded unseasonable wall-building, it attached great weight to the use of the people's labor, valuing their comforting and nurturing. Therefore, those who serve as Prefects and Magistrates should uphold the integrity of "Lambskin" (Gaoyang), foster the frugality of "White Silk" (Susi), encourage diligence in cultivating wheat and barley, and restore the customs of "The Cricket" (Xishuai) in order to increase the people's wealth—and thus the people can be made prosperous. They should not weary them with construction projects, nor conscript them during the three farming seasons, nor…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
疲以奔命勿擾以追呼以養民力而民可
安矣生之而不傷厚之而不困事至而爲
之備患生而爲之防以結民心而民樂於
用命矣脩此三者而守之以誠居之以寛
持之以健守之以恒兼之以城堡之固甲
兵之厲而內治脩矣彼三關而外簡壯猷
之方叔寄萬里之長城方其無事則選將
帥清行伍訓士卒練士兵開屯田復鹽課
實邊儲拳曩時所稱媮惰因循之弊一切
刷去將使五內四支脊就奠安順治威嚴
===
一統鞏固而爲
國家樹億萬載不拔之基者端在兹矣又奚
必調才望有司於附塞而後爲勝筭哉雖
然猶有可慮者大同爲三晉藩籬
京師肩背樹藩未固室家靡寧覆背未豐寒
且及體是又何可忽也今大同之民疲矣
寡閭閻桑梓之樂抱門庭枹鼓之憂加以
軍屯之擾供應之煩地半荒隙而租稅之
punctuated: 疲以奔命，勿擾以追呼，以養民力，而民可安矣。生之而不傷，厚之而不困，事至而爲之備，患生而爲之防，以結民心，而民樂於用命矣。脩此三者，而守之以誠，居之以寛，持之以健，守之以恒，兼之以城堡之固、甲兵之厲，而內治脩矣。彼三關而外，簡壯猷之方叔，寄萬里之長城。方其無事，則選將帥，清行伍，訓士卒，練士兵，開屯田，復鹽課，實邊儲，拳曩時所稱媮惰因循之弊一切刷去，將使五內四支脊就奠安，順治威嚴，一統鞏固，而爲國家樹億萬載不拔之基者，端在兹矣。又奚必調才望有司於附塞，而後爲勝筭哉？雖然，猶有可慮者。大同爲三晉藩籬，京師肩背。樹藩未固，室家靡寧；覆背未豐，寒且及體，是又何可忽也！今大同之民疲矣，寡閭閻桑梓之樂，抱門庭枹鼓之憂，加以軍屯之擾，供應之煩，地半荒隙，而租稅之
translation_en:
… exhaust them with constant rushing about on orders, and do not harass them with the shouting of tax collectors—thereby nurturing the people's strength, and the people can be at peace. Give them life without harming them, enrich them without distressing them, make preparations when affairs arise, and set up defenses when calamities emerge—thereby binding the hearts of the people, and the people will gladly obey orders. Cultivate these three things, and guard them with sincerity, dwell in them with宽容 (magnanimity), uphold them with vigor, and maintain them with constancy; combine this with the solidity of walled forts and the sharpness of armor and weapons, and internal governance will be well ordered.

Beyond those Three Passes (Sanguan), select a Fang Shu of grand strategy and entrust him with the Great Wall of ten thousand li. While things are peaceful, select commanders, clear out the ranks, train the soldiers, drill the local militia, open up military agricultural colonies (tuntian), restore the salt tax quotas, fill the frontier granaries, and completely sweep away [reading 舉 for 拳?] all the abuses of laxity, indolence, and routinism spoken of in former times. This will bring the five viscera and four limbs all [reading 皆 for 脊?] into settled peace; with internal order and external awe, the unified realm will be consolidated, and the establishment of an unshakable foundation for the State for ahundred million myriad years truly lies right here. Why then would it be necessary to transfer local officials of talent and reputation to the frontier-adjacent counties before considering it a winning strategy?

Even so, there is still something to be concerned about. Datong serves as the protective hedge of the Three Jin (Shanxi) and the shoulders and back of the Capital. If the hedge is not planted firmly, the household knows no peace; if the covering on the back is not thick, the cold will reach the body—how can this be neglected? Today the people of Datong are exhausted! They have little joy in their home villages and native communities, and harbor anxiety over war drums at their very gates and courtyards. Added to this are the disturbances of military colonies and the burdens of provisioning; half the land lies barren and uncultivated, yet the tax…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
徵求如故民喁喁然日望
蠲租之令未下也於是乎牽育之念微而樂
土之思作矣及今不存恤而招徠之杈廾
之亭不可爲炯鑒乎於乎此利害安危之
機非守令將帥所能及也免曠土之租罷
不急之役以豐肩背而固藩籬是在
廟堂之上加之意耳
punctuated: 徵求如故。民喁喁然日望蠲租之令，未下也。於是乎牽育之念微，而樂土之思作矣。及今不存恤而招徠之，杈廾之亭，不可爲炯鑒乎？於乎！此利害安危之機，非守令、將帥所能及也。免曠土之租，罷不急之役，以豐肩背而固藩籬，是在廟堂之上加之意耳。
translation_en: …exactions continue as before. The people look up expectantly every day, hoping for a decree remitting taxes, which has not yet been issued. Consequently, their attachment to home and family grows faint, while thoughts of seeking a happier land elsewhere arise. If we do not comfort, relieve, and draw them back now, will not the rebellion at Chagongting [? 杈廾之亭, i.e., Wuqiaoling 烏鞘嶺 / Fort Chagong] serve as a stark warning? Alas! This is a pivot of benefit or harm, safety or peril, which lies beyond the reach of local magistrates, prefects, and military commanders. Remitting the taxes on abandoned lands and halting non-urgent labor services so as to strengthen the shoulders and back [of the capital] and secure the defensive screen [of the province]—this simply rests with the court above paying greater heed to it.

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
萬曆己卯山西鄉試錄成本
原晉事述唐虞夏后氏以來
名世之倫用廣厲多士敎諭
日新論說具矣銳復何言銳
竊惟恒山大河之間雖古帝
王所更都乃其四封左擁燕
薊右接秦關前引楚疆後控
===
胡虜不無事矣在唐虞時壺
口龍門則禹功所自始益焚
稷播契乃振德以至編戶可
旌臯陶猶勤猾夏之憂惟是
五官炳烺千古與山川不朽
下逮五伯七雄之際三晉之
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

萬曆己卯《山西鄉試錄》成，本原晉事，述唐、虞、夏后氏以來名世之倫，用廣厲多士，敎諭日新論說具矣，銳復何言？銳竊惟恒山、大河之間，雖古帝王所更都，乃其四封，左擁燕薊，右接秦關，前引楚疆，後控胡虜，不無事矣。在唐、虞時，壺口、龍門則禹功所自始，益焚、稷播，契乃振德，以至編戶可旌，臯陶猶勤猾夏之憂，惟是五官炳烺千古，與山川不朽。下逮五伯、七雄之際，三晉之
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

Now that the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination of the jimao year of the Wanli era [1579] has been completed, Instructor Ri Xin 日新 has already set forth a full exposition, tracing the origins of the affairs of Jin and recounting the renowned worthies since the eras of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Lord of Xia in order to broadly encourage the many scholars. What more need I, Rui 銳, say? Yet I humbly reflect that although the region between Mount Heng and the Yellow River was where the ancient sovereigns successively established their capitals, as for its four borders—embracing Yan and Ji on the left, connecting with the passes of Qin on the right, drawing toward the frontiers of Chu in front, and holding back the northern barbarians behind—it has never been free of troubles. In the time of Tang and Yu, Hukou and Longmen were where the meritorious labors of Yu began; Yi burned [the marshes], Ji sowed [the grain], and Xie roused virtue among the people, until even the registered households could be honored for their conduct, while Gao Yao still diligently attended to the worry of barbarians disturbing the Xia. Only through this have the five officials shone brilliantly through a thousand ages, as imperishable as the mountains and rivers. Coming down to the era of the Five Hegemons and the Seven Warring States, the [land] of the Three Jin…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
地介乎秦楚爲天下樞日尋
於干戈諸侯蠶食六卿瓜分
征繕無寧日秦漢一統方內
無事而匈奴爲患時入蹂躪
建元元朔之間漢數遣將出
雲中出代出鴈門出定襄屯
向注生蜚狐征繕無寧歲唐阻
===
澤潞宋淪金元當是時帝王
之氣銷鑠且盡士方倚烽荷
戈何暇論俎豆之業乎
國家都燕則晉爲右輔
皇風洽餘二百年以至嘉靖之
季虜患不減漢時西河河東
流血暴骨而士不廢業登儁
punctuated: 地介乎秦、楚，爲天下樞，日尋於干戈，諸侯蠶食，六卿瓜分，征繕無寧日。秦、漢一統，方內無事，而匈奴爲患，時入蹂躪。建元、元朔之間，漢數遣將出雲中，出代，出鴈門，出定襄，屯向注生蜚狐，征繕無寧歲。唐阻澤、潞，宋淪金、元。當是時，帝王之氣銷鑠且盡，士方倚烽荷戈，何暇論俎豆之業乎！國家都燕，則晉爲右輔，皇風洽餘二百年。以至嘉靖之季，虜患不減漢時，西河、河東流血暴骨，而士不廢業，登儁
translation_en:
… territory lay between Qin 秦 and Chu 楚, serving as the pivot of the realm. Daily engaged in warfare, it was nibbled away by the feudal lords and carved up by the Six Ministers, with no peaceful day free from military levies and repairs of armor. When Qin and Han 漢 unified the empire, there was peace within the realm, yet the Xiongnu 匈奴 posed a threat, periodically invading and trampling the land. During the Jianyuan 建元 (140–135 BCE) and Yuanshuo 元朔 (128–123 BCE) eras, the Han repeatedly dispatched generals to march out from Yunzhong 雲中, from Dai 代, from Yanmen 鴈門, and from Dingxiang 定襄, and to garrison Juzhu [?] and Feihu 蜚狐, with no peaceful year free from military levies and repairs of armor. Under the Tang 唐, it was obstructed by rebellion in Ze 澤 and Lu 潞; under the Song 宋, it fell to the Jin 金 and Yuan 元. At those times, the aura of the sage-emperors and kings was worn away almost to nothing; scholars were just then leaning beside beacon towers and shouldering halberds—what leisure did they have to discuss the pursuits of ritual vessels?

Our dynasty established its capital at Yan 燕, making Jin 晉 (Shanxi) its right-hand bulwark, and the imperial influence has suffused the land for over two hundred years. Down to the end of the Jiajing 嘉靖 era (1522–1566), the menace of the northern caitiffs was no less than in Han times; in Xihe 西河 and Hedong 河東 blood flowed and bones lay exposed, yet scholars did not abandon their studies, and the elevation of talented men …

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
如昔
天子神聖垂意問學興建太平虜
嚮風慕義願受約束世世保
塞爲外藩坐息邊烽使全晉
之士咽餔綏帶朝禮樂而夕
詩書庸詎非千載一時盛際
邪〔銳〕嘗尚論典謨慨然遐想
===
唐虞夏后氏之風雖不及身
親見之夫平陽蒲阪安邑今
猶古也顧安得西游其地而
問俗焉乃今幸以聘至且得
縱觀多士之文諸所論著雄
渾博大稱其土風譔學則精
一執中闡德則欽明濬哲擬
punctuated: 如昔。天子神聖，垂意問學，興建太平。虜嚮風慕義，願受約束，世世保塞爲外藩，坐息邊烽，使全晉之士咽餔綏帶，朝禮樂而夕詩書，庸詎非千載一時盛際邪？〔銳〕嘗尚論典謨，慨然遐想唐、虞、夏后氏之風。雖不及身親見之，夫平陽、蒲阪、安邑，今猶古也，顧安得西游其地而問俗焉？乃今幸以聘至，且得縱觀多士之文。諸所論著，雄渾博大，稱其土風：譔學則精一執中，闡德則欽明濬哲，擬
translation_en:
… as of old. Now the Son of Heaven is divinely sage, turning his mind to learning and inquiry and establishing an era of Great Peace. The northern caitiffs, drawn to our moral influence and admiring our righteousness, have willingly submitted to our agreements, pledging generation after generation to guard the frontier passes as an outer screen. Thus the border beacon fires have been extinguished without a fight, allowing the scholars of all Jin to eat their fill and wear loosely tied sashes, devoting their mornings to rites and music and their evenings to the Odes and Documents—how could this be anything less than the flourishing opportunity of a thousand years?

I, Rui, have in the past evaluated the past through the canons and counsels of antiquity, sighing with distant longing for the ethos of Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the House of Xia. Even though I could not witness those ages in person, Pingyang, Puban, and Anyi are today as they were in antiquity—yet how could I ever manage to travel west to those lands and inquire into their customs? Now, happily, I have come here by invitation to serve as examiner, and have moreover been able to read at length the essays of the many scholars. All that they argue and compose is vigorous, profound, and expansive, well matching the character of their native land: when discoursing on learning, they speak of "subtlety and unity, holding fast the mean"; when elucidating virtue, they speak of being "reverent and明 [illustrious], profound and wise"; when modeling…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
治則時雍從欲敘功則平成
永賴陳議則知人安民非堯
舜不譚非禹皐不列濟濟乎
斌斌乎盛矣雖然秉不必屈
惟其才良也鼎不必汾惟其
器眞也多士晉產出爲國琛
寧啻屈之乘汾之鼎乎哉乃
===
今固服輿納廟之時良驁眞
贗於是焉在則多士何居末
世夸士言高於青天行入於
汙瀆許身欲置五臣之中所
就業尚出春秋列國諸子之
下蓋堯舜御世野無遺賢極
其選也僅僅二十有二人而
punctuated: 治則時雍從欲，敘功則平成永賴，陳議則知人安民。非堯、舜不譚，非禹、皐不列，濟濟乎、斌斌乎，盛矣！雖然，秉不必屈，惟其才良也；鼎不必汾，惟其器眞也。多士晉產，出爲國琛，寧啻屈之乘、汾之鼎乎哉？乃今固服輿納廟之時，良驁、眞贗於是焉在，則多士何居？末世夸士，言高於青天，行入於汙瀆；許身欲置五臣之中，所就業尚出春秋列國諸子之下。蓋堯、舜御世，野無遺賢，極其選也，僅僅二十有二人；而
translation_en: … governance, they write of universal harmony and the people following the ruler's desires; when recounting achievements, they write of regulation and completion to be relied upon forever; when presenting counsels, they write of knowing men and bringing peace to the people. They do not speak unless it is of Yao and Shun; they do not cite examples unless they are of Yu and Gao Yao. How numerous and dignified, how refined and balanced—flourishing indeed! Even so, a team of horses need not come from Qu [Note: 秉 is a graphic error for 乘], so long as their mettle is fine; a ritual tripod need not come from the Fen River, so long as the vessel is genuine. The many scholars born in Jin who go forth to become treasures of the state—how could they be merely the horse-teams of Qu or the tripods of the Fen! Yet now is truly the time when they are harnessed to the carriage and placed in the ancestral temple; whether they are fine steeds or nags, genuine vessels or counterfeits, will be determined right here. Where, then, will the many scholars stand? Boastful scholars of a decadent age speak words higher than the blue heavens while their conduct sinks into filthy ditches. In their self-estimation they wish to place themselves among the Five Ministers [of Shun], yet what they accomplish in their careers still falls below the various nobles of the feudal states of the Spring and Autumn period. For when Yao and Shun ruled the world and no worthy was left neglected in the wilderness, at the very height of their selection there were merely twenty-two men; whereas…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
天府者一何纍纍也〔銳〕竊私計所
籍六十五人者夫有一二廡
幾五臣者乎微獨五臣夫夫
晉產也請以晉論令多士爲
政有趙衰趙盾士會士匄趙
孟韓起魏舒無有乎謀國有
===
狐偃先軫魏絳李克無有乎
師保有荀息羊舌肸牛畜荀
欣徐越無有乎沓慶有師服
史趙師曠蔡墨無有乎進賢
有祁奚曰季魏成無有乎能
言有周舍左師觸龍無有乎
爲邑有尹鐸西門豹無有乎
punctuated: 天府者，一何纍纍也！〔銳〕竊私計所籍六十五人者，夫有一二廡幾五臣者乎？微獨五臣，夫夫晉產也，請以晉論。令多士爲政，有趙衰、趙盾、士會、士匄、趙孟、韓起、魏舒無有乎？謀國有狐偃、先軫、魏絳、李克無有乎？師保有荀息、羊舌肸、牛畜、荀欣、徐越無有乎？沓慶有師服、史趙、師曠、蔡墨無有乎？進賢有祁奚、曰季、魏成無有乎？能言有周舍、左師觸龍無有乎？爲邑有尹鐸、西門豹無有乎？
translation_en: …the Imperial Archives, how numerous they are! I, [Rui], privately reckon regarding the sixty-five men whom we have registered: are there one or two among them who come close [廡, for 庶?] to the Five Ministers [of Shun]? Not to speak only of the Five Ministers—these gentlemen are natives of Jin, so let me discuss the matter in terms of Jin. Suppose you many gentlemen take up governance: will there or will there not be a Zhao Cui 趙衰, a Zhao Dun 趙盾, a Shi Hui 士會, a Shi Gai 士匄, a Zhao Meng 趙孟 [Zhao Wu 趙武], a Han Qi 韓起, or a Wei Shu 魏舒? In planning for the state, will there or will there not be a Hu Yan 狐偃, a Xian Zhen 先軫, a Wei Jiang 魏絳, or a Li Ke 李克? As tutors and protectors, will there or will there not be a Xun Xi 荀息, a Yangshe Xi 羊舌肸 [Shuxiang 叔向], a Niu Xu 牛畜, a Xun Xin 荀欣, or a Xu Yue 徐越? In consulting on auspicious and inauspicious signs [沓慶, for 占慶/災祥?], will there or will there not be a Music Master Fu (Shi Fu 師服), a Scribe Zhao (Shi Zhao 史趙), a Music Master Kuang (Shi Kuang 師曠), or a Cai Mo 蔡墨? In recommending the worthy, will there or will there not be a Qi Xi 祁奚, a Jiu Ji 臼季 [transcribed 曰季], or a Wei Cheng 魏成? Inoffering candid counsel, will there or will there not be a Zhou She 周舍 or a Left Mentor Chu Long (Zuoshi Chulong 左師觸龍)? In governing cities, will there or will there not be a Yin Duo 尹鐸 or a Ximen Bao 西門豹?…

title: 萬曆七年山西鄉試錄
text:
載在晉志惟多士所擇之此
而無有何論五臣蓋鄒魯家
言行勉不足言愼有餘今也
不揆事實而槩言唐虞夏后
氏精一干戈論雖篤猶色莊
耳譬之圖繪非不爛然乃不
可以適用以觀晉之風有
===
二蓋天下莫先焉詩列唐魏
二國好樂無荒儉也宛然左
辟讓也非晉風邪粤在古昔
不翦不椽而卑且菲焉不矜
不伐而能且功焉斯亦唐虞
夏后氏之遺也夫士有侈心
則宫壘而寵賂章士有競心
punctuated: 載在晉志，惟多士所擇之。此而無有，何論五臣？蓋鄒、魯家言行勉不足、言愼有餘，今也不揆事實，而槩言唐、虞、夏后氏，精一干戈，論雖篤，猶色莊耳。譬之圖繪，非不爛然，乃不可以適用。以觀晉之風，有二，蓋天下莫先焉。《詩》列《唐》、《魏》二國，「好樂無荒」，儉也；「宛然左辟」，讓也。非晉風邪？粤在古昔，不翦不椽，而卑且菲焉；不矜不伐，而能且功焉，斯亦唐、虞、夏后氏之遺也。夫士有侈心，則宫壘而寵賂章；士有競心，
translation_en: They are recorded in the annals of Jin, awaiting only the choice of our many scholars. If even these are lacking, what need is there to speak of the Five Ministers [of Shun]? Indeed, the Confucian traditions of Zou and Lu teach striving where one's actions fall short and exercising caution where one's words are in excess. Nowadays, however, people do not weigh actual facts, but make sweeping pronouncements about Tang [Yao], Yu [Shun], and the Lord of Xia, discoursing on "refinement and singleness of mind" or on "shields and halberds." Though their arguments may sound earnest, they are merely putting on a solemn countenance. It is like a painting: it is not without brilliant colors, yet it cannot be put to practical use. When we observe the customs of Jin, there are two in which none in the realm can surpass it. The Book of Odes (Shi) includes the airs of the two states of Tang and Wei: "loving pleasure without running to excess" is frugality; "courteously stepping aside to the left" is yielding. Are these not the customs of Jin? Looking back to antiquity, thatched roofs were left untrimmed and rafters unhewn, while palaces were kept low and offerings sparse; men neither boasted nor bragged, yet they possessed both ability and achievement. This, too, is the legacy of Tang, Yu, and the Lord of Xia. Now, when scholars harbor extravagant desires, palaces and pleasure-towers rise and favoritism and bribery become rampant; when scholars harbor contentious desires, …
